The Department of Physics at Umeå University (https://www.umu.se/en/department-of-physics/) conducts strong research in condensed matter physics, nanotechnology, photonics, ultrafast spectroscopy, and theoretical and computational physics. We announce a PhD position within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network SPARK for the doctoral project ‘Spatiotemporal Information Processing’. 

Last day to apply is November 30, 2026.
The earliest starting date is February 2027, or by agreement.

Project description 

The project will develop ultrafast optical logic and memory concepts using spatiotemporal metamaterials. The doctoral candidate will design metamaterial structures coupled to quantum emitters for ultrafast information processing and investigate how structured ultrashort light pulses can control optical and magnetic properties on femtosecond timescales.

The research will focus on developing sub-10 fs protocols for all-optical logic operations, data processing, and spatiotemporal magnetic memories. The work combines nanophotonics, metamaterials, quantum emitters, ultrafast optics, and light–matter interaction, with the aim of creating new routes for information processing beyond conventional electronic approaches.

The doctoral candidate position is funded by the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network SPARK. The network offers a structured international training environment with research-specific and transferable-skills courses, workshops, conferences, and network-wide events. The project includes a 3-month industrial secondment at NKT Photonics in Denmark, focusing on vectorial ultrashort pulses, and a 6-month research secondment at Imperial College London in the United Kingdom, focusing on nanofabrication and characterization.

The doctoral project will be carried out at Umeå University under the supervision of Associate Professor Nicolò Maccaferri. The candidate will also benefit from co-supervision and mentoring by Professor Riccardo Sapienza at Imperial College London and from an industrial mentor at NKT Photonics. The position provides the opportunity to work in a stimulating, multidisciplinary, and international research environment within a prestigious European training network.

Competence requirements

To be admitted for studies at third-cycle level, applicants are required to have completed a second-cycle level degree or completed course requirements of at least 240 ECTS credits. The recruitment procedure will follow the Higher Education Ordinance (Högskoleförordningen). Applicants should have a Master’s degree, or equivalent, in physics, applied physics, optics/photonics, nanoscience, materials science, electrical engineering, or a closely related field. Fluency in English is mandatory. A documented background in photonics, nanophotonics, ultrafast optics, condensed matter physics, quantum optics, metamaterials, magnetism, or related experimental or theoretical methods is meritorious.

Willingness to work in an inter-cultural, international, and diverse group, and the ability to work independently or as part of a team, are fundamental.

The applicant must meet the MSCA eligibility and mobility requirements: the candidate must not hold a doctoral degree at the time of recruitment and must not have resided or carried out their main activity, such as work or studies, in Sweden for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before recruitment.

Terms of employment

The employment is expected to result in a doctoral degree, and the main assignment for the doctoral student is to take part in research education, including participation in the described research project and relevant courses. Teaching and other departmental work, up to a maximum of 20%, may be included. 

The salary follows the established salary level for doctoral students at Umeå University. The position is funded for 36 months through the MSCA Doctoral Network SPARK, with a salary corresponding to at least the MSCA level (approximately 33 100 SEK gross per month), with the possibility of additional MSCA allowances for mobility and accompanying family members. Funding for the remainder of the employment period is provided from other sources. Employment conditions and additional benefits for employees according to applicable regulations.

The employment is limited to four years at full-time or up to five years if teaching and other departmental work is performed. The employment starts in February 2027 or according to agreement.

The application 

The application should contain:

  1. A cover letter with summary of research interests and motivation (max. 1 page)
  2. Curriculum Vitae.
  3. Certified copies of relevant degree certificate(s) translated to English or Swedish.
  4. Transcripts with grades, with English or Swedish translation. Note that for international applicants the grading system should be explained in brief.
  5. Copies of student theses and publications (if any).
  6. Names and contact information of at least one reference person.

You apply via our e-recruitment system Varbi. The deadline for applications is November 30, 2026. Log in and submit your application via the button at the bottom of the page. All application documents must be uploaded in PDF format and should be written in English (preferred) or Swedish.

More information

For further information, contact the Principal Investigator of the project, Associate Professor Nicolò Maccaferri, nicolo.maccaferri@umu.se.

We look forward to receiving your application!

Umeå University is offering a PhD position in Computing Science with a focus on machine learning for graph transformations. The project investigates a hybrid approach that combines deep learning with grammatical inference to develop models that are interpretable, efficient, and mathematically verifiable while leveraging the flexibility of neural methods. If successful, the work has the potential to advance applications such as automated theorem proving, knowledge-graph inference, and causal analysis.

The Department of Computing Science has experienced rapid growth in recent years, with a strong emphasis on fostering an inclusive, collaborative, and bottom-up-driven research environment. Our workplace brings together a diverse community of individuals from a wide range of nationalities.

As a PhD student with us, you benefit from comprehensive career development support, opportunities for networking, and access to robust administrative and technical services—all within a setting that offers attractive employment conditions.

To learn more about the department, please visit: https://www.umu.se/en/department-of-computing-science/

Project description

Graphs are a fundamental way of representing structured information from sentences and computer programs to social networks and they are becoming increasingly important as generative AI systems move beyond text. To keep such systems safe and reliable, we need mechanisms that can ensure their outputs follow the right rules, much like guardrails that prevent language models from producing harmful content or incorrect code. This project introduces a new idea: instead of relying on opaque, heavy machine-learning models, it learns transparent, rule-based rewriting systems that can transform graphs, check the correctness of AI-generated structures, and even guide neural networks during inference. By combining techniques from grammatical inference, reinforcement learning, and efficient search algorithms, the method can automatically discover both the rules and probabilities needed to model complex graph behaviors, offering a more interpretable and verifiable alternative for future AI systems.

The student will collaborate closely with the PI and her research group at Umeå University to investigate the proposed learning approach. The PhD student is expected to produce research outputs relevant to the fields of theoretical computer science and symbolic machine learning.

Admission requirements

The general admission requirements for doctoral studies are a second- cycle level degree, or completed course requirements of at least 240 ECTS credits, of which at least 60 ECTS credits are at second-cycle level, or have an equivalent education from abroad, or equivalent qualifications.

To be admitted to doctoral studies in the field of computer science, the applicant must have completed courses totaling at least 90 higher education credits in computer science or in subjects directly relevant to the specific specialization.

Requirements

We are looking for candidates who have:

Solid analytical and mathematical abilities Experience with machine learning Experience with formal language theory or automata theory Strong communication skills and proficiency in English The ability to work independently as well as collaboratively

Meritorious Qualifications

It is considered an advantage if you have:

Experience with academic writing Strong programming skills, particularly in Python Familiarity with knowledge graphs Experience with graph neural network

Personal Qualities

We value candidates who are:

Intellectually curious Self-motivated and well-organized Eager to engage with the scientific community

About the position

The position provides you with the opportunity to pursue PhD studies in Computing Science for four years, with the goal of achieving the degree of Doctor in Computing Science. While the position is mainly devoted to PhD studies (at least 80% of the time), it may include up to 20% department service (usually teaching). If so, the total time for the position is extended accordingly, resulting in a maximum of five years.

The procedure for recruitment for the position is in accordance with the Higher Education Ordinance (chapter 12, 2§) and the decision regarding the position cannot be appealed.

The expected starting date is January 12, 2027 or as otherwise agreed.

Application

A complete application should contain the following documents:

A cover letter including a description of your research interests, your reasons to apply for the position, and your contact information A curriculum vitae Reprints / copies of completed BSc and/or MSc theses and other relevant publications, if any Copies of degree certificates, including documentation of completed academic courses and obtained grades Documentation and description of other relevant experiences or competences.

The application must be written in English or Swedish. Attached documents must be in pdf format. Applications must be submitted electronically using the e-recruitment system of Umeå University, and be received no later than November 30, 2026.

The Department of Computing Science values gender diversity, and therefore particularly encourages women and those outside the gender binary to apply for the position.

For additional information, please contact Professor Johanna Björklund (email: johanna@cs.umu.se).

The Department of Physics at Umeå University (https://www.umu.se/en/department-of-physics/) conducts strong research in condensed matter physics, nanotechnology, photonics, ultrafast spectroscopy, and theoretical and computational physics. We announce a PhD position within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network SPARK for the doctoral project ‘Spatiotemporal Hybrid Light–Matter States’. 

Last day to apply is November 30, 2026. 
The earliest starting date is February 2027, or by agreement.

Project description

The project will create spatiotemporal polaritons through ultrafast light–matter interactions in engineered metamaterial systems. The doctoral candidate will explore wide-bandgap semiconductors and high-quality excitonic or molecular emitters coupled to time-modulated gratings, with the goal of realizing hybrid light–matter states whose properties can be controlled on femtosecond timescales.

The research will combine ultrafast pump–push–probe experiments with sub-10 fs resolution, finite-element simulations, and quantum models extending the Tavis–Cummings Hamiltonian. The aim is to demonstrate coherent control of spatiotemporal polaritons and to design spatiotemporal metamaterial platforms supporting new forms of hybrid light–matter dynamics. The work combines nanophotonics, metamaterials, ultrafast optics, condensed matter physics, and quantum optics.

The doctoral candidate position is funded by the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network SPARK. The network offers a structured international training environment with research-specific and transferable-skills courses, workshops, conferences, and network-wide events. The project includes a 6-month research secondment at Universidad Autónoma de Madrid in Spain, where theoretical skills will be developed, and a 3-month industrial secondment at Ultrafast Innovations GmbH in Germany.

The doctoral project will be carried out at Umeå University under the supervision of Associate Professor Nicolò Maccaferri. The candidate will also benefit from co-supervision and mentoring by Associate Professor Paloma Arroyo Huidobro at Universidad Autónoma de Madrid and from an industrial mentor at Ultrafast Innovations GmbH. English fluency, both written and spoken, is mandatory. A documented background in photonics, nanophotonics, ultrafast optics, condensed matter physics, quantum optics, exciton–polaritons, light–matter interaction, numerical simulations, or quantum modelling is meritorious.

Willingness to work in an inter-cultural, international, and diverse group, and the ability to work independently or as part of a team, are fundamental.

jobs.title: Doctoral student in English Language and Linguistics
jobs.department: Lund University, Centre for Languages and Literature, HT
jobs.description_html:
About the subject

English Language and Linguistics is concerned with research on the English language and its many varieties, primarily with regard to semantics, syntax, text and discourse analysis, language policy, language acquisition, language teaching and testing methods. Some types of research are comparative and therefore involve other languages. 

About the education

Information about doctoral studies in English Language and Linguistics can be found at https://www.sol.lu.se/en/engelska/ interested-in-phd-studies/. Information about doctoral studies at the Joint Faculties of Humanities and Theology can be found at https://www.ht.lu.se/en/education/doctoral-studies/.

The education is carried out in Lund.

Work assignments

Doctoral studies. Departmental work, such as teaching and administrative tasks, can be assigned. The maximum amount of such work is 20 %.

Entry requirements

Eligibility for admission to doctoral studies in English Language and Linguistics is set out in the general syllabus for the subject, available at https://www.ht.lu.se/en/education/doctoral-studies/general-syllabi/. 

Assessment criteria

The selection process will primarily take into account the applicants’ ability to benefit from doctoral studies. This is assessed against the criteria quality, quantity, progression and relevance.

We welcome applications from candidates whose research interests align with the subject’s current areas of expertise (see https://www.sol.lu.se/en/engelska/research/) and who have the relevant theoretical and methodological background to undertake doctoral research in one or more of these fields. In the current round of applications, we particularly welcome candidates whose background and proposed doctoral project fall within one or more of the following areas and address questions relating to the English language:

Applied Linguistics: We welcome proposals on English as a foreign/second language, its acquisition and use; lexical processing and the multilingual mental lexicon; language testing and assessment, and the psychology of language learning and teaching. We also welcome research on language teacher education, as well as research on language planning and policy, English-medium instruction (EMI), and content and language integrated learning (CLIL). We encourage innovative projects that combine or draw on a range of methodological approaches, whether quantitative, qualitative, or mixed-methods.

Cognitive Linguistics and Multilingual Cognition, including research on language-cognition interactions in a variety of domains, including motion, time, aspect, gender, number, and colour, as well as research on conceptual transfer/restructuring, decision-making, and broader cognitive functions in multilingual individuals, societies, and real-life settings. Projects that engage in comparisons between speakers of English and other languages, different varieties of English, and multilingual settings where English is one of the languages spoken are welcome.

Corpus Linguistics, including corpus-based approaches to English language variation and use, for example in sociolinguistics, stance and evaluation, and discourse-pragmatic phenomena. We also welcome research on language in digital and social contexts, as well as studies integrating corpus data with experimental or other empirical methods. Projects with a comparative or cross-linguistic dimension, in which English constitutes a central component, are also of interest.

Neurolinguistics, particularly sentence processing from syntactic, semantic or pragmatic perspectives, using EEG.

Application

Instructions for applying for a doctoral position can be found here: https://www.ht.lu.se/en/education/doctoral-studies/become-a-doctoral-student-at-the-ht-faculties/application-and-admission/.

Information about accepted English language proficiency tests is available here: https://www.sol.lu.se/en/engelska/interested-in-phd-studies/.

Limit of tenure, four years according to 5 kap. 7 § HF.

jobs.department: Lund University, Department of Philosophy, HT
jobs.description_html:
About the subject

Cognitive Science is an interdisciplinary subject dealing with different aspects of cognition in biological and artificial systems. Among the phenomena studied are perception, memory, learning, language, thought and problem-solving. Central disciplines involved are psychology, neuroscience, linguistics, philosophy and computer science. 

About the education

The project Irony Re-examined in Interactive Settings (IRIS) seeks to bring about a paradigm shift in the experimental study of pragmatics by studying diﬀerences in comprehension between addressees and overhearers, focusing on irony as a test case. The main hypothesis of the project is that addressees and overhearers use diﬀerent comprehension strategies when understanding irony, with repercussions for irony processing, the development of irony comprehension, and how comprehenders hold ironic speakers accountable for the meanings that they convey. IRIS will develop a novel experimental paradigm that studies both addressees and overhearers, combining accuracy and rating-scales measures with recent technical advances in cognitive pupillometry.

Within the project, the doctoral student will write a dissertation on how differences in conversational roles (i.e., addressees and overhearers) impact how speakers are held accountable for the ironic and literal meanings that they communicate. The dissertation will be based on the results of experimental studies that the student will be expected to conduct.

IRIS is a project funded by an ERC starting grant awarded to Camilo Rodríguez Ronderos.

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Computer Science – human-centred monitoring of autonomous AI-enabled systems
jobs.department: Lund University, LTH, Department of Computer Science
jobs.description_html:
About the workplace

The position is placed in the Software Engineering (SE) division at the Department of Computer Science. The division conducts empirical research on how software-intensive systems are developed, verified and evolved in practice, in close collaboration with industry. The division has a long tradition of research on quality assurance, testing, requirements engineering and continuous software engineering.

As a doctoral student in the project, you will become part of an active doctoral environment where several ongoing thesis projects address related questions, including AI-driven DevOps, AI alignment through continuous operational testing, and software engineering for software-defined vehicles. The project is carried out in collaboration with Blekinge Institute of Technology (BTH) and with industrial partners.

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

As a doctoral student, you are trained in a scientific approach. In brief, this means that you practise thinking critically and analytically, solving problems independently using appropriate methods, and developing an awareness of research ethics. You will also have the opportunity to work on projects and to develop your leadership and teaching skills. Throughout your studies, you are guided by supervisors. The doctoral studies conclude with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at LTH at lth.se.

Subject and project description

The research subject is Computer Science. The position focuses on software engineering and is part of a research project funded within the strategic research environment ELLIIT and carried out by Lund University together with Blekinge Institute of Technology.

Modern autonomous and AI-enabled systems, such as driver-assistance systems in vehicles, industrial robots or AI agents in software services, are continuously updated through DevOps practices and feedback from use in the field. Each update may be correct and comply with requirements and standards, yet over time the system’s behaviour may gradually drift away from what users and other stakeholders intend and expect. This is called alignment drift. The project investigates how alignment drift can be characterised, how it can be detected through indicators in operational data (e.g. telemetry, test outcomes and customer feedback), and how humans can interpret and act on these signals within existing CI/CD workflows.

The project is empirical and design-oriented. It develops and evaluates support for how alignment drift can be characterised, detected and managed in industrial practice. You will work with retrospective case studies, analysis of data from issue trackers and logs, interviews and observations with engineers, and longitudinal action research in industry. The focus is on software engineering and on the interplay between people, processes and data – not on developing new machine-learning models or autonomous functions.

Work duties

Your main duty will be your doctoral studies, which include participation in research projects as well as doctoral courses, seminars and conferences.

You will drive the project’s research, from characterising alignment drift to evaluating new practices in industrial settings. The work is carried out in close collaboration with supervisors at Lund University and BTH and with industrial partners. The position involves some travel, e.g. to BTH in Karlskrona, industrial partners and conferences.

The duties include:

  • planning and conducting empirical studies, e.g. retrospective case studies, interview studies, and analysis of data from issue trackers, logs and test results
  • developing and evaluating support for how alignment drift can be characterised, detected and managed, in collaboration with engineers in industry
  • writing scientific papers and presenting results at international conferences and to industrial partners
  • participating in doctoral courses and seminars.
  • The duties may also include teaching and other departmental duties (no more than 20 % of working hours).

Qualifications

To be admitted and employed as a doctoral student, you need to meet the requirements below.

Admission requirements

You meet the general admission requirements for third-cycle studies if you have:

  • been awarded a second-cycle qualification or
  • satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits, of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way.

You meet the specific admission requirements for doctoral studies in Computer Science if you have:

  • at least 60 credits at second-cycle level relevant to the subject area, or
  • a Master of Science in Engineering in computer engineering, electrical engineering, information and communication technology, engineering physics, or engineering mathematics.

Finally, the student must be judged to have the ability required to complete the programme.

Additional requirements

To benefit from the doctoral programme in question, the following is also required:

  • in-depth knowledge of software engineering corresponding to at least 30 credits of courses in the field, e.g. requirements engineering, testing and verification, software processes, DevOps or software architecture
  • good knowledge of programming and data analysis, corresponding to the ability to analyse large amounts of data from software development and operation and to build simple prototypes
  • good ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle scientific problems
  • the ability to plan and drive the work forward on your own, across several parallel studies, and to adapt plans when conditions change, e.g. access to data and industrial cases
  • good written and oral communication skills, including with professionals outside academia
  • good collaboration skills
  • very good knowledge of English, spoken and written

Other qualifications

The following is considered meritorious for this doctoral programme:

  • knowledge in one or more of the following areas: continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD), DevOps or MLOps, requirements engineering and traceability, testing of AI-based systems, machine learning, and autonomous systems, e.g. in vehicles, robotics or AI agents
  • a second-cycle course in research methodology or empirical methods, e.g. case studies, interview studies, qualitative data analysis, surveys or mining software repositories
  • a degree project with an empirical focus, preferably in collaboration with industry, where the quality of the degree project is assessed based on the attached work
  • professional experience of software development, especially in environments with continuous integration and delivery
  • good academic results in courses in software engineering and computer science.

We offer

Lund University is a public authority, which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous pension scheme. You will work in a research environment with close industrial collaboration, with supervision from both Lund University and Blekinge Institute of Technology and the opportunity to build a network within ELLIIT.

Read more about working at Lund University at lu.se. 

Terms of employment

The employment is a fixed-term, full-time position, starting by agreement. Doctoral studies comprise four years of full-time study. If the position includes teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Regulations on employment as a doctoral student are found in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), Chapter 5, Sections 1–7.

Read more about employment conditions for doctoral students on Lund University’s staff pages. 

Other information

Selection takes place in several stages and includes interviews, a work sample and reference checks. Interviews are planned for December 2026 and January 2027.

How to apply

Applications must be written in English and must include:

  • CV (maximum two pages) starting with your education. State your degrees, relevant courses, the title of your degree project, any professional experience, and any publications and links to examples of your own code or reports.
  • Cover letter (maximum one page) structured under the following four headings:
    • Motivation: why you are applying for this particular position and how the project matches your interests.
    • Educational background: which courses and which degree project are most relevant to the project, and why.
    • Methodological experience: concrete examples of empirical studies or data analyses you have conducted and what your role was.
    • Reflection (maximum 150 words): How could one detect that a continuously updated software system is gradually starting to behave in ways that deviate from what its users and other stakeholders expect?
  • Transcript of records with a list of courses, and degree certificate or a statement of expected graduation. The transcript must show the grade for each course and the grading scale used. These must demonstrate that you meet the general and specific admission requirements and have the subject knowledge required for the doctoral project.
  • Degree project at second-cycle level (or equivalent independent work). If it is not yet completed, attach a summary and a description of its current status.
  • Anything else you wish to refer to, e.g. letters of recommendation or contact details of referees.

Please also answer the selection questions in the recruitment system. It is important that all documents are attached, as they form the basis for the assessment of eligibility and qualifications.

Welcome to apply!

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Physics with focus on attosecond Physics
jobs.description_html:
The research at the Division of Atomic Physics is centered on different applications of optics and lasers, including atomic and molecular physics with ultrashort light pulses, high-intensity laser-plasma physics, quantum information, and biophotonics. The Division operates the High-Power Laser Facility, including several advanced femtosecond laser systems and collaborate with several free electron laser facilities. It is a central part of a major interdisciplinary research environment within the Lund University, the Lund Laser Centre, LLC. The division is also heavily involved in undergraduate education, especially within the Photonics programme.

Work duties

At the division, research is performed on the generation and application of extremely short light pulses, in the attosecond and extreme ultraviolet range. The activities span from ultrafast laser technology and extreme nonlinear optics to studies of the electron dynamics in atoms and molecules as well as more complex systems using attosecond light pulses. The division of Atomic Physics is now looking for one PhD student for the project described below.

The project is funded through a Marie Sklodowska-Curie doctoral network:

Quantum information science and ultrafast nonlinear control at the attosecond timescale – QU-ATTO

This means that the positions come with some additional constraints and possibilities. The candidates recruited for these positions cannot have worked in Sweden for the last 5 years to be eligible. The positions come with a training network in Europe together with 15 PhD students in different countries.

The project focuses on using a technique for the tomographic reconstruction of entangled states in photoionization. The goal is to improve the technique that has been developed in Lund for the reconstruction of the density matrix of photoelectron originating from the absorption of ultrashort XUV pulses by atoms and molecules.

The main duties of doctoral students are to devote themselves to their research studies which includes participating in research projects and third cycle courses. The work duties can also include teaching and other departmental duties (no more than 20%).

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if he or she:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third-cycle studies in Physics if he or she has:

  • at least 30 second-cycle credits of relevance to the subject, of which at least 15 credits shall comprise a second-cycle degree project, or
  • an MSc in engineering physics or an associated field, or a Master’s degree in physics or an associated field.

 Equivalent knowledge acquired through corresponding programmes will be assessed individually. In order to enable interdisciplinary initiatives and important specialisations in certain areas, students with qualifications in subjects other than Physics may be considered for admission.

Finally, the student must be judged to have the potential to complete the programme.

Additional requirements:

  • Very good oral and written proficiency in English.
  • The student should have a background in optics/photonics and/or atomic physics/quantum mechanics.

Other assessment criteria

Experience in some of the following areas is a qualification for all the projects:

  • Femtosecond lasers and ultrafast optics
  • Quantum optics
  • High-order harmonic generation and attosecond physics
  • Photoelectron and photoion spectroscopy
  • Data analysis, vacuum technique, and mechanical design

Basis of assessment

Selection to postgraduate studies is based on the expected ability to perform well in the studies. The evaluation of the ability to perform well is based primarily on the results of studies at the basic and advanced levels, in particular:

  1. Knowledge and skills relevant to the thesis project and the subject of the study.
  2. An assessment of ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle research problems.
  3. Written and oral communication skills
  4. Other experience relevant to postgraduate studies, such as professional experience.

Consideration will also be given to good collaborative skills, drive and independence, and how the applicant, through his or her experience and skills, is deemed to have the abilities necessary for successfully completing the third cycle programme.

Terms of employment

Only those admitted to third cycle studies may be appointed to a doctoral studentship. Third cycle studies at LTH consist of full-time studies for 4 years. A doctoral studentship is a fixed-term employment of a maximum of 5 years (including 20% departmental duties). Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§.

Instructions on how to apply

Applications may be written in English or Swedish and include a cover letter stating the reasons why you are interested in the position and in what way the research project corresponds to your interests and educational background. The application must also contain a CV, degree certificate or equivalent, and other documents you wish to be considered (grade transcripts, contact information for your references, letters of recommendation, etc.).

jobs.title: Doctoral student in computer science with focus on program transformation
jobs.department: Lund University, LTH, Department of Computer Science
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

The position is within the Software Development and Environments division, part of the Department of Computer Science.  The division is exploring novel tools, languages, and methods for supporting software development, and conducts research in a variety of topics that include refactoring, program analysis, compiler construction, declarative specification languages, distributed development environments, and automatic program repair. Its research involves strong collaborations both locally within Lund University, internationally with other universities, and with industrial partners, such as ABB and Ericsson, including research driven by industrial PhD students. The division currently has twelve members, and regularly organises group activities to foster a positive working environment.

The division is actively developing the JastAdd metacompilation framework, which is the foundation for several compilers and software tools, including the division's ExtendJ extensible Java compiler and the static analysis tools IntraJ and MetaDL.

More about the Software Development and Environments group (sde.cs.lth.se/)
More about JastAdd (jastadd.cs.lth.se/web/)
More about ExtendJ (extendj.org)
More about MetaDL (github.com/lu-cs-sde/metadl)

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

As a doctoral student, you will learn to approach questions and challenges scientifically. In short, this means that you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at LTH on lth.se. 

Subject and project description

This research project aims to develop novel tools and techniques that enforce rigid guard-rails during software refactoring and other forms of software evolution. We assume an unreliable source of program transformations, such as a human developer or a large language model.  The guard-rail mechanism will then inspect, steer, and augment any sequence of program transformations to detect and recover from unintended behavioural change.
The position is funded by the Excellence Center at Linköping – Lund in Information Technology (ELLIIT), and it is a collaboration with the Natural Language Processing group at Linköping University, part of the division of Artificial Intelligence and Integrated Computer Systems.

More about ELLIIT (elliit.se)
More about the Division of Artificial Intelligence and Integrated Computer Systems at Linköping University (liu.se/en/organisation/liu/ida/aiics)

Work duties

You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral programme, which includes participation in research projects as well as third cycle courses, seminars and conferences.

The work duties include:

  • Research on automatic program analysis and program transformation applied to preventing unintended behavioural change during refactoring and similar program evolution tasks. You will work towards exploring approaches that can aid real-world software evolution, and examine qualitative aspects of these approaches.
  • Applying appropriate research methods: depending on the trajectory of this research, different and possibly novel methodologies may be required to provide robust answers to the underlying research questions. You will learn, apply, and possibly support the development of suitable methods.
  • Artefact-oriented activity: You will develop software tools, algorithms, and other software components. These should be evaluated in realistic scenarios and integrated with, as well as shared within, the project team.
  • Presentation and collaboration: You will present your research findings at the annual ELLIIT workshop in southern Sweden and discuss your work at meetings with academic project partners, including personal meetings with our collaboration partners in Linköping.
  • Interaction with the industry: You will have opportunities to discuss your work and collaborate with industrial researchers, especially in Lund.
  • The duties also include participation in teaching and other departmental work (limited to a maximum of 20% of working hours).

Qualifications

To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below.

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in computer science if the applicant has:

  • at least 60 second-cycle credits at an advanced level with relevance for the research topic, or
  • an MSc in Engineering in Computer Science and Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Information and Communication Technology, Engineering Physics or Engineering Mathematics.

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required:

  • Knowledge or experience in at least one of the following areas (demonstrated e.g. in the form of a university course, or through professional experiences or contributions to relevant open source projects):
    • o compiler construction, or
    • o the foundations of static program analysis.
  • good ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle research problems.
  • good written and oral communication skills.
  • good ability to cooperate.
  • very good knowledge of English, in speech and writing.
  • very good programming experience (demonstrated e.g. in the form of professional experiences, contributions to open source projects, or outstanding results in university courses).
  • persistence and the ability to plan and structure your own work
  • curiosity and willingness to learn and adopt new techniques, especially within the cross-disciplinary scope of the project

Other qualifications (advantages)

For the doctoral programme in question, it is advantageous if you can demonstrate experience or knowledge in one or more of the following subjects:

  • developing automatic program transformation tools, such as
    • o refactoring tools, or
    • o meta-programming tools.
  • software development in teams, especially in the context of:
    • o professional software engineering,
    • o open source projects, or
    • o legacy software engineering projects.
  • dynamic program analysis.
  • programming in Java.
  • functional or declarative programming (logic programming, reference attribute grammars etc.).
  • natural language processing, machine learning, and/or applying large language models, such as
    • o working with the underlying machine learning techniques, such as latent/embedding spaces, representation learning, or transformers,
    • o training or fine-tuning such models, or
    • o applying them to software development / software engineering tasks.
  • systematic evaluation of software systems and relevant statistical methods.
  • systems programming.
  • areas of discrete mathematics with relation to program analysis (lattice theory, type theory, Galois connections etc.).

We offer

Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme.  This project additionally offers collaboration opportunities with Linköping University via its joint supervision structure, and industrial outreach opportunities via ELLIIT, such as the annual ELLIIT workshop.

More about working at Lund University on lu.se. 

About the employment

The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, with intended start date in the spring of 2027 or according to agreement, but no later than 2027-12-31. Third cycle studies at LTH consist of full-time studies for 4 years. In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§.

More about terms of employment for doctoral students on Lund University’s Staffpages. 

How to apply

Applications shall be written in English and include:

  • CV and a cover letter stating the reasons why you are interested in the doctoral programme/employment and in what way the research project corresponds to your interests and educational background.
  • Copies of issued study certificates and/or awarded degree certificates. These must confirm that you meet the general and specific admission requirements for the doctoral programme and show that you have the subject knowledge required for the doctoral programme project.
  • Other documents you wish to be considered (grade transcripts, contact information for your references, letters of recommendation, etc.)

 

We welcome your application.

Description of the workplace

The position will be based in the Division of Mathematics at the Centre for Mathematical Sciences. The Centre for Mathematical Sciences is a joint department of the Faculty of Engineering (LTH) and the Faculty of Science (N) at Lund University, bringing together all mathematical sciences. The Division of Mathematics (N) unites leading experts in areas such as Algebra and Algebraic Topology, as well as Partial Differential Equations, Operator Theory and Complex Analysis, Harmonic Analysis and Applications, Inverse Problems and Differential Geometry. We attach great importance to a good, collegial working environment. The department is international with a relatively even gender distribution among employees.

Project description

The position is partly funded by the Swedish Research Council as part of the project “Local to global extensions of topological quantum field theories”. It is also possible to work on related topics including and not limited to stable homotopy theory, higher category theory, homological algebra and geometric topology.

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Biology (Invertebrate colour vision)
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

For your doctoral research, you will be a part of the Bok lab, which uses a wide range of techniques to study the evolution and ecology of vision in diverse invertebrates. Or lab is embedded within in the Lund Vision Group, a highly collaborative cluster of eight labs, internationally recognised as one of the leading centres in comparative visual science in the world. With 35-40 academics at all education and career stages, our vision research stretches across the entire animal kingdom, from jellyfishes, insects, and crustaceans, to squids and vertebrates. Our speciality is the design and evolution of eyes, how eyes are adapted to different lifestyles and habitats, and how vision is used for navigation and for controlling behaviour. Our techniques range from optics, electrophysiology and theoretical modelling, to microscopy, molecular biology and behavioural experiments. This thriving research environment offers broad support for doctoral education and research.

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.

More about being a doctoral student at the Faculty of Science at naturvetenskap.se Doctoral studies | Faculty of Science

Subject and project description

Aims: Colour vision has only to date been conclusively shown to exist in two of Earth’s approximately 32 animal phyla – vertebrates and arthropods. However, there are two additional known examples where colour vision may be possible – the firefly squid, a mollusc, and the alciopid worm, an annelid. Both are midwater marine species that are night active and live in deep water, yet they have astonishing retinal specializations that may contribute to colour vision. The aims of this PhD thesis will be to discover if these marine invertebrates have convergently evolved colour vision. Further, what behaviours are controlled by colour vision, and do they use the same visual processing circuits and principles to interpret colour information as we see in arthropods and vertebrates? This project will answer these questions using molecular, neurological, electrophysiological, and behavioural techniques in the field and lab.

Project background: This project grows naturally from ongoing research in the Bok Lab and contributes directly to our overall projects regarding the evolution of complex eyes and visual capabilities in crustaceans (water fleas and mantis shrimp) cephalopods (firefly squid), and polychaetes (alciopids and fan worms). The student will benefit from mentorship from the Bok lab's existing postdoctoral researchers who have completed preliminary work for this project. Further, the project synergises well with other research in Sensory Biology and Aquatic Ecology units. The Bok lab has recently been awarded several large grants from the ERC, Swedish Research Council, and the Human Frontiers Science Program, so the PhD student will benefit from a growing and dynamic academic environment.

  • Link to the general syllabus for third-cycle studies in Biology: General syllabus

Work duties

You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral education, which mainly consists of writing a doctoral thesis. You are expected to participate in a research project, doctoral courses, seminars and conferences. In the research project, you will use cutting edge behavioural, molecular, and neuroanatomical techniques to explore the function and evolution of possible colour receptors and their role in the visual ecology of polychaetes and cephalopods:

  1. ) Behaviour: At field stations in Italy and Japan, we will perform behavioural experiments testing the response of both species to colour and polarization stimuli. This will be based on custom light sources and projection screen setups that can vary the two light modalities independently.   
  2. ) Molecules: Alongside postdocs in the Bok Lab (Vanessa Stenvers and Alida Avola), the PhD student will use the results of single-nucleolus transcriptomic data to localize distinct photoreceptor and visual interneuron classes in the retina and optic lobe of both species. 
  3. ) Circuits: SBEM will be used to create connectomic resolution volume data for the retina and optic lobe of both species. Photoreceptor and interneuron synaptic connections and projections will be mapped to decipher the visual circuits. These data, along with the results from the molecular section will then be used to inform electrophysiology recordings to discover putative colour and polarisation opponent neurons in the optic lobe.

In addition to studies, a maximum of 20% of working time may be spent on teaching and other departmental work. You are expected to gain pedagogical experience as lab instructors for undergradate courses run by the Sensory Biology unit, and there are ample opportunities to gain experience in outreach and academic activities. You will be provided ample opportunities to present your work at local and international research conferences.

Qualifications

To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below.

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in Biology if the applicant has completed an independent work (e.g. degree project) in a relevant subject comprising at least 30 higher education credits and have good oral and written proficiency in English. The special qualification may also have been obtained through other equivalent education, which is assessed on a case-by-case basis. In order to enable interdisciplinary initiatives and significant in-depth studies in certain areas, qualifications other than the applicant's subject-specific competence in Biology may be taken into account.

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required:

  • Master’s degree in biology/marine biology or substantial equivalent knowledge acquired in some other way.
  • Practical experience with animal vision behavioral experiments.
  • Experience with fieldwork-based research.
  • Good ability to work independently and to formulate and tackle research problems.
  • Good written and oral communication skills
  • Good ability to cooperate with colleagues and collaborators
  • Very good knowledge of English, spoken and written

Selection criteria

The selection of eligible applicants will be made taking into account the ability to benefit from the training based on the following criteria:

  • Knowledge and/or expereince with animal vision, sensory biology, and visual ecology, and with the requirements and methods listed above.
  • Experience in data processing, statistical computing, and scripting in Python, Matlab and R, or equivalent.
  • Demonstrate independence, collegiality and enthusaism.
  • Passion for scientific communication and outreach.

We offer
Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme.

In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§.

More about terms of employment for doctoral students on Lund University’s Staff-pages. https://www.staff.lu.se/research-and-education/research-support/doctoral-education/terms-employment-doctoral-students

Other

How to apply

  • CV and personal letter with a justification of why you are interested in the training place/employment and in what way the research project matches your interests and your educational background.
  • Copies of issued study certificates and/or diplomas. These should prove your basic and special eligibility for the doctoral education subject and show that you have the subject knowledge required for the doctoral education project.

We welcome your application.

jobs.title: Doctoral student in Geographic Information Science (GIS) at MGeo
jobs.description_html:
The PhD student will be based at the GIS Centre, Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences, Lund University. The GIS Centre conducts research, education and development in Geographical Information Science (GIScience), with particular expertise in geospatial analysis, GeoAI, digital twins, and spatial data infrastructures.

The position will be part of the Centre's research activities in GeoAI and Spatial Intelligence, with a particular focus on Autonomous GIS. This emerging research direction explores how artificial intelligence, large language models and multi-agent systems can enable GIS to understand complex spatial problems, reason about geographic information, and autonomously plan and execute geospatial workflows.

The GIS Centre provides an interdisciplinary research environment where expertise in GIScience, geospatial technologies and AI meet applications in environmental analysis, urban planning, sustainability and other societal challenges. The PhD student will work closely with researchers at the Centre and have opportunities to collaborate with national and international research partners.

The Centre offers a collegial, supportive and collaborative working environment that encourages scientific curiosity, independent thinking and professional development.

Being a doctoral student

As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

As a doctoral student, you will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree.


Subject and project description

The doctoral student will be admitted to third-cycle studies in Geobiosphere Science, with a specialisation in Geographical Information Science (GIScience). GIScience is an interdisciplinary research field concerned with the theories, methods and technologies for collecting, managing, analysing, modelling and communicating geographical information. The subject encompasses both fundamental methodological research and applications across environmental, societal and technological domains.

The doctoral research will focus on Autonomous GIS and Spatial Intelligence, an emerging research direction at the intersection of GIScience and artificial intelligence. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs), GeoAI and multi-agent systems are creating new opportunities to transform GIS from systems that primarily execute user-defined operations into intelligent systems capable of interpreting spatial problems, reasoning about geographical information, planning and executing geospatial workflows, and evaluating their results.

Despite these advances, important scientific challenges remain. These include the ability of AI systems to understand spatial concepts and relationships, integrate geographic knowledge with computational reasoning, select and coordinate appropriate geospatial methods, and ensure the reliability, transparency and geographical validity of autonomous analyses.

The doctoral student will investigate methods and frameworks for advancing Spatial Intelligence and Autonomous GIS, potentially addressing topics such as geospatial reasoning with LLMs, multi-agent architectures, autonomous geospatial workflow planning and execution, integration of geographic knowledge and analytical tools, and evaluation of the reliability and quality of AI-generated geospatial analyses.

The research is expected to contribute new scientific knowledge and methods in GIScience while advancing the foundations of intelligent and increasingly autonomous geospatial systems. The specific research questions and methodological approaches will be further developed in collaboration with the supervisors during the doctoral studies.

Work duties

Your main responsibility will be to pursue doctoral studies and conduct independent research in Autonomous GIS and Spatial Intelligence, leading to a doctoral thesis. You will develop research questions, investigate and develop new methods, design and conduct experiments, evaluate results, and communicate your findings primarily through publications in high-quality, peer-reviewed scientific journals..

You will work closely with your supervisors and other researchers at the GIS Centre, while gradually developing your independence as a researcher. Your doctoral education will also include relevant doctoral courses, participation in research seminars, and opportunities to present and discuss your research at national and international scientific conferences. You will be encouraged to engage in research collaborations and contribute to the Centre's academic activities and research environment. International travel may be required for conferences, research visits and collaborative activities.

In addition to your doctoral studies, you may participate in teaching and other departmental duties, corresponding to a maximum of 20% of your working time. These duties may include assisting with teaching, supervising student exercises and projects, and contributing to educational activities, particularly in GIS, geospatial analysis and GeoAI. The extent and nature of these duties will be determined based on departmental needs and your qualifications and interests.

Admission requirements

A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant:

  • has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or
  • has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or
  • has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.

Specific admission requirements

  • To meet the specific admission requirements for third-cycle studies in Geobiosphere Science with a specialisation in Geographical Information Science, the applicant must have completed an independent degree project in a relevant subject comprising at least 30 higher education credits, or have acquired equivalent qualifications. Qualifications from other relevant disciplines may also be considered, particularly when appropriate for the interdisciplinary nature of the doctoral research.

 

Additional requirements

In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following qualifications and competences are also required:

  • A Master's degree in Geographical Information Science, Geoinformatics, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, or a closely related field.
  • Good knowledge of artificial intelligence and machine learning, including an understanding of fundamental methods and principles, and familiarity with modern deep learning approaches and large language models (LLMs).
  • Experience with AI and machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or similar technologies.
  • Strong programming skills in Python, with the ability to develop, implement, test and evaluate computational methods and algorithms.
  • Good analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to approach complex scientific and technical challenges systematically.
  • An interest in GIScience, geospatial analysis and spatial intelligence, with the motivation and ability to develop interdisciplinary expertise at the intersection of geographical information science and artificial intelligence.
  • Good ability to work independently and collaboratively, including the capacity to formulate research problems, take initiative and contribute constructively to an interdisciplinary research environment.
  • Good communication skills in English, both written and spoken.

 

The following qualifications will be considered advantageous:

  • Practical experience developing applications using LLMs, agentic AI, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool integration or multi-agent systems.
  • Experience with geospatial programming libraries and tools such as GeoPandas, Shapely, Rasterio, PyQGIS or ArcPy.
  • Knowledge of spatial reasoning and knowledge representation, including geographic semantics, ontologies, knowledge graphs or neuro-symbolic AI.
  • Experience in developing and evaluating computational methods and AI-based systems, including experimental design, software testing, version control, and integration of computational tools and APIs.
  • Demonstrated scientific writing skills, particularly experience preparing manuscripts or publications for peer-reviewed scientific journals.
  • Previous involvement in scientific research or publications in artificial intelligence, GIScience, GeoAI or related fields.

 

Selection criteria

The selection of eligible applicants will be made based on the above-mentioned qualifications and competences. In addition, personal qualifications will also be considered in the evaluation process including:

  • Strong scientific curiosity and creativity, with the ability to formulate original ideas and explore innovative approaches.
  • Ability to think critically, evaluate methods and results, and approach scientific challenges constructively.
  • A collegial and cooperative attitude, with a willingness to share knowledge, support colleagues and contribute positively to the research environment.
  • Good interpersonal and communication skills, including openness to feedback and respect for different perspectives.
  • Reliability, responsibility and professionalism, including the ability to honour commitments and contribute constructively to shared activities.
  • Motivation and enthusiasm for interdisciplinary research at the intersection of artificial intelligence and GIScience.

About the employment

The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, starting 2027-01-07 or due agreement. Third cycle studies at the Faculty of Science consist of full-time studies for 4 years. In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§.

How to apply

jobs.title: PhD student in biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases
jobs.description_html:
Description of the workplace

The Biomarkers in Brain Disease research group at the Department of Experimental Medical Science investigates how disease mechanisms in the body and brain interact in Huntington’s disease. This work involves in vivo and in vitro experiments, microscopy and molecular biology methods.

The workplace and research environment are shared by five research groups, all working on neurodegenerative diseases, with approximately 25–30 people in total.

Together, they create a stimulating and international research environment in which we share research equipment and chemicals and hold joint laboratory meetings. The atmosphere is friendly and encourages a wide range of discussions. The research group is active in the European Huntington’s Disease Network and Lund University Huntington Centre.

Project description

The body’s biological clock regulates functions such as sleep, metabolism, immune function and brain activity. The central clock in the hypothalamus coordinates rhythms in the body’s cells and organs, which also have their own rhythms. Disturbances in sleep and circadian rhythms are common in neurodegenerative diseases, including Huntington’s disease (HD). Research suggests that these disturbances are not merely symptoms but may contribute to neurodegeneration.

HD is an inherited disorder that affects movement, cognition and psychiatric function. The mutated gene, which contains an expanded CAG repeat sequence, and the huntingtin protein are expressed not only in neurons but also in cells throughout the body.

Despite increasing knowledge, it remains unclear how disruptions to the body’s biological clocks affect the course of HD. It is also unknown whether modifying clock function could alter disease progression in HD.

This doctoral project will combine in vitro and in vivo studies and use methods such as RNA sequencing. The project requires a balance between experimental laboratory work and data analysis.

Tasks and responsibilities

The main task for a doctoral student is to devote yourself to your doctoral studies, therefore you will be both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University.

In addition to your full-time doctoral studies, you may participate in the supervision of Bachelor’s or Master’s students.

Great emphasis will be placed on how the applicant, through his/her experience and competence, is judged to have the ability needed to complete the doctoral studies
