jobs.title: PhD in Physics-informed generative AI for dynamic cardiac MRI
jobs.description_html:
Do you want to make cardiac MRI safer for patients and the environment? Join PRIMA-CMR, a EuroTech Universities Alliance project between TU/e and the Technical University of Munich (TUM) and help to develop trustworthy generative AI that makes it possible to scan with far less contrast agent.

Information
Cardiac MRI gives unmatched insight into heart disease, but some of its most important exams depend on gadolinium-based contrast agents. Gadolinium can build up in the body, cannot be given to all patients, and is now an environmental pollutant. A large reduction in the dose would make cardiac MRI safer and available to more patients. At low doses, however, the images no longer contain enough signal for a reliable diagnosis. Current AI methods can make images that look realistic, but they cannot guarantee that what they show is real.

We are looking for a motivated PhD candidate to develop new generative AI methods that recover diagnostic information from low-dose cardiac MRI in a reliable and trustworthy way. Your work will combine knowledge of MR imaging physics, patient-specific clinical information, and uncertainty quantification. The aim is a model whose outputs clinicians can trust, and which tells them when it is not certain. You will validate the methods on real clinical data together with our clinical partners.

This PhD position is part of PRIMA-CMR, a collaborative project within the EuroTech Universities Alliance programme. You will be based at TU/e and spend six months at TUM in the group of prof. Julia Schnabel, which is a world leader in generative and multimodal AI. You will also work with international clinical and academic partners across Europe. This position is embedded in the Medical Image Analysis group, Department of Biomedical Engineering, TU/e. You will be supervised by dr. Cian Scannell, and co-supervised by prof. Julia Schnabel (TUM).

jobs.title: PhD Candidate in Complex Networks
jobs.description_html:
The Mathematical Institute (MI) of Leiden University and the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science (LIACS) are looking for a PhD Candidate in Complex Networks to commence at the earliest possible date and no later than April 2027.

The project investigates how structural properties observed in complex networks can be understood and modeled using mathematically tractable network models. The research will combine theoretical modeling with computational and data-driven investigation of real-world networks, with a particular emphasis on understanding how features such as spatial structure, clustering, heterogeneity, and connectivity shape network behavior.

Possible research directions include, but are not limited to, network science, spatial network modeling, random graph models, and data-driven methods for network analysis. We welcome candidates with an interest in real-world network data as well as in developing and analyzing mathematical models of complex networks. The precise balance between theoretical, computational, and data-driven work will depend on the candidate’s background and interests.

The position will be co-supervised by dr. Moritz Otto (MI) and dr. Akrati Saxena (LIACS). Michel Mandjes (MI) will act as promotor. Academic excellence is the main selection criterion.

What you will do
  • Conducting complex networks research at the intersection of mathematics and computer science.
  • Writing a publication-based PhD thesis.
  • Engaging in a limited number of teaching and supervision activities.

Where you will work
The PhD candidate will be employed at the Mathematical Institute and also be affiliated with the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science and AI (LIACS). In particular, the candidate will become part of the Leiden AlFa (Algorithmic Fairness: https://alfa.liacs.nl) group and the Probability research group, and collaborate closely with the Network Science group.
Both the research groups and the institutes are highly international and feature a mix of disciplinary and cultural backgrounds. There are plenty of additional opportunities for other types of interaction and collaboration, for example, at the Faculty of Science through the Leiden Complex Networks Network (LCN2) and nationally through the Dutch Network Science Society.

The Mathematical Institute focuses on four key research themes: Algebra, Geometry, and Number Theory; Analysis and Dynamical Systems; Probability; and Statistics and Data Science. There is extensive collaboration between these themes. For more information about the Mathematical Institute, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science/mathematics.
LIACS is one of the leading computer science departments in the Netherlands. We strive for excellence in a supportive institute where academic achievement, enjoyment, and diversity go hand in hand. For more information about LIACS, visit our website: http://www.cs.leiden.edu

What you bring
  • A university degree* in mathematics, computer science or a closely related field.
  • Knowledge in an area of research related to network science/complex networks, e.g., graph theory, probability, random graphs, complex systems, or topological data analysis.
  • Programming experience, preferably in Python, and willingness to develop strong computational skills (please mention your level of proficiency and knowledge of other programming languages in your CV).
  • Strong motivation for academic research.
  • Good English communication skills.
  • The ability to work independently and in a team.
  • You live and are officially registered as resident in The Netherlands or are willing to relocate upon starting the position.
    • Candidates who expect to complete their Master’s degree by early spring 2027 are also encouraged to apply.

What we offer
  • We offer a full-time position for initially one year. After a positive evaluation of the progress of the thesis, personal capabilities and compatibility, the appointment will be extended by a further three years.
  • A salary starting from € 3.204,= to € 4.051,= gross per month, based on a full-time appointment (38 hours, Payscale P)
  • A holiday allowance (8%), an end-of-year bonus (8,3%), and an attractive pension scheme at ABP;
  • Full reimbursement of public transport commuting costs for home-to-work travel;
  • Flexible working hours: as a standard, you are entitled to a minimum of 29 leave days on the basis of a full-time working week of 38 hours;
  • Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription and bicycle scheme;
  • If your work allows it, hybrid working is possible within the Netherlands;
  • A home-working allowance (day and internet allowance) and attention for good workplaces. The University will also provide you with a laptop and a mobile telephone.

For more information about employment conditions, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions

What we value
Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. We strive to be an open community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to fully develop themselves. We consider an inclusive academic environment, where students and staff can share their experiences and viewpoints, to be essential for the development of talent.

Want to apply or find out more?
Only applications received via the university’s application tool by 24 November 2026 can be considered.

Please send us
  • Your CV and full academic transcripts (bachelor’s and master’s)
  • A short cover letter of at most 2 pages detailing your motivation to apply for the position
  • A recent writing example (paper or thesis) that you are proud of and that reflects your academic writing skills
  • Names and contact details of at least one person who has agreed to be contacted for an academic reference (there is no need to send letters)

In case of doubt or questions about the suitability of your research interest for this position, feel very welcome to reach out to dr. Moritz Otto (m.f.p.otto@math.leidenuniv.nl) or dr. Akrati Saxena (a.saxena@liacs.leidenuniv.nl), before formally applying.

If you have any questions about the application procedure, please contact hr@math.leidenuniv.nl.

Interviews are expected to take place from 1 December 2026.

jobs.title: PhD position: Bacterial packaging of biocatalytic nanofactories
jobs.description_html:
What you will do
With the recent rapid progress in synthetic cells, sometimes known as artificial cells, the toolbox for liposome-encapsulated biocatalyst has massively expanded, creating complex systems that can act as ‘chemical nanofactories’ for biocatalytic cascade reactions. In this PhD project, you will optimise, apply and exploit a new technology in which biocatalysts are ‘packaged’ and confined in lipid vesicles during bacterial expression, which not only massively enriches biocatalyst yields, but also creates a ready-to-go liposome-encapsulated systems.

About the project
This project is a good match if:
  • you are interested in the expression, characterisation and engineering of biocatalysts.
  • you like working in a multidisciplinary team.
  • you are interested in contributing to the field of Synthetic Cells and biotechnology.

What you bring
We are looking for a highly motivated candidate who:
  • has a Master’s degree in Life Sciences and Technology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, or a related discipline
  • has experience in cloning, expression, purification and characterisation of biocatalysts, and preferably also in the preparation and analysis of lipid vesicles.
  • has a strong interest in structure-function relationship of enzymes, with proven excellent technical experimental and analytical skills and ability to work independently.
  • has a good proficiency in (scientific) English, and excellent communication skills.
  • feels comfortable working in a collaborative environment.

What we offer
We offer a vibrant research environment within the group of Prof. Lars Jeuken. The Jeuken lab is member of the Macromolecular Biochemistry group in the Leiden Institute of Chemistry, with a shared biochemical lab headed by 8 group leaders. We value ourselves on providing effective support to our PhD students, who work in a collaborative, transparent and inclusive work environment that inspires new knowledge.

We also offer:
  • An employment contract for the duration of one year with a view to permanent employment. This contract falls under the CLA of Dutch Universities;
  • A salary between €3204 - €4051 gross per month, based on a full-time appointment (38 hours) (PhD student);
  • A holiday allowance (8%), an end-of-year bonus (8,3%), and an attractive pension scheme at ABP;
  • Full reimbursement of public transport commuting costs for home-to-work travel;
  • Flexible working hours: as a standard, you are entitled to a minimum of 29 leave days on the basis of a full-time working week of 38 hours; you can also save for extra leave, for example by working 40 hours a week, and in this way accrue an extra 96 leave hours, or exchange 96 leave hours for a 36-hour week.
  • Lots of options when it comes to secondary employment conditions; we can, for example, discuss options for a sabbatical or paid parental leave. Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription and bicycle scheme;
  • If your work allows it, hybrid working is possible within the Netherlands;
  • A home-working allowance (day and internet allowance) and attention for good workplaces. The University will also provide you with a laptop and a mobile telephone.

For more information about employment conditions, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions

Want to apply or find out more?
If you want to apply to this position, please click the application button.

Do you have questions about this position? Please contact Prof. Lars Jeuken at L.J.C.Jeuken@lic.leidenuniv.nl

Your application should include a motivation letter clearly indicating WHY you apply for this position and project and WHAT makes you a suitable candidate, an extensive CV, the courses you took and grades you obtained in your Master’s studies, and the names and contact details of at least two references.

You can apply until 27 November 2026 using the application button below.
  • In choosing between candidates, in case of equal suitability, preference will be given to internal candidates, women, the occupationally disabled and employees with a migration background.
  • You live and are officially registered as resident in The Netherlands or are willing to relocate upon starting the position.
  • A pre-employment screening (references, diplomas, certificate of good conduct (VOG)) may be part of the selection procedure.
  • We ensure that our lecturers have a good level of English competency. Lectures who teach subjects in English have a minimum level of C1 for their English proficiency. We also believe it is important for international staff to have a good level of Dutch: they are expected to have at least C1 level of Dutch proficiency. Other staff who have the prospect of a permanent position are expected to have at least a passive understanding of Dutch.
  • Leiden University expects faculty members to obtain the Basic Teaching Qualification (BKO). If the new employee does not yet hold this qualification or its equivalent, they must be willing to obtain it within two years.
  • Acquisition in response to this vacancy is not appreciated. If you nevertheless choose to send us CVs, no rights can be derived from this. #LI-Hybrid

You can find more information about the faculty of Science at https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science/about-faculty-of-science. For more information about working at Leiden university please visit https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at.

Where you will work
Leiden University is one of Europe’s leading international research universities. Thanks to its committed and inspired employees, the university enjoys a leading role in academic research and education. Every year, Leiden University scores very well in prominent rankings. This means that, to maintain our position, the bar is set very high. Regardless of the work you do at our university, you are always encouraged to broaden your horizons, develop your talents and reach your full potential.

About the Faculty and Institute
The Faculty of Science at Leiden University is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. It is a faculty where personal and academic development are top priorities. Our people are committed to expand fundamental knowledge by curiosity and to look beyond the borders of their own discipline; their aim is to benefit science, and to contribute to addressing the major societal challenges of the future.

The research carried out at the Faculty of Science is very diverse, ranging from mathematics, information science, astronomy, physics, chemistry and bio-pharmaceutical sciences to biology and environmental sciences. The research activities are organized in eight institutes. These institutes offer eight bachelors’ and twelve master’s programmes. The faculty has grown strongly in recent years and now has more than 2,300 staff and over 5,000 students. We are located at the heart of Leiden’s Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s biggest science parks, where university and business life come together.

The research is embedded within the Leiden Institute of Chemistry, with its long-standing traditions of excellence in research. Apart from a state-of-the-art electrochemistry laboratory, and excellent synthesis facilities, preparation and measurement facilities, unconventional nanofabrication equipment and experimental setups to measure ion transport will be designed supported by outstanding mechanical and electronic workshops. We foster an international and collaborative atmosphere and have close ties to other institutes housed within our Faculty of Science and with many research groups within the Netherlands, and many prominent labs abroad.

What we value
Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. Leiden University aims to be an inclusive community in which all students and staff members feel valued, respected, and have the freedom to develop to their full potential. Diversity in experiences and perspectives enriches our teaching and strengthens our research. High-quality education and research mean inclusive education and research.

jobs.title: PhD student on Key Performance Indicators for biodiversity-inclusive agriculture
jobs.description_html:
The Institute of Environmental Sciences CML and Faculty of Science is looking for:
PhD student on Key Performance Indicators for biodiversity-inclusive agriculture

In collaboration with Technical University Eindhoven and Wageningen University and Research, you will design validated and tangible key performance indicators of biodiversity improvements in agriculture and horticulture.

What you will do
Are you motivated to contribute to the transition towards nature-inclusive agriculture and horticulture? Do you want to work at the interface of innovation science, system dynamics, value chains, biodiversity restoration, and real-world decision-making by farmers and agrifood stakeholders? Join the NWO-KIC project RISE – Resilient Integrated Systems for Ecosystem restoration as a PhD candidate and co-develop a system dynamics model for agrifood transitions in an interdisciplinary team of four PhD candidates, with farmers and societal stakeholders.

Within that project, your key responsibilities are:
  • Evaluating the barriers and opportunities for nature-inclusive initiatives in farming practices.
  • Designing validated Key Performance Indicators for biodiversity improvement in farming practices for two regional case areas.
  • Creating actionable biodiversity strategies and indicators for regional agricultural stakeholders.
  • Upscaling frameworks of biodiversity strategies in agricultural landscapes to new applications.

Where you will work

Research at our faculty
Leiden University is situated between Amsterdam (36 km) and The Hague (15 km) and was founded in 1575, making it the oldest university in the Netherlands. It houses around 35,000 students originating from 112 nationalities, facilitated by approximately 8,000 staff.

The Institute of Environmental Science (CML) at Leiden University offers a vibrant and supportive community of scientists committed to the challenges of sustainability. CML distinguishes itself for its attention to professional development in coordination with the interests of its scientists. As such, there are plenty of opportunities to learn new skills, expand your knowledge, collaborate across disciplines, and experiment in a friendly environment fully embodying academic freedom across all career levels.

The core focus of CML is to perform research and education in the interdisciplinary field of Environmental Sciences. CML focuses on the sustainable use of natural resources and preservation of natural capital and biodiversity. CML has a culture of mutual support and collaboration between researchers. CML has two Departments: Industrial Ecology (CML-IE) and Environmental Biology (CML-EB). Presently, about 150 fte (including postdocs and PhDs) are employed at CML. CML further collaborates with TU Delft and Erasmus University in the Leiden-Delft-Erasmus Centre for Sustainability (LDE-CfS), and with the Naturalis Biodiversity Centre.

The Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML) is positioned in the Faculty of Sciences. The Faculty of Science is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. It is a faculty where personal and academic development are top priorities. Our people are committed to expanding fundamental knowledge by curiosity and looking beyond the borders of their own discipline; their aim is to benefit science and to make a contribution to addressing the major societal challenges of the future. The research carried out at the Faculty of Science is very diverse, ranging from mathematics, information science, astronomy, physics, chemistry and bio-pharmaceutical sciences to biology and environmental sciences. The research activities are organized in eight institutes. These institutes offer eight bachelor’s and twelve master’s programmes. The faculty has grown strongly in recent years and now has more than 2.800 staff and almost 6000 students. We are located at the heart of Leiden’s Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s biggest science parks, where university and business life come together.

For more information, see www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science. Information about CML can be found at www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science/environmental-sciences.

What you bring
A successful candidate has:
  • A master’s degree in biology, environmental sciences, or a related field
  • Demonstrated interest in biodiversity research, ideally in agricultural or horticultural settings
  • Interest in working in an interdisciplinary team
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to interact with academic and non-academic stakeholders.
  • Excellent written and spoken English.
  • Willingness to conduct fieldwork in Dutch agricultural and horticultural regions.
  • Speaking Dutch is a strong advantage, because the project involves interviews and workshops with Dutch farmers, growers, and regional stakeholders.

We are committed to building an inclusive and diverse team, welcoming applications from individuals of all backgrounds and experiences. Your unique perspectives will enrich our research and foster a collaborative and innovative environment.

What we offer
We offer an initial one-year contract, with an option to extend for up to 4 years based on performance, following the pay scale P in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities. Salary ranges from € 3.204 to € 4.051 gross per month based on a full-time position.

At our institution, we believe in flexibility and work-life balance! With a full-time position (38 hours per week), you are entitled to 232 vacation hours per year, which is equivalent to 30.5 vacation days (based on a 38-hour work week). If you value flexibility, you have the freedom to adjust your working hours. For example, you could choose to work 40 hours per week, earning extra compensation hours. Alternatively, if you prefer a shorter work week, you can work 36 hours per week by using some of your vacation days to create more time for yourself. You’ll work closely with your supervisor to tailor your schedule in a way that suits both your needs and the team’s.

In addition, we offer a comprehensive benefits package, including:
  • Holiday allowance (8%) and an end-of-year bonus (8.3%)
  • An attractive pension scheme with ABP, ensuring your financial well-being both now and in the future
  • Extensive options for secondary employment conditions: You can explore options such as sabbaticals, paid parental leave, and the individual choices model, which allows you to exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits like an advantageous sports subscription, bicycle scheme, and childcare options
  • Hybrid working options: If your role allows, you can enjoy the flexibility of working from home within the Netherlands
  • Home-working allowance: You’ll receive a home-working allowance (for both workdays and internet), and the university will provide you with a laptop and support for creating a comfortable home office
  • PhD student support: As a PhD student, you’ll be part of the Graduate School of Science, which offers a variety of training courses at three levels: professional courses, skills training, and personal effectiveness

We are committed to offering a flexible, supportive, and rewarding work environment, designed to help you grow both professionally and personally. For more information about the working conditions, please visit: https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions

What we value

Diversity
At the Faculty of Science, we value inclusiveness and strive for a diverse community with equal opportunities for all. We give full support to our staff in achieving their potential to become independent academic researchers and teachers. For more information about our policy on diversity and equality please go to the diversity page on our website: https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/dossiers/diversity

Female researchers are also welcome to join the Researchers In Science for Equality network of the Faculty of Science (rise.nu).

  • Curriculum Vitae
  • Cover letter (max 2 pages.)
  • Names and contact details of at least two referees

The deadline for submissions is Monday November 23rd, 2026; applications received after this date will not be considered.

The interviews will take place on first or second week of December 2026. The interviews will be conducted online to ensure a level playing field for (international) applicants.

jobs.title: PhD Researcher: Environmental Impacts of Spatial Demographic Change
jobs.description_html:
The Institute of Environmental Sciences CML and Faculty of Science is looking for:
PhD Researcher: Environmental impacts of spatial demographic change

Excited to use geospatial and environmental analysis tools to explore the implications of spatial demographic change for urban planning, resource demand, and the environment?

Key responsibilities
The primary objective of this PhD project is to advance understanding of how spatial population distribution, demographic change (including aging population and smaller households), and urban form jointly shape future resource demand and GHG emissions. The project will evaluate core trade-offs in material and energy requirements and emissions, balancing the efficiency gains of urban density against the rise in vacant buildings and underutilized infrastructure caused by regional depopulation. Ultimately, the research will inform urban and regional development strategies to minimize net land take and GHG emissions, while catering to the needs of changing populations across the rural-urban continuum in Europe.

As a PhD researcher on this project, you will:
  • Develop high-resolution activity demand models for building and transport sectors under future spatially refined scenarios of European demographic change.
  • Integrate activity demand projections with material flow and life-cycle models to quantify future energy requirements, material intensity, and GHG emissions.
  • Evaluate adaptive reuse and circular strategies for vacant buildings and underutilized transport infrastructure in depopulating and/or aging regions.
  • Design integrated spatial planning scenarios combining built environment transformations with transport infrastructure investments to support high wellbeing and low resource/emissions pathways across population change and urban/rural contexts

Where you will work
Leiden University is situated between Amsterdam (36 km) and The Hague (15 km) and was founded in 1575, making it the oldest university in the Netherlands. It houses around 35,000 students originating from 112 nationalities, facilitated by approximately 8,000 staff.

The Institute of Environmental Science (CML) at Leiden University offers a vibrant and supportive community of scientists committed to the challenges of sustainability. CML distinguishes itself for its attention to professional development in coordination with the interests of its scientists. As such, there are plenty of opportunities to learn new skills, expand your knowledge, collaborate across disciplines, and experiment in a friendly environment fully embodying academic freedom across all career levels.

The core focus of CML is to perform research and education in the interdisciplinary field of Environmental Sciences. CML focuses on the sustainable use of natural resources and preservation of natural capital and biodiversity. CML has a culture of mutual support and collaboration between researchers. CML has two Departments: Industrial Ecology (CML-IE) and Environmental Biology (CML-EB). Presently, about 150 fte (including postdocs and PhDs) are employed at CML. CML further collaborates with TU Delft and Erasmus University in the Leiden-Delft-Erasmus Centre for Sustainability (LDE-CfS), and with the Naturalis Biodiversity Centre.

The Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML) is positioned in the Faculty of Sciences. The Faculty of Science is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. It is a faculty where personal and academic development are top priorities. Our people are committed to expanding fundamental knowledge by curiosity and looking beyond the borders of their own discipline; their aim is to benefit science and to make a contribution to addressing the major societal challenges of the future. The research carried out at the Faculty of Science is very diverse, ranging from mathematics, information science, astronomy, physics, chemistry and bio-pharmaceutical sciences to biology and environmental sciences. The research activities are organized in eight institutes. These institutes offer eight bachelor’s and twelve master’s programmes. The faculty has grown strongly in recent years and now has more than 2.800 staff and almost 6000 students. We are located at the heart of Leiden’s Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s biggest science parks, where university and business life come together.

For more information, see www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science. Information about CML can be found at www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science/environmental-sciences.

jobs.title: PhD on Ultracold electron source development for time-resolved protein crystallography
jobs.description_html:
Are you excited to solve technical challenges with a real-world application?
Are you eager to build something truly unique in the world?

Development of a pulsed electron source with extreme transverse bunch brightness, based on photo-ionization of laser-cooled atoms, for time-resolved protein crystallography.

Context: ERC-funded project “Cool T-ReX”

Goal: Develop a unique and innovative instrument to enable time-resolved protein crystallography with electrons (and be the first in the world in doing so).

Scientific relevance: Understanding how proteins function is crucial to improving medicine and unraveling processes that are fundamental to life. Time-resolved protein crystallography uniquely allows following the conformational change of a protein with unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution, yielding a “molecular movie” of how the protein performs its function. This is currently only possible on large-scale X-ray facilities. In this project we will build the very first instrument that can make such movies through time-resolved protein crystallography with electrons rather than X-rays, on a laboratory-scale setup. Next, through collaboration with leading research groups in time-resolved protein crystallography, we will demonstrate the instrument’s capabilities in time-resolved crystallography experiments on photo-active proteins with medical relevance (and used in the field of optogenetics, awarded this year’s Nobel Prize in Medicine!).

Your role: Drive the development of this unique instrument. You will build on our research group’s two decades of experience in building electron sources based on the photo-ionization of laser-cooled atoms. This technique has demonstrated electron pulses with record-low transverse temperatures, corresponding to a high transverse coherence, as needed for protein crystallography. In this project we will push this transverse coherence even further, making use of some of the unique capabilities of this source technology. The result will be an electron beam with a “transverse bunch brightness” that is three orders of magnitude beyond the current state of the art. To reach this ambitious goal, you will work with a team of experienced technicians, a second PhD student, a PostDoc, and the PI (Julius Huijts). We are part of the larger Coherence and Quantum Technology group in the Department of Applied Physics.

jobs.title: PhD in Photonic Sensors for Light-Starved Applications
jobs.description_html:
Are you passionate about cutting-edge semiconductor technology for solving real societal problems? Then this PhD position could be a fit for you. In this project you will push the limit of spectroscopic analysis by developing novel photonic chips working at ultralow light levels (down to femtowatts). These chips will form the core of sensors which are crucial for advancing healthcare and the energy transition.

Information
Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) allows characterizing materials and tissues, and it is widely used in industry. Our group has recently developed integrated spectral sensors, based on an advanced nanophotonic platform. These low-cost spectral chips, already commercialized by our spin-off MantiSpectra, provide detailed spectral information in the spectral region 900-1700 nm and allow measuring materials properties. However, they are based on reflection and therefore require a powerful light source to illuminate the object. Their application could be widely extended if they were sensitive enough to measure light emitted by a sample through fluorescence or Raman scattering. This requires pushing the limit of spectral sensing technology to combine spectral discrimination and detection at the femtowatt/low picowatt level, in a single device. To this aim the project will explore advanced device designs and fabrication methods, and collaborate with other TU/e research groups for the integration with low-noise amplification. The sensors will be fabricated at the NanoLab@TU/e cleanroom facility, using advanced semiconductor equipment. Their application to low-light sensing applications will also be explored during the project, in collaboration with industrial partners.

jobs.title: PhD student: Effect van interventies op luchtkwaliteit in Nederland
jobs.description_html:
Luchtverontreiniging is verantwoordelijk voor ongeveer 80% van de ziektelast. Wereldwijd is blootstelling thuis en op het werk naar schatting verantwoordelijk voor 16% van alle sterfgevallen. In Nederland wordt naar schatting 8,5% toegeschreven aan milieuvervuiling en nog eens 2,7% aan vervuiling op het werk. Het Institute for Risk Assessment Sciences (IRAS) van de Universiteit Utrecht onderzoekt hoe lokale interventies en bredere maatschappelijke transities de luchtverontreiniging beïnvloeden in praktijkgerichte Living Labs en aan de hand van beschikbare data.

Wat ga je doen?
Je gaat werken aan het NWA-ORC project ExpACT: een onderzoeksproject dat de gezondheidseffecten van luchtverontreiniging onderzoekt. Het project ontwikkelt verbeterde monitoringtechnologieën en methoden die kunnen inspelen op veranderende niveaus en bronnen van luchtverontreiniging. Je onderzoekt hoe interventies en transities in de praktijk de luchtverontreiniging in de ExpACT Living Labs veranderen. Interventies zijn lokale maatregelen, zoals een geluidsscherm langs een spoorlijn of de tijdelijke sluiting van een luchthaven. Ook onderzoek je hoe goed de gebruikte meet- en modelleermethoden deze effecten kunnen vaststellen. In elk Living Lab worden de onderzoeksvragen en methoden doorlopend bijgesteld door middel van co-creatie met relevante belanghebbenden, onder wie inwoners en professionals. Je werkt daarbij nauw samen met de Living Labs en met ExpACT-partners die nieuwe sensoren en apparatuur ontwikkelen. Je integreert hun technologieën en modelleertechnieken in de Living Labs.

In landelijke gebieden, waar veranderingen in de landbouw invloed hebben op de ammoniakuitstoot, gaat het onder meer om uitbreiding van een passief NH3-meetnetwerk, evaluatie van een mobiele NH3-sensor en onderzoek naar de vraag of filters kunnen worden gebruikt om bio-organische deeltjes en pollen te detecteren.

In stedelijke gebieden kan het onderzoek bestaan uit het meten van metalen en mogelijk andere emissies van spoorwegen, en het vaststellen van het effect van een gepland geluidsscherm op deze concentraties.

In Eindhoven onderzoek je het effect van de geplande tijdelijke sluiting van Eindhoven Airport op de concentraties ultrafijnstof. Je bespreekt gedurende het hele project met inwoners en professionals wat er gemeten moet worden, wat de resultaten betekenen en hoe bruikbaar de instrumenten in de praktijk zijn.

Je wordt begeleid binnen het Institute for Risk Assessment Sciences (IRAS) van de Universiteit Utrecht. Je profiteert van nauwe samenwerking met onderzoekers, onderzoeksinstituten en partners van Living Labs in heel Nederland.

jobs.title: PhD in supramolecular interactions in organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors
jobs.description_html:
Are you fascinated by how molecular-scale interactions determine the real-world performance of functional materials? In this PhD project, you will study a new class of materials that find application in future technologies ranging from neuromorphic computing and bioelectronics to energy storage. Are you ready to help unravel the inner workings of these fascinating materials by investigating them during operation?

Your research
In your PhD project, you will uncover how intermolecular interactions and supramolecular morphology govern the functionality of organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs). Bridging the fields of OMIECs and supramolecular chemistry, you will investigate these relationships through in-depth operando characterization.

OMIECs are soft materials that conduct both electrons and ions, highly promising for applications ranging from energy storage and solar fuels to bioelectronics and neuromorphic computing. However, electrons, ions, solvent and the molecular structure all reorganize during operation, making it difficult to disentangle how molecular-scale interactions ultimately determine macroscopic function.

You will develop characterization methods and experimental setups to probe intermolecular interactions as OMIECs operate. Spectroelectrochemistry will be a key tool; developing operando cells, setups, and experiments that enable you to discern dynamic spectral signatures of molecular packing. By following changes in supramolecular organization during electrochemical doping, your work will reveal how doping affects supramolecular organization.

You will also determine how supramolecular packing governs doping efficiency and dynamics, linking morphology to device-relevant properties, by studying varied samples of available supramolecular building blocks. These fundamental insights will provide a supramolecular knob for tuning material functionality, thereby introducing new ways to control material behavior.

The key outcome of your research is a mechanistic framework describing the bidirectional interplay between OMIEC doping and supramolecular interactions. Building on this framework, you will ultimately design switchable supramolecular OMIEC systems in collaboration with other researchers, targeting applications in in-material computing. Beyond these systems, your fundamental insights will contribute to the general development of next-generation computing and adaptive bioelectronics.

Your environment and support
As a member of the Optoelectronic Mixed Conductors group at the Department of Chemical Engineering and Chemistry, you will conduct your research under the supervision of Prof. Tom van der Pol. Your project is highly interdisciplinary, with opportunities to collaborate with researchers across the department. You will become part of a broad and vibrant scientific community, including the Institute for Complex Molecular Systems.

At TU/e and within the Optoelectronic Mixed Conductors group, curiosity-driven research and personal development go hand in hand. You will have the freedom to pursue ambitious scientific questions while receiving the guidance and support needed to develop your own ideas and expertise. Your supervisory team will support you in developing the skills, confidence, and scientific perspective needed to uncover the mechanisms that govern OMIECs and to shape your own path as a researcher.

jobs.title: PhD in Multifunctional Polymer Composites
jobs.description_html:
Are you inspired to push the limits of polymeric materials for lighter and smarter defense platforms? Join us to develop a new generation of 3D-printed composite panels that shield electronics from electromagnetic threats and withstand impact.

Information
We are offering 2 PhD positions within project VALOR, an ambitious, interdisciplinary collaboration between academia, industry and government partners. The project aims to develop a new generation of lightweight composite panels that both shield sensitive electronics from electromagnetic threats and withstand impact events, helping to make defense platforms safer and more resilient.

Naval ships, drones and military vehicles increasingly depend on electronic radar, communication and navigation systems that must be protected against electromagnetic interference and radar detection. Today, this is mostly done with metals, which block practically all wave power with only a thin layer. However, they add weight, corrode, and reflect electromagnetic waves, making platforms easier to detect. Project VALOR tackles this challenge by merging two fields that have so far been developed separately: absorption-based electromagnetic shielding and impact-resistant sandwich structures. By combining 3D-printed architected nanocomposite materials with predictive modelling into one integrated design strategy, the project will construct a design framework for panels that are able to both carry loads and absorb electromagnetic waves, with a performance that can be tailored to specific (defense) applications.

Your role
We are recruiting two PhD candidates who will work as a team throughout the project, i.e. from material screening to design and testing of larger scale panel demonstrators. Both candidates will conduct a combination of experimental and numerical work and collaborate closely with industrial partners within the consortium. More specifically:
  • PhD 1 focuses on mechanics and manufacturing: 3D printing nanocomposite lattice materials, fabricating composite facesheets, conducting mechanical tests, constructing and validating mechanical finite element models.
  • PhD 2 focuses on electromagnetic testing and design: formulating polymer nanocomposite materials and characterizing their electromagnetic behaviour, designing and testing absorbing architected nanocomposite structures, conducting electromagnetic shielding simulations.

Your team and network
You will join the Processing and Performance of Materials section in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at TU/e. The group has around 20 PhD and post-doctoral researchers working on how processing, structure and properties connect in polymers and polymer-based composite materials. The group is known for its integrated experimental-numerical approach to tailor the performance of these materials. You will have access to state-of-the-art computational facilities and laboratories dedicated to rheology, polymer processing (incl. additive manufacturing) and mechanical testing. You will be supervised by Frederik Van Loock (project leader), Ruth Cardinaels and Tom Engels.

jobs.title: PhD in Communication-Optimized Inference in Large Language Models
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in the communication networks behind modern AI systems? Would you like to combine mathematical modeling with experiments on programmable network hardware to make AI infrastructure faster and more energy-efficient? In this PhD project, you will develop models and orchestration methods for the networks that connect GPUs during large language model inference. Are you our next PhD candidate in high-performance AI networking?

Your research challenge
Large language models rely on powerful computing infrastructure to generate responses. When inference is distributed across multiple GPUs, these devices must continuously exchange intermediate results. Network congestion and communication overhead can therefore limit performance and increase energy consumption, even when substantial computing resources are available.

In the project Communication-Optimized Inference in Large Language Models (COIL), you will investigate how analytical network models can support the design and operation of AI clusters. The project combines network performance modeling, optimization, and experimental research, giving you the opportunity to connect mathematical foundations with practical challenges in AI infrastructure.

You will develop fast, composable analytical models using Network Calculus, a mathematical framework for analyzing communication networks. These models will capture interactions between inference traffic, network architecture, and mechanisms such as flow control and congestion feedback. They will provide bounds on communication latency and buffer requirements, complemented by energy estimates based on measurement-calibrated power models.

Building on these models, you will explore how architectural choices—including network topology, link bandwidth, and parallelization strategies—affect performance and energy consumption. You will develop tools that help cluster designers evaluate promising configurations efficiently.

You will also investigate how the models can guide runtime decisions, such as workload placement, prioritization, routing, or resource reservation. A focused prototype will demonstrate how model-informed decisions can improve the operation of an existing network.

Experimental validation will be an integral part of your research. You will use measurements from AI infrastructure and conduct reproducible experiments on programmable networking testbeds. Technologies of interest include Ethernet-based AI networks, emerging Ultra Ethernet mechanisms, P4-programmable switches, and SmartNICs. Finally, you will evaluate the results from the testbeds on real AI infrastructure in collaboration with our partner SURF.

Through this combination of theory, software development, and experimentation, you will contribute to more responsive and energy-efficient AI infrastructure. The project also offers opportunities to share your findings with networking standardization communities and to release research tools and experimental results openly.

An interdisciplinary and international environment
You will conduct your research under the main supervision of Prof. Lisa Maile who leads the Network Modeling and Design (NoMaD) lab. NoMaD is part of the Electronic Systems group in the Department of Electrical Engineering at Eindhoven University of Technology. Your supervision will also include partners from the Advanced Models by Open Research and Engineering (AMOR/e) Lab of Computer Science and the Model-Based Design Lab from Electrical Engineering.

The position is funded through the EuroTech programme, which promotes research collaboration between leading technical universities across Europe. As part of this project, you will collaborate closely with Prof. Georg Carle and his research group on Network Architectures and Services at the Technical University of Munich (TUM). As part of this collaboration, you will spend six-month in Munich with the group at TUM, where you will gain hands-on experience with programmable network hardware and reproducible experimental infrastructure.

jobs.title: PhD in experimental physics: how do you make the first antimatter molecule?
jobs.description_html:
When a proton meets a hydrogen atom, the pair can emit a photon and stay together as H₂⁺. This is how the first molecules formed after the Big Bang, and it is one of the proposed routes to the first antimatter molecule, yet it has never been measured. In the NWO Vidi project SAMURAI, you will study these collisions one quantum state at a time: instead of colliding atoms, we use lasers to prepare a hydrogen molecule at the moment of a collision and watch it fall apart. You will be part of a small group in which experiment and theory go hand in hand.

Your duties
  • excite H₂ with two tunable extreme-ultraviolet lasers (60–205 nm), built in our lab and unique in the Netherlands, and image the fragments with velocity-map imaging
  • aim for the first spectroscopic observation of the excited electronic states of H₂⁺, calculated by Edward Teller in his PhD thesis in 1930 and never seen since
  • trap H₂⁺ ions and use millimetre waves and magnetic fields to control how they come apart
  • work towards the first measurement of radiative association: joining a cold proton and a cold hydrogen atom with light, next to a crystal of laser-cooled Be⁺ ions
  • compare your data with multichannel quantum-defect theory and scattering calculations, and contribute to the theory yourself if you like
  • develop your skills in lasers and nonlinear optics, ultrahigh vacuum, electronics, CAD design and scientific programming
  • present your results at international conferences and publish them in peer-reviewed journals

jobs.title: PhD Position Bayesian Modeling and Counterfactual Methods for Nanoparticle Transport in Human Tissue
jobs.description_html:
Shape the future of nanoparticle safety and design. Join TU Delft as a PhD researcher using Bayesian and counterfactual modelling to predict nanoparticle transport in human tissue.

Job description
We are looking for a PhD candidate to build the computational model at the center of a European project on nanoparticle transport in human tissue. You will join the research group of Dr. Sepinoud Azimi, working within the SYNERGIE project (Horizon Europe), a consortium of thirteen partners including Fraunhofer, Roche, the Karolinska Institute, University Hospital Aachen, Mimetas, Ruhr University Bochum and Maastricht University.

Small particles from the environment have been detected in human blood, placenta and brain tissue, but it is still not clear what they do there. Dose-response data for humans does not exist and animal studies have not transferred well, and as a result there is no exposure limit for these particles.

Part of the reason prediction is so hard is that a particle changes as it moves through the body. It acquires a layer of proteins, it aggregates with other particles, and depending on the material it may partly degrade, so that the particle reaching a given tissue is not the same object that was administered or characterised at the start. Most transport models do not account for this. They treat the particle as fixed, which means they are predicting the fate of something that has already changed.

The same difficulty affects engineered nanoparticles for drug delivery, and it is one of the reasons so few of them reach their intended target.

SYNERGIE is building a platform of nine human tissue-on-chip models that can be connected to follow a particle through uptake, circulation and storage. TU Delft leads the in silico work package.

As a PhD candidate, you will:
  • Build a mechanistic model of how particles move between nine human tissues, and calibrate it against experimental data using Bayesian inference.
  • Work out which physical and chemical properties of a particle decide where it ends up.
  • Develop methods that go beyond prediction: for a particle that behaves badly, what is the smallest change that would fix it, and when should that answer not be trusted.
  • Release the model as open-source software and support its use in regulatory dialogue.

You will also contribute to teaching in the department and to the supervision of BSc projects.

You will work alongside a postdoctoral researcher and PhD candidates on related problems, and interact with experimental partners across the SYNERGIE consortium. You will have access to the DelftBlue high-performance computing cluster.

The intended start date is January 2027.     

Job requirements
  • MSc in applied mathematics, computational science, physics, systems biology, or a closely related quantitative field.
  • Demonstrated experience building and solving ODE or dynamical systems models.
  • Demonstrated experience with Bayesian inference in a probabilistic programming framework such as PyMC, Stan or NumPyro.
  • Strong scientific programming in Python. Please point us to a repository.
  • Excellent written and spoken English.

Preferred qualifications:
  • Continuous optimization or optimal control.
  • Causal inference or counterfactual reasoning.
  • Surrogate modelling, Gaussian processes, or emulation.
  • Physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling or systems pharmacology.
  • Experience packaging and documenting scientific software.
  • No background in toxicology, nanomaterials, chemistry or biology is required.

TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.

For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.

At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.

Faculty Technology, Policy & Management
The Faculty of TPM provides an important contribution to solving complex technical-social issues, such as energy transition, mobility, digitalisation, water management and (cyber) security. TPM does this with its excellent education and research at the intersection of technology, society and policy. We combine insights from both engineering and social sciences as well as the humanities. TPM develops robust models and designs, is internationally oriented and has an extensive network of knowledge institutions, companies, social organisations and governments.

Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Technology, Policy and Management.

Conditions of employment
Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met.

Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%.

As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills.

The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged.

Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. jobs.title: PhD Position in Neuroimaging, LLM, Genetics and Cross-species comparison
jobs.description_html:
Do you enjoy working with complex neuroimaging data, large datasets and computational methods? Do you want to work at the intersection of genetics, neuroimaging, neuroscience, neurodiversity and cross-species analyses? We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to join the Connectome Lab at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam

The Connectome Lab at the Center for Neurogenomics and Cognitive Research (CNCR), Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, is seeking a PhD candidate in Neuroimaging, Genetics and Cross-species comparison.

The project aims to understand how variation in brain anatomy and connectivity contributes to the remarkable diversity of the human brain, and how these features relate to principles of brain evolution. We will combine large-scale human neuroimaging datasets with comparative datasets across species to investigate variation in brain structure, connectivity and functional organization.

A central goal is to understand which aspects of brain organization are highly conserved, which show substantial variation between individuals, and which features may have emerged or expanded during human brain evolution. The project therefore brings together neuroimaging, connectomics, neurodiversity, comparative neuroscience and computational neuroscience.

You will work with large structural MRI, diffusion MRI and resting-state fMRI datasets and develop and apply computational approaches to quantify variation in brain organization across individuals, populations and species. There is particularly attention for the use of LLM in data mining.

You will be part of the computational neuroimaging Lab led by Prof. Martijn van den Heuvel and work in an interdisciplinary environment with researchers from neuroimaging, computational neuroscience, genetics, psychology, psychiatry and artificial intelligence.

Your duties
  • analyse large-scale structural MRI, diffusion MRI and resting-state fMRI datasets
  • develop and apply pipelines for cortical reconstruction, tractography, functional connectivity and connectome analysis
  • investigate individual variation and neurodiversity in brain structure and connectivity
  • integrate genetics with neuroimaging
  • perform comparative analyses of human and non-human brain organization in the context of brain evolution
  • integrate findings across different neuroimaging datasets and imaging modalities
  • develop and apply computational and statistical approaches for analysing brain networks
  • contribute to reproducible and open neuroimaging workflows

jobs.title: PhD: Developing methodological standards for studying the effectiveness of new digital interventions
jobs.description_html:
Join our interdisciplinary team at the Methodology of Educational Science Research Group (CMPO) and the Center for Contextual Psychiatry (CCP) at KU Leuven, one of Europe’s most renowned research universities. The CMPO, part of the Faculty of Psychology and Educational Sciences, is internationally recognized for its expertise in advanced statistical modeling and research methodology, encompassing both quantitative and qualitative approaches. Prof. Ginette Lafit leads innovative work to advance quantitative methods in ESM study design and drives methodological innovation in intensive longitudinal research. The CCP, housed within the Department of Neurosciences in the School of Medicine, is an internationally leading research center specializing in Experience Sampling Methodology (ESM) in mental health research. Under the leadership of Prof. Inez Myin-Germeys, the CCP brings together a vibrant group of 25 researchers from diverse backgrounds and is widely recognized for its expertise in designing, implementing, and analyzing experimental studies and clinical trials. A major advancement of the project is developing tailored interventions that combine EMIs with VR technology. As a PhD student, you will play a pivotal role in advancing statistical methodologies to optimize EMI design through MRTs, enhance EMI effectiveness by incorporating data from VR-based tasks, and develop rigorous measures to evaluate the clinical impact of the EMI-VR intervention framework.

This position is part of eMotion, a recently funded, large-scale research program aimed at creating new treatments for negative symptoms—among the most challenging aspects of psychiatric care. jobs.title: PhD in Process-Aware Information Systems for Circular Care Pathways
jobs.description_html:
Are you excited about designing digital innovations for sustainable healthcare and eager to support Dutch care organizations in reducing medication waste while ensuring safe and compliant care? Join us as a PhD candidate on the NWO project REMARK.

Information
Healthcare organizations are under increasing pressure to become more sustainable while continuing to deliver safe, high-quality, and compliant care. Circular care pathways offer opportunities to reduce waste and improve resource utilization, but they also introduce new challenges. Healthcare organizations need to track resources across organizational boundaries, ensure compliance with regulations and quality standards, and monitor increasingly complex processes involving multiple stakeholders.

Existing healthcare information systems provide only limited support for monitoring circular processes and demonstrating compliance throughout the care pathway. As healthcare systems transition from linear to circular models, new methods are needed to continuously monitor processes, detect deviations, assess compliance risks, and provide actionable insights to healthcare professionals and managers.

In this PhD project, you will investigate how process-aware information systems can support the monitoring and governance of circular care pathways. You will develop novel methods that use event data and healthcare process information to provide visibility into the execution of care pathways and identify opportunities for improving compliance, transparency, and sustainability. A central goal is to understand how organizations can continuously monitor circular healthcare processes and ensure that circular interventions remain safe and compliant with regulatory requirements.

You will become member of the Information Systems group within the Department of Industrial Engineering & Innovation Sciences at Eindhoven University of Technology. Your work is embedded in the NWO KIC funded REMARK project, in which a multidisciplinary consortium investigates how circular healthcare pathways can be designed and implemented in practice. For this project, you will collaborate with researchers from multiple universities, Dutch healthcare organizations and industry partners, giving you a unique opportunity to achieve both scientific and societal impact.

jobs.title: Promovendus 'Verbeterde diagnostiek en kennisdeling voor Multipele Systeem Atrofie'
jobs.description_html:
Functie
Multiple systeematrofie (MSA) is een zeldzame en ernstige hersenziekte die zich vaak uit met Parkinsonverschijnselen, maar meestal veel sneller verloopt dan de ziekte van Parkinson. Dit onderzoeksproject probeert in een tweetal samenhangende deelprojecten oplossingen te bieden voor twee problemen rondom de ziekte MSA. Ten eerste: de slechte verspreiding van (nieuwe) kennis omtrent MSA onder professionals; ten tweede: de lange tijd tot aan een diagnose die mensen met MSA ervaren.

Deelproject 1 ‘MSA-Kennisradar’
De meeste neurologen krijgen MSA maar weinig te zien. Daardoor bereiken nieuwe inzichten over het herkennen en vaststellen van MSA hen vaak niet of pas laat. Ook voor neurologen en wetenschappers die gespecialiseerd zijn in bewegingsstoornissen is het moeilijk om alle nieuwe wetenschappelijke informatie bij te houden. De hoeveelheid onderzoek naar MSA groeit snel en de kennis is verspreid over veel verschillende wetenschappelijke publicaties. Met kunstmatige intelligentie (AI) systemen gaan we in dit project op een verantwoorde en veilige manier kennisoverdracht en scholing ontwikkelen omtrent MSA. De kern van dit MSA-kennisradar project is het ontwikkelen van een doorlopend en grotendeels geautomatiseerd proces dat nieuwe wetenschappelijke kennis over MSA omzet in betrouwbare en praktisch bruikbare informatie voor neurologen en wetenschappers op het gebied van MSA.

Deelproject 2: ‘MAESTRO’
In het begin van de ziekte kunnen de klachten van MSA en Parkinson sterk op elkaar lijken. Daardoor is het vaak moeilijk om in een vroeg stadium met zekerheid vast te stellen om welke ziekte het gaat. Het onderscheid is heel belangrijk, omdat mensen met MSA meestal minder goed reageren op de medicijnen die bij Parkinson worden gebruikt. Deze medicijnen kunnen bij mensen met MSA bovendien bijwerkingen veroorzaken. Daarnaast is het zo dat met mensen met MSA hun diagnose vaak pas na vele jaren krijgen. Zij ervaren dit als een van de meest frustrerende aspecten van hun ziekte.

Het doel van de MAESTRO-studie is om biomarkers te vinden waarmee MSA al in een vroeg stadium zo betrouwbaar mogelijk kan worden vastgesteld. We onderzoeken of een combinatie van verschillende meetbare biomarkers hierbij kan helpen, zoals bijvoorbeeld biomarkers in hersenvocht of bloed, zichtbare afwijkingen op een MRI of oogbewegingsstoornissen. We onderzoeken mensen bij wie neurologen denken aan MSA, maar bij wie tijdens het eerste bezoek nog niet met zekerheid kan worden vastgesteld welke aandoening zij hebben. Juist bij deze mensen is in de dagelijkse praktijk behoefte aan aanvullende onderzoeken die de arts kunnen helpen om sneller tot een betrouwbare diagnose te komen. Tijdens het eerste onderzoek bezoek worden verschillende mogelijke biomarkers onderzocht. Daarna volgen we de deelnemers gedurende drie jaar, waarna de klinische diagnose wordt vastgesteld. In de MAESTRO studie onderzoeken we welke biomarkers deze klinische diagnose het beste voorspellen.

Het strekt tot aanbeveling als je naast jouw onderzoek als promovendus bereid bent om gemiddeld één dag in de week als trialarts te werken voor meerdere studies binnen het onderzoekteam. Je beoordeelt of patiënten veilig kunnen deelnemen aan onderzoek en verricht studie-specifieke medische handelingen. Het biedt dus een mooie gelegenheid om je klinische vaardigheden op peil te houden.

jobs.title: PhD position: Optical metasurfaces controlling quantum electron wavepackets
jobs.description_html:
Work Activities
In this project, you will study the fundamental interactions between high-energy electrons and extreme light fields in a scanning electron microscope (SEM). Gaining control over these interactions may lead to new forms of electron microscopy that exploit the quantum-mechanical nature of electron wavepackets. The project uses an emerging technique, photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM), in which electrons in a 1-ps-pulsed electron beam exchange energy with a strongly confined optical near field generated by intense laser pulses. This interaction changes the electrons' energy, which in turn modifies the electron wavepacket in space and time, creating, for example, attosecond electron pulse trains. You will develop specially designed non-local optical metasurfaces to control the interaction of the electrons with the strong light fields. Structured 2D dielectrics integrated with nanometer-thin transition-metal dichalcogenide layers, exhibiting strong optical resonances, will be designed to enhance and control the coupling in an ultrafast 1-30 keV SEM.

Your research will include:
  • PINEM and metasurface design (years 1): learn to operate the ultrafast SEM at AMOLF, study PINEM theory and modeling, and design and fabricate metasurfaces in the Amsterdam NanoCenter cleanroom.
  • PINEM-metasurface integration (year 2): measure the electron-light interaction of optimized metasurfaces and tailor electron wavepackets by design, including through two subsequent coherent PINEM interactions.
  • Coherence and entanglement (year 3-4): investigate correlations between electron energy loss and cathodoluminescence, and test a quantum-eraser geometry in which the which-path information is erased.

The project combines the ultrafast electron-light-matter interaction and cathodoluminescence expertise of Prof. Albert Polman (AMOLF) with metasurface design, fabrication and optical characterization expertise of Dr. Jorik van de Groep (University of Amsterdam). You will be based in the Photonic Materials group of Prof. Polman at AMOLF, with close interaction with the 2D Nanophotonics group of Dr. van de Groep at the University of Amsterdam.

Qualifications
We invite applications from highly motivated candidates with a strong background in physics and a keen interest in nanophotonics, quantum physics, nanofabrication and electron microscopy. We especially encourage individuals from underrepresented groups to apply. Prospective PhD candidates must hold an MSc degree in physics or equivalent qualification.

Work environment
Work environment The Photonic Materials group (www.erbium.nl), led by Prof. Albert Polman, studies light-matter interactions at the nanoscale. The group is composed of an international team of PhD students, postdocs and master students that work in a collaborative atmosphere with many social group activities. Every week we hold a group meeting and departmental colloquium and poster sessions. We also regularly organize an international group labtour.

AMOLF provides state-of-the-art ultrafast electron microscopy systems for time-, angle- and polarization-resolved cathodoluminescence spectroscopy and PINEM, and a shared cleanroom for nanofabrication and characterization (Amsterdam NanoCenter). We offer a highly collaborative and supportive environment, fostering strong connections both within the group and with our national and international partners. PhD students benefit from a variety of courses designed to enhance their research skills.

AMOLF is a part of NWO-I and initiates and performs leading fundamental research on the physics of complex forms of matter, and creates new functional materials, in partnership with academia and industry. The institute is located at Amsterdam Science Park and currently employs about 140 researchers and 80 support employees. www.amolf.nl The 2D Nanophotonics lab (https://vandegroeplab.com), led by Dr. Jorik van de Groep, studies nanophotonic metasurfaces that enable active control over light by harnessing the highly tunable optical properties of two-dimensional quantum materials. By combining resonant metallic and semiconductor nanostructures with exciton resonances in 2D semiconductors, we create dynamic metasurfaces that actively tune light emission, scattering, and absorption at the nanoscale. Our group is part of the Institute of Physics at the University of Amsterdam (https://iop.uva.nl) and works in a collaborative atmosphere with other researchers within the department and (inter)national collaborators.

Working conditions
  • The working atmosphere at the institute is largely determined by young, enthusiastic, mostly non-Dutch employees. Communication is informal and runs through short lines of communication.
  • The position is intended as full-time (40 hours / week, 12 months / year) appointment for the duration of four years. The planned start date is December 1, 2026. · The starting salary is 3.115 Euros gross per month and a range of employment benefits.
  • After successful completion of the PhD research a PhD degree will be granted at the University of Amsterdam.
  • Several courses are offered, specially developed for PhD-students.
  • AMOLF assists any new foreign PhD-student with housing and visa applications and compensates their transport costs and furnishing expenses.

More information?
For further information about the position, please contact Albert Polman: a.polman@amolf.nl and Jorik van de Groep: j.vandegroep@uva.nl

Application
You can respond to this vacancy online via the button below.

Online screening may be part of the selection.

Diversity code
AMOLF is highly committed to an inclusive and diverse work environment: we want to develop talent and creativity by bringing together people from different backgrounds and cultures. We recruit and select on the basis of competencies and talents. We strongly encourage anyone with the right qualifications to apply for the vacancy, regardless of age, gender, origin, sexual orientation or physical ability.

AMOLF has won the NNV Diversity Award 2022, which is awarded every two years by the Netherlands Physical Society for demonstrating the most successful implementation of equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI).

Commercial activities in response to this ad are not appreciated.

jobs.title: PhD in Early Modern Religious Debates. The use of AI in analysing sources
jobs.description_html:
In the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, in the Low Countries many public religious debates were organized between, for example, Calvinists and Mennonites, or Catholics and Lutherans. Their written reports constitute an underexplored treasure of information about the religious dynamics following the Reformation and the development of a public sphere.

A PhD position is available within the NWO-funded project “In Search of the Truth, in Search of Adherents”. This interdisciplinary project investigates early modern religious debates in the Dutch language.

As a PhD candidate, you will investigate early modern religious debates using digital humanities methods and tools. You will analyse how participants drew on classical and ecclesiastical traditions, examining how different religious groups appropriated and used these traditions to support their arguments and distinguish themselves from their opponents. In addition to conducting your own research, you will contribute to the preparation of a critical edition of early modern Dutch-language debates. You will also help develop and refine methods and tools for producing digital critical editions, making them more effective and widely applicable.

You will work closely with a second PhD candidate in the project, whose research focuses on the rhetorical and argumentative strategies employed by participants in religious debates and the role of these debates in the emergence of a public sphere. Together, the two PhD projects will offer complementary perspectives on the practices, intellectual traditions, and wider cultural significance of early modern religious debate. This position offers an opportunity to work at the intersection of digital humanities and religious history, combining historical research with the development and application of digital methods. A full description of the project is available upon request.

Duties and Responsibilities
  • Conduct independent research and write a PhD dissertation, as well as academic articles.
  • Contribute to knowledge exchange and public engagement activities.
  • Contribute to the preparation of a critical edition of early modern Dutch-language religious debates.
  • Help develop, refine, and improve methods and tools for producing digital critical editions.
  • Contribute to the activities of the research group, research section, and department.
  • Participate in relevant courses and training offered by the Graduate School and NOSTER.
