jobs.title: PhD: viral manipulation of caterpillar behaviour in a multidimensional context
jobs.description_html:
Many parasites, including viruses, manipulate the behaviour of host organisms to increase their own transmission, linking to the concept of the ‘extended phenotype’. Fascinating examples include behavioural manipulation of caterpillars by baculoviruses, with infected caterpillars expressing hyperactivity as well as climbing to elevated positions on plants just prior to death. These behavioural alterations have a crucial evolutionary benefit to the virus, enhancing its transmission. Until now, parasitic manipulation of host behaviour has been investigated as a bidirectional interaction between the manipulative parasite and the host.

While the possible influence of the host or parasite microbiome on host behavioural manipulation is starting to be recognized, the influence of the host’s resident virome has so far been ignored. The past decades, evidence has accumulated that insects harbour a wide range of covert virus infections that do not cause any signs of disease. In this project, you will study manipulative parasite-host interactions in a multidimensional context, by investigating how covert virus infections modulate crosstalk between manipulative baculoviruses and their caterpillar host.

You will start with analysing the phenotype of baculovirus-induced behavioural manipulation across several closely and more distantly related baculoviruses and lepidopteran hosts, and determine the impact of the insect’s virome on the manipulation. Next, you will investigate in detail the molecular mechanisms underlying the manipulation, especially focusing on changes induced in the lepidopteran central nervous system (CNS). You will specifically perform an in-depth analysis of viral CNS invasion and determine localisation of baculoviruses as well as covert virus infections.

Furthermore, you will validate putative mechanisms by functional analyses of candidate genes and proteins, using a range of techniques including RNAi and CRISPR/Cas9 technology. This research will aid in identifying how virus-induced manipulation has evolved across lepidopterans and identify commonalities and differences in underlying mechanisms, and will also reveal how the behavioural outcome of manipulation is dependent on the context of resident viruses present in the host.

This PhD project is part of a larger Vici project, funded by the Dutch Research Council (NWO). As such, you will closely collaborate with another PhD student and a postdoc in this project, working on related questions.

As a PhD candidate you will contribute to fundamental science in the context of insect virology. In addition, you will participate in cursory teaching of the chair group. You will be embedded in the Laboratory of Virology. In addition, you will collaborate with (inter)national colleagues from both in- and outside Wageningen University & Research.

Your duties and responsibilities include:
  • Designing and executing experiments with insects and viruses, measuring behavioural manipulation;
  • Investigating the molecular mechanisms underlying behavioural manipulation using dissections, transcriptome, proteome and small RNA profiling;
  • Studying virus invasion of the lepidopteran central nervous system, using GFP-labelled viruses, hybridisation techniques, antibody labelling and microscopy;
  • Teaching in courses and supervise BSc and MSc students;
  • Writing and presenting research at/in internationally renowned conferences/journals.

You will work here
You will work with in the Insect Virology group, as part of the NWO Vici project ‘Invisible influencers: How hidden virus infections shape insect life’ led by Dr. Vera Ros. The project is aimed at disentangling how the insect’s virome (i.e. the assemblage of viruses) impacts insect immune responses, fitness and behaviour, and thereby influences interactions with and effects of incoming virus infections.

The Insect Virology group is part of the chair group Laboratory of Virology, and research in Insect Virology focuses on multiple aspects of insect-virus interactions including mechanisms behind viral manipulation of insect behaviour, virus discovery, covert virus infections (i.e. infections without clear symptoms) in insects and the use of viruses for biological control of insect pests. You will be supervised by Dr. Vera Ros (WUR Laboratory of Virology) and Prof. Monique van Oers (chair of the WUR Laboratory of Virology). In addition, you will also be embedded in the PE&RC graduate school (Home | PE&RC), which will allow you to follow a wide variety of training courses and will provide support during your academic journey.

The Laboratory of Virology is part of the Plant Sciences Group of Wageningen University. It is located at the Wageningen Campus in the Radix building. We provide virology teaching at Wageningen University within BSc and MSc programs across various disciplines. The Virology chair group comprises around 35 members, including research/teaching staff, technicians, PhD candidates, postdocs and visiting researchers. Each year, an average of 25 BSc and MSc students undertake their final-year thesis research within Virology. The Virology group conducts fundamental research into plant viruses, insect viruses and arboviruses. Where possible, the knowledge generated is translated into applications aimed at improving food production and human and animal health.

jobs.title: PhD Insect Virology: impact of the insect’s virome on insect immunity & fitness
jobs.description_html:
Insects are exposed to a diverse range of infectious viruses throughout their lives. In recent years, advances in largescale sequencing technologies have accelerated virus discovery, revealing a rich and diverse resident assemblage of viruses or 'virome' in insects, including covert viral infections that appear asymptomatic. To date it is unclear how such a virome impacts insect life.

In this project you will investigate how the resident virome impacts insect immune responses and fitness and thereby influences interactions with and effects of incoming virus infections. First, you will define the virome in several lepidopteran species and determine how the virome impacts insect life history traits and responses to incoming infections. In a next step, you will study in detail vertical transmission of the virome and investigate how the virome affects transgenerational immune priming (TgIP), a process whereby incoming infections lead to immune protection against secondary infections in the next generation.

By integrating virome sequencing and experimental infections with -omics approaches, microscopy, and gene editing tools, you will reveal fundamental mechanisms of insect immunity and virus-induced TgIP and the impact of the virome thereon.

jobs.title: PhD Position in AI for Software Reuse and Agentic Development
jobs.description_html:
How can AI agents build on existing software instead of reinventing it? Join this collaboration between TU Delft and ING to research more reliable agentic software development.

Job description
Software intensive organizations rely on increasingly large and complex software ecosystems consisting of services, libraries, APIs, frameworks, documentation, and other shared engineering knowledge. Recent advances in generative AI and software engineering agents are changing how software is developed and how developers interact with these ecosystems. TU Delft is collaborating with ING to investigate how we can make enterprise software development more sustainable and reliable in this changing landscape.

We will develop new techniques and tools that help developers and AI agents make better use of existing software and developer knowledge. Our research will combine AI with software repository mining, program and architecture analysis, empirical software engineering, and studies with practitioners. The research will focus on real-world software engineering challenges at ING, while contributing scientific insights and open research results that can benefit the broader software engineering community.

Within this collaboration, we explore two main research directions:

Direction 1: Software Reuse in Enterprise Software Ecosystems

Large organizations invest substantially in reusable software assets. However, as a consequence similar functionality can be implemented independently across teams, increasing fragmentation and long-term maintenance costs. AI-assisted software development makes this challenge even more important: software engineering agents can rapidly generate new code, but may reproduce functionality that already exists elsewhere in an organization.

This direction investigates how software assets are discovered, consumed, adapted, and evolved across large software ecosystems. We will study where opportunities for reuse exist, how software can successfully be adapted across teams, how reusable assets evolve over time, and how developers and AI agents can be guided towards suitable existing software. Ultimately, we aim to develop intelligent techniques that help organizations maximize reuse while reducing unnecessary duplication and maintenance effort.

Direction 2: Reliable Agentic Software Development

AI software engineering agents can increasingly perform tasks such as implementing features, fixing bugs, testing, and refactoring software. Their success, however, depends not only on the underlying AI models, but also on the engineering context available to them. In enterprise environments, relevant knowledge is distributed across source code, documentation, architecture descriptions, requirements, APIs, development history, and organizational practices.

This direction investigates the engineering foundations required for reliable agentic software development. We will study what context agents need for different software engineering tasks, what makes specifications sufficiently complete and precise, how stale or incomplete context and software complexity affect agent performance, and how organizations can determine when tasks can be reliably delegated to AI agents. The goal is to develop techniques and safeguards that enable organizations to integrate increasingly autonomous software engineering agents while maintaining software quality and human oversight.

We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive research environment and encourage applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of their background or experience. We believe that diversity contributes to a more innovative and creative research community. If you do not meet some of the optional requirements listed, we encourage you to still apply and explain how your unique experience and skills can contribute to our research.

Job requirements
Required
  • Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, or a related field
  • Proficiency in the English language

Additional requirements:
  • Research focus, characterized by curiosity, data fluency, and critical thinking
  • Engineering mindset, including ability to create experimental prototypes and demonstrators
  • Team player, good listener, and ready to help

To thrive as a PhD candidate, it’s crucial to have a strong research mindset driven by curiosity and passion for your topic. Reflecting on your motivation for pursuing a PhD trajectory is essential, as this path involves unique challenges and uncertainties inherent to scientific exploration. Success requires dedication, adaptability, the ability to analyze complex problems, manage your time effectively, innovate and stay resilient under pressure. Combined with the ability and willingness to work independently and collaborate well, these qualities are indispensable for a fulfilling PhD journey. These experiences will build you as an independent researcher, expand your professional network, and pave the way for diverse career pave the way for diverse career paths, inside or outside academia.

TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Delft University of Technology is built on strong foundations. As creators of the world-famous Dutch waterworks and pioneers in biotech, TU Delft is a top international university combining science, engineering and design. It delivers world class results in education, research and innovation to address challenges in the areas of energy, climate, mobility, health and digital society. For generations, our engineers have proven to be entrepreneurial problem-solvers, both in business and in a social context.

At TU Delft we embrace diversity as one of our core values and we actively engage to be a university where you feel at home and can flourish. We value different perspectives and qualities. jobs.title: PhD-student Online/offline relaties van jongeren
jobs.description_html:
Jouw functie
Sociale media verbod, smartphones thuis of in de kluis en zorgen over schermgebruik: het online gedrag van jongeren is volop in het nieuws. Maar wat gebeurt er écht in hun digitale leefwereld? Hoe beïnvloeden online interacties de sociale relaties in de off- en online wereld, en hoe kunnen digitale ervaringen juist bijdragen aan positieve sociale relaties, mentaal welzijn en het floreren van jongeren? Heb jij interesse in deze vragen en wil je impact maken? Dan is deze promotieplek mogelijk iets voor jou!

In dit PhD-project binnen het sronger2gether-consortium onderzoek je hoe online en offline sociale relaties met elkaar verweven zijn. Daarbij onderzoek je op basis van bestaande wetenschappelijke kennis op welke manier de online leefwereld een positieve bijdrage kan leveren aan de sociale relaties en het floreren van jongeren. Samen met leerlingen in het beroepsonderwijs (vmbo & mbo) en het voortgezet speciaal onderwijs, hun docenten en andere professionals die voor jongeren belangrijk zijn voer je focusgroepen uit en ontwikkel en evalueer je - in co-creatie - interventies en bestaande aanpakken die docenten kunnen inzetten om positieve relaties tussen jongeren te bevorderen, o.a. gericht op hun online /offline leefwereld. Door nauw samen te werken met praktijkprofessionals en jongeren draag je bij aan de ontwikkeling van het CARES-model (Child & Adolescent Relationships & Ecological Support) én aan inzichten die direct toepasbaar zijn in de praktijk.

Over het S2G project
Als onderzoeker binnen Stronger2gether maak je deel uit van een transdisciplinaire onderzoeksgemeenschap. Deze gemeenschap werkt op het snijvlak van wetenschap en praktijk: 1) We onderzoeken mechanismen van sociale relaties en bouwen aan een overkoepelend raamwerk; 2) We (her)ontwikkelen, implementeren en evalueren interventies in samenwerking met jongeren en professionals; 3) We werken met jongeren als co-onderzoekers in Research & Development Communities (RDC’s), en; 4) We vertalen inzichten naar opleidingen, beleid en praktijk via onze Transdisciplinary Research & Development Communities (T-RDC’s).

Als promovendus binnen Stronger2gether krijg je de kans om:
  • samen te werken met jongeren als volwaardige partners in onderzoek;
  • deel te nemen aan intervisie, scholingen en methodetrainingen;
  • onderdeel uit te maken van een landelijk consortium waarin je leert van en met andere promovendi, onderzoekers en praktijkprofessionals;
  • bij te dragen aan duurzame professionalisering en curriculumontwikkeling;
  • impact te hebben in het leven van jongeren, ook de doelgroep die in onderzoek en beleid ondergerepresenteerd is (VMBO, MBO, VSO)

Meer informatie over Stronger2gether is hier te vinden.

  • Bijdragen aan een systematische review over online/offline sociale relaties

jobs.title: PhD Position: Turning Faecal Sludge into Clean Energy in Kenya and Ethiopa
jobs.description_html:
Are you passionate about developing a sustainable alternative for traditional biofuel? Do you want to contribute to the just energy transition in Africa? We are seeking a highly motivated PhD candidate to join an exciting transdisciplinary research program focused on upscaling Faecal Sludge Briquettes (FSB) production as a sustainable alternative to traditional biofuels funded by the Dutch Research Council (NWO), NRF-Kenya and MInT, Ethiopia. The PhD candidate is expected to work on the improvement of faecal sludge briquettes (FSB) as an alternative cooking fuel for wider FSB adoption and just energy transitions in Kenya & Ethiopia.

The widespread dependence on traditional biofuel such as firewood and charcoal for cooking in East African countries contribute significantly to deforestation, environmental degradation, biodiversity loss and adverse climate change impacts. Indoor air pollution caused by biofuel burning leads to severe health risks, particularly for women and children. Simultaneously, inadequate wastewater and faecal sludge management in many urban areas pose environmental and public health hazards. To address these interlinked challenges, faecal sludge briquettes (FSB) is seen as a sustainable alternative to traditional biofuels and by utilizing waste-to-energy innovations, FSB production promotes resource recovery, climate resilience, and the Water-Energy-Food (WEF) nexus. However, scaling up production and wider adoption of FSB require a deeper understanding of the enabling environments facilitated by technical improvements, economic viability, social and political acceptability, participatory infrastructure planning, supportive policy landscape and technological improvements.

Your Job
The PhD candidate will conduct a laboratory-intensive project investigating the development and optimization of FSB. The candidate will systematically characterize the physico-chemical and microbial properties of faecal sludge from different sanitation facilities, establishing a rigorous understanding of feedstock variability and pre-treatment requirements. Then, you will design and conduct laboratory experiments to identify optimal combinations of locally available binding materials that maximize the strength, calorific value and storage stability of the briquettes. Necessary tests will be conducted to determine the emission profile of the briquettes while improving the overall caloric value of the fuel.

jobs.title: PhD in Bioreactor-based preservation of human heart valves
jobs.description_html:
• Are you fascinated by the potential of maintaining heart valves outside of the human body?
  • Are you eager to contribute to better and sustainable healthcare at the interface of engineering and biology?
  • Are you passionate about inspiring and mentoring students and working in a high-end collaborative and interdisciplinary research environment?
  • Are you our next PhD candidate in bioreactor-based preservation of human heart valves?

Information
The Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) is seeking a highly talented, ambitious and passionate PhD candidate to investigate and further develop our model of heart valve preservation. We aim to develop a way to keep heart valves alive outside of the human body using dynamic bioreactors where the valves open and close as they do in the human body. As the successful candidate, your research with us will contribute to broader efforts to culture living cardiac tissues and to study their function and their response to immune cells and immune protective technology, closely aligned with our BIOSHIELD consortium funded by the Dutch Heart Foundation. Our group’s research concentrates on developing and improving heart valve replacements in young children born with congenital heart disease. The current valve replacement options available in clinical practice cannot adapt to the growing heart of a child and can elicit immune responses that destroy and calcify implanted valves. Therefore, these young patients require multiple invasive operations throughout their lives. We investigate how to develop a living valve that can grow with the heart and is safe from immune rejection. Alongside our advances in in-situ tissue engineering of heart valves, we investigate strategies for immune shielding and culture of living human donor heart valves as an alternative approach. An essential step in moving this approach forward is to maintain and preserve heart valves outside the human body. In this project, we will focus on extended culture and preservation of donor valves, unravelling valve homeostatic maintenance, and translating this knowledge into smart culture conditions and bioreactor designs with feedback options. This presents an exciting engineering challenge: designing systems that can reproduce the complex flow conditions, pressures, and mechanical stimuli experienced by heart valves in the human body. By combining mechanical design, fluid dynamics, and biomedical engineering, we aim to develop innovative bioreactor technologies.

You will generate unprecedented experimental data as a pioneer in the field to unravel the conditions for optimal ex vivo cardiovascular tissue preservation. Your investigations will build upon our track record on bioreactor design for tissue-engineered heart valves and in-house expertise with heart perfusion models to build a system that can maintain heart valves viable outside of the human body.

To that end, your research will include a selection of techniques including: i) flow-based bioreactor development, ii) sterile vessel and tissue culture, and iii) sophisticated tissue analysis including advanced microscopy. You are expected to write a doctoral thesis and publish your research results in scientific journals. A small part of your doctoral position will involve teaching in courses as well as the supervision of students at the bachelor’s and master’s levels offered by the group. Also, an educational and professional development program will be offered to you.

You will be embedded in a highly inspiring research environment, both socially and professionally, which facilitates access to high-end research facilities, as well as fosters interdisciplinary collaborations. You will be an integral member of the Soft Tissue Engineering and Mechanobiology (STEM) group of the Department Biomedical Engineering, and specifically operate at the interface of the teams led by Assistant Professor dr Marijn Peters (Translational Engineering for Pediatric Cardiovascular Regeneration) and Professor Carlijn Bouten (Cell-Matrix Interactions for Cardiovascular Regeneration) at the Department of Biomedical Engineering at TU/e. You will also work together with the team of Julie Legrand (Mechanical Engineering) and Assistant Professor Marcel Rutten (Cardiovascular Biomechanics) to build upon their work on Soft Robotics Systems, Biomechanical models, and Vascular Bioreactors.

Your project is aligned with our BIOSHIELD consortium of the Hartstichting: BIOengineering immune Shielded Heart valve Implants: Engineering Living Donor tissue by translating prenatal protection mechanisms from the womb to the heart. In this consortium, we work together with cardiothoracic surgery and transplantation immunology at the University Medical Center Utrecht and the Wilhelmina Children’s Hospital and the ETB-Bislife Multi Tissue Center. We stimulate and foster cross-institutional collaborations as part of the project.

jobs.title: PhD Position: Movement Ecology
jobs.description_html:
Climate change is affecting ecosystems, species, populations and individuals worldwide. This project will link unique long-term individual tracking data with remote sensing products and explore the dependence of waterfowl on small to intermediate water bodies throughout the year, focussing on the availability of freshwater as a key requirement for survival and reproduction.

Freshwater availability is a key determinant of life on earth, yet climate change is rapidly altering hydrological systems worldwide. Migratory waterbirds are particularly sensitive to these changes because they depend on water bodies at multiple sites along their flyway. While the role of waterbodies in shaping spring migration of waterbirds is relatively well understood, its importance during breeding, autumn migration and winter periods remains largely unexplored.

The aim of this project is to fill this gap and quantify how changes in freshwater availability influence movements throughout the annual cycle, identifying feedbacks between hydrological conditions and waterbird behaviour. The greater white-fronted goose (Anser albifrons), one of the most abundant goose species wintering in the Netherlands, will serve as a model species. The project builds on a unique long-term dataset comprising GPS tracks of more than 200 individuals collected since 2013 and which is continuously expanding.

The following research questions are central to this project:
  1. How do greater white-fronted geese adjust their movement decisions in relation to snow cover and freshwater availability in their Arctic summer ranges?
  2. Which water bodies do greater white-fronted geese use for resting during autumn migration and how is this influenced by water availability and breeding success?
  3. What is the effect of yearly temperature changes on freshwater roost availability and the movement of greater white-fronted geese during winter?

You will curate and analyse GPS tracking data, integrate them with remotely sensed environmental datasets, and develop statistical models to understand the ecological processes underlying the year-round movements of geese. You will also participate in BSc and MSc teaching activities. Your teaching load may be up to 10% of your working time.

jobs.title: PhD Position Sensing Viscosity with Ultrasound
jobs.description_html:
Develop innovative ultrasound technology to measure the viscosity of flowing fluids in real time. Work closely with the University of Twente and leading industry partners to advance more efficient industrial processes, reduce waste and enable more precise medical applications.

Job description
Many industrial and medical processes rely on accurate, continuous measurements of fluid properties, such as flow rate and viscosity. These measurements are essential in the production of food, medicines and semiconductor products, as well as in environmental monitoring and medical infusion systems for neonatal care. Reliable, real-time measurements provide immediate insight into processes, helping manufacturers maintain product quality, detect deviations and prevent waste caused by production errors. In this way, better fluid measurement contributes to more efficient manufacturing, improved healthcare and sustainable food production.

In this PhD project, you will develop innovative, modular and scalable flowmeters that measure both flow rate and viscosity using ultrasonic surface acoustic wave (SAW) sensing. Although SAW-based sensing principles are already known, the mechanisms behind viscosity measurements are not yet fully understood or commercially applied in ultrasonic flowmeters. Your research will help establish the principles needed for accurate, quantitative measurements.

You will work at TU Delft in close collaboration with the University of Twente and leading companies in flow sensing. Combining theoretical modelling with experimental research, you will investigate how ultrasonic waves interact with flowing fluids and translate your findings into new measurement strategies and sensor designs.

Your responsibilities
As a PhD-researcher you will:
  • Investigating ultrasonic sensing principles and the relationship between fluid flow, viscosity and surface acoustic waves.
  • Developing novel measurement strategies for quantitatively determining the viscosity of flowing fluids.
  • Building a model of the sensing principles and validating it through experiments.
  • Designing and developing an experimental platform for ultrasound-based sensing.
  • Characterising propagation losses, quality factors, wave travel speeds and resonance behaviour.
  • Identifying optimal excitation frequencies to improve measurement accuracy and signal-to-noise ratio.
  • Publishing your findings in peer-reviewed journals, presenting at international conferences and writing your PhD thesis.

jobs.title: PhD: How taste is encoded in the brain of caterpillars & butterflies
jobs.description_html:
Are you a highly motivated and curious PhD candidate, willing to bridge across the fields of neuroscience, ecology and evolutionary biology? Do you want to explore how butterflies and caterpillars use their taste system to recognize the plants they coevolved with? And have you ever wondered if a plant tastes the same to a caterpillar as it does to a butterfly? Then we, at Wageningen University & Research, have an exciting opportunity for you.

You would be leading a PhD study with the aim to decipher the neuronal code used by the taste system of specialist caterpillars and butterflies to recognize their host plant. Insect herbivores and plants are intertwined in an intimate coevolutionary arms race in which plants produce toxic defence compounds and insects in turn evolved detoxification mechanisms allowing them to feed on specific plants. In parallel to these feeding adaptations, insects also evolved specific detection mechanisms for those plants to which they have become adapted.

These detection mechanisms rely on the recognition of certain plant chemicals as sign stimuli and others as deterrent signals. However, how the brain integrates these positive and negative signals is not yet known. Moreover, butterflies and caterpillars of the same species do not always use the same chemical cues, leading to different preferences in the two life stages.

You will use the model system of the cabbage white butterflies, Pieris spp.. These insects lay their eggs almost exclusively on plants containing glucosinolates, toxic compounds to which these insects have specifically adapted. At the same time, most Pieris species avoid cardenolides, a distinct group of defensive chemicals in some Brassica plants. The exception to this rule are Pieris napi butterflies which readily oviposit on cardenolide containing plants, giving us the opportunity to compare the gustatory code both between closely related species and between life stages.

To unravel these different coding mechanisms we will use both intra- and extracellular electrophysiological recordings to measure responses to the different chemical and their combination in the butterfly and caterpillar brain. In addition, we will create mutant butterflies lacking the most relevant receptor genes using Crispr/Cas9 to investigate how the silencing of specific neuronal channels changes the encoding of the host plant in the brain. Combined, these results will provide a unique insight into the neuronal mechanisms underlying the coevolution of insect and plants, which is a major driving factor of biodiversity and has shaped many of today’s terrestrial (agro-) ecosystems.

As a PhD candidate, you will contribute to fundamental research in the context of insect-plant coevolution and sensory ecology. You will be embedded in a diverse group of international scientists and collaborate with colleagues from both in- and outside Wageningen University & Research.

Your duties and responsibilities include:
  • Establishing intra- and extracellular electrophysiological recordings from the insect suboesophageal ganglion;
  • Visualize neuronal networks in the insect brain, using confocal microscopy and computer reconstructions;
  • Generate and maintain transgenic insect lines;

You will work here

jobs.title: PhD: Worldwide Forest Carbon Uptake Under Climate Change and Disturbance
jobs.description_html:
Are you excited to unravel the rapid changes in the carbon balance in forests worldwide? Would the idea of using a supercomputer make you smile? Are you a team-player who gets things done? As PhD candidate “Worldwide Forest Carbon Uptake” you will combine atmospheric observations, Earth Observation products and numerical models to quantify how the global carbon sink in forests is changing at a time where society urgently relies on this sink to remove CO₂ from the air.

The ongoing changes are driven by forest management, biodiversity loss, fire, pests, and climate change. The carbon cycle impacts differ from one continent to the next, and one of the challenges is to quantify both direct and delayed impacts on time scales of decades to days using a wide variety of datasets. This includes atmospheric CO₂ observations from high-precision monitoring networks such as ICOS, but also Earth Observation (EO) data that gauge changes in forest biomass, or forest age structure, or ongoing disturbances such as fires. As PhD candidate you will integrate these into an existing prototype numerical modelling framework and add new data assimilation capacity for these large EO datasets where needed. The project aims to expand this capacity from the current European domain to the rest of the world.

You will have access to national and institutional high-performance computing facilities to develop and run large-scale carbon cycle simulations, and to analyse the resulting datasets. With these integrated forest carbon balances you will address questions like: How has forest carbon uptake changed globally over the past decades? Can atmospheric observations detect signatures of forest management and disturbance? Which Earth Observation products most improve regional carbon balance estimates? Ultimately, the outcomes of your work will be compared to national accounting methods for land-use and land-use change that inform countries’ efforts to enhance carbon storage in forests.

This position is part of EUFOR-G3W, a Horizon Europe project contributing to the WMO Global Greenhouse Gas Watch (G3W). EUFOR-G3W develops observation- and model-based products to quantify greenhouse-gas sources and sinks at global to national scales. You will have access to national and institutional high-performance computing facilities to run and develop large-scale carbon cycle simulations.

Your duties and responsibilities include:
  • To apply and enhance our prototype forest carbon balance numerical model to use more EO data and the more advanced data assimilation methods they require
  • To operate within the EUFOR-G3W project team and uphold collaboration and communication with (inter)national partners
  • To support the broader carbon cycle team in the development and publication of science with our 'CarbonTracker' family of greenhouse gas models and data products
  • To support science of our BSc/MSc students through co-supervision, mentoring, problem-solving, and technical training

You will work here
The Meteorology and Air Quality (MAQ) Group at Wageningen University aims to advance understanding of atmospheric processes and their interactions with the Earth’s surface to address scientific and societal challenges. The group focuses on six themes, all related to weather, climate, and atmospheric composition.

Research in the carbon cycle theme focuses on exchange of CO₂ and other greenhouse gases between land, ocean and the atmosphere on regional to global scales. You will work directly with the carbon cycle research team at Wageningen University led by Prof. Wouter Peters, Prof. Guido van der Werf, and dr. Ingrid Luijkx. Together with multiple postdocs and PhD students, we investigate greenhouse gas exchange worldwide, with a focus on the exchange of CO₂ through the well-known CarbonTracker data assimilation we maintain and develop. Atmosphere, biosphere, and fire modeling and observations are our core activities, often using data assimilation techniques to combine data streams.

Our group offers an open, social, diverse, collaborative, and stimulating environment that thrives on teamwork, while helping individuals grow in their scientific career.

You will work at the interface of atmospheric science, Earth Observation, ecosystem science and climate policy, contributing to one of Europe's flagship efforts to monitor greenhouse-gas sources and sinks. Close collaboration is foreseen with a 2nd PhD candidate working under Simon Besnard at the GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences in Potsdam, Germany. While GFZ focuses on translating Earth Observation data into forest carbon information, the WUR candidate focuses on integrated forest carbon balances using (atmospheric) modelling and data assimilation. The position thus offers direct collaboration with leading research groups in Wageningen and Potsdam, access to state-of-the-art modelling systems and observations, and opportunities to present your work internationally.

jobs.title: PhD Position Projection System for TE Imaging in Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM)
jobs.description_html:
PhD Position: High resolution Transmission Electron Imaging in Scanning Electron Microscopy

Job description
Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) is one of the most widely used imaging tools in nanoscience, materials research, semiconductor manufacturing, and the life sciences. Despite its wide applications and accessibility, the highest spatial resolution is still obtained through transmission electron (TE) imaging, which can only be done through a large, expensive, and highly specialized (Scanning) Transmission Electron Microscopes ((S)TEM). The aim of this project is to "democratize" this imaging technique by bringing transformative TE techniques, including electron diffraction, low-energy STEM, and phase-contrast imaging, to compact, affordable, and widely accessible SEM platforms. As a PhD candidate at TU Delft, you will work closely with our industrial partner Delmic, a world-leading company in correlative and multimodal microscopy, to develop a proof-of-concept transmission electron projection column based on miniaturized electron-optical components.

The ambition is to create a compact, cost-effective projection system that can be integrated into conventional SEMs, enabling high-resolution transmission imaging alongside complementary modalities such as light microscopy, cathodoluminescence, and focused ion beam processing. By combining the strengths of multiple imaging techniques within a single instrument, this technology has the potential to significantly expand the capabilities and accessibility of electron microscopy. Working at the intersection of electron optics, MEMS technology, microscopy instrumentation, and imaging physics, you will design, simulate, fabricate, and experimentally validate a novel MEMS-based transmission electron projection column integrated inside an SEM. The project combines theoretical modelling, numerical simulations, hardware development, precision engineering, and experimental validation, providing a unique opportunity to contribute to the development of next-generation electron microscopy instrumentation.

The four-year research programme is organized into three main phases. During the first phase, you will develop analytical and numerical models describing the electron optics of the projection column and optimize its performance through large-scale simulations. You will use commercial electron-optical simulation software but also develop custom Python-based modelling tools developed within the project. Your research will be supported by access to DelftBlue, TU Delft's state-of-the-art high-performance computing infrastructure, enabling computationally intensive simulations and optimization. In the second phase, you will work closely with our experienced technical staff to design and realize the electron-optical components. Depending on the final design, these components will be fabricated using advanced MEMS technology, high-precision machining, or a combination of both.

You will gain hands-on experience with state-of-the-art microfabrication and cleanroom facilities, while also contributing to the development of the associated electronics, vacuum hardware, and experimental instrumentation required for the prototype. The final phase focuses on assembling, testing, and validating the prototype inside an SEM. You will compare experimental measurements with numerical predictions to validate the physical models and further optimize the instrument design. Throughout the project, you will work closely with researchers at TU Delft and engineers at Delmic, with opportunities for regular interaction and knowledge exchange between academia and industry. As part of your PhD, you will publish your findings in leading international journals, present your work at major scientific conferences, and contribute to the supervision of BSc and MSc students through laboratory work, tutorials, and research projects.

You will join "the Gheidari Lab" part of the Microscopy Instrumentation and Techniques (MInT) Group within the Department of Imaging Physics at TU Delft.

Job requirements

Embracing the opportunity to work with leading industrial partners, you know how to collaborate and achieve meaningful results geared to the development of pragmatic applications. jobs.title: PhD position Participatory Data Governance for a Just Energy Transition
jobs.description_html:
We seek a participatory design researcher who can make questions of justice, data rights and shared stewardship concrete in the design and operation of energy data infrastructures.

Job Description
The Delft University of Technology is hiring a doctoral candidate on the subject of "Energy data sharing for city-level policy making using digital twins". The PhD position is a part of the FEDERATE NWO project.

Energy data can help communities, municipalities and grid operators make better decisions about the energy transition. Yet people and organisations who contribute data may have little insight into how it is used, limited influence over the terms of sharing, or no clear way to benefit from the resulting decisions. FEDERATE, aims developing ways to share data across energy systems and digital twins while addressing these questions of trust, power and justice.

We are looking for a PhD candidate to lead the research in Work Package 2: Participatory Data Governance for Equitable and Transparent Data-Sharing Processes of the FEDERATE project. You will work with residents, local organisations, municipalities, grid operators and technology partners to design and test governance arrangements that make data sharing understandable, negotiable and accountable. Your research will connect social and organisational design with the technical work on data-sharing interfaces, privacy, forgetting mechanisms and interoperable digital twins.

What you will do
You will investigate how energy data is currently collected, shared and used, and whose needs, efforts, risks and knowledge are recognised in those processes. Through interviews, data ethnography, stakeholder and power mapping, and participatory workshops, you will build an understanding of both personal energy data and wider energy system data.

Working with project partners and communities in Heiloo and Alkmaar, you will:
  • Develop a participatory data governance framework informed by Human-Data Interaction principles of legibility, agency and negotiability, and by Energy Data Justice.
  • Facilitate inclusive workshops with residents, businesses, public authorities and technical partners. You will use methods such as role play, serious games and scenario-based co-design to make competing interests and power differences discussable.
  • Co-design governance roles, decision processes, data access and control arrangements, and ways for people to question, contest or revise data-sharing terms.
  • Design and prototype social and digital interactions that help people understand data practices, join governance processes and exercise meaningful influence. This includes approaches for people who are digitally excluded or less often represented.
  • Explore fair incentives and ways for the value created through data sharing to flow back to those who contribute data, effort or local knowledge.
  • Develop an onboarding playbook and a practical governance and stewardship toolkit, then help test these arrangements in the project’s joint case study.
  • Translate findings into actionable governance requirements and data rights constraints for the project’s technical researchers, while learning from what their prototypes make possible in practice.
  • Publish your research in academic venues and share usable findings with project partners and participating communities.

jobs.title: PhD Candidate 'AI-Driven Handheld Ultrasound for Military Trauma Care'
jobs.description_html:
Job description
Do you want to develop artificial intelligence for medical imaging to improve care for injured military personnel?

Military trauma care takes place under challenging conditions. During military operations, medical resources may be limited, specialist expertise may not always be available, and evacuation to a hospital may take hours or even days. Under these circumstances, healthcare providers must be able to rapidly and reliably identify a patient’s injuries and determine the treatment required. Rapid diagnostics can be lifesaving.

Ultrasound offers significant opportunities in this regard. Portable ultrasound equipment enables healthcare providers to examine patients at the point of care, without relying on extensive diagnostic facilities. One important application is the Extended Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma (EFAST), which can be used to detect signs of internal bleeding and pneumothorax, among other conditions. However, performing and interpreting ultrasound examinations requires specific knowledge and experience, which may not be readily accessible in forward-deployed medical treatment facilities.

Can artificial intelligence make ultrasound more accessible and effective for military healthcare providers in operational environments?

This is the central challenge of this PhD research project. Ultrasound offers valuable opportunities for rapid, portable diagnostics in military trauma care, particularly in forward-deployed settings where access to advanced diagnostic equipment and specialised expertise may be limited.

You will investigate how artificial intelligence can support military healthcare providers in acquiring and interpreting ultrasound images. The research will start by exploring existing AI-assisted ultrasound technologies, identifying unmet operational needs and determining where further technological development could provide the greatest benefit to military healthcare.

Applications such as Extended Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma (EFAST), used to identify potentially life-threatening injuries, provide a relevant starting point. However, the research will also explore other promising applications of ultrasound and AI across military trauma care.

Beyond developing and evaluating AI algorithms, the project will investigate how these technologies can be effectively integrated into military medical practice, taking into account the capabilities of healthcare providers and the specific challenges of operational environments.

Although military healthcare is the primary focus, the resulting knowledge and technologies may also benefit civilian emergency care, including ambulance services and emergency departments.

jobs.title: PhD in Synthesis of Sustainable PFAS-Free Polymers for High-Performance Applications
jobs.description_html:
Fluorinated polymers and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widely used in high-performance applications because of their exceptional thermal stability, chemical resistance and low surface energy. These properties make them essential in demanding applications, including automotive and aerospace components, sealing systems, and chemical processing equipment. However, growing environmental concerns and increasing regulatory pressure, particularly in Europe, are driving the need to replace PFAS with safer and more sustainable alternatives. Developing innovative PFAS-free materials that combine environmental sustainability with outstanding performance under demanding operating conditions represents an important scientific and technological challenge.

Research challenge
In this project, the research challenge will be to design, synthesize, and characterize novel fluorine-free thermoplastic materials that combine the outstanding surface and bulk properties of fluorinated polymers. The project will explore how molecular architecture and surface segregation can be used to achieve low surface energy while maintaining high thermal stability, chemical resistance, and robust thermomechanical properties. By combining molecular design with surface thermodynamics, the research will establish fundamental structure–property relationships linking polymer architecture and interfacial organization to macroscopic material performance. The research activities will involve the synthesis of novel polymer architectures and their comprehensive characterization using chemical, structural, thermal, rheological, and mechanical techniques, complemented by the investigation of surface and interfacial properties. The ultimate goal is to establish rational design principles for sustainable, high-performance thermoplastics suitable for demanding industrial applications, including sealing systems and high-durability components.

An interdisciplinary and international environment
The PhD research will be carried out under the supervision of Prof. Željko Tomović and Dr. Catarina Esteves in the Department of Chemical Engineering and Chemistry at Eindhoven University of Technology. You will join the Polymer Performance Materials research group, which focuses on sustainable polymer chemistry. You will also become part of the interdisciplinary Institute for Complex Molecular Systems, which connects TU/e researchers working across polymer science and related fields.

The PhD project will be carried out within the HARFF project, funded by the Dutch Polymer Institute (DPI), which promotes research collaboration between industry and leading universities across Europe. The industrial partners involved in this project are Envalior, SKF, Teijin Aramid, and SABIC Specialties. Through this collaborative network, you will develop new skills, build valuable academic and industrial connections, and explore how your research can contribute to developing future sustainable technologies.

Working at TU/e
At TU/e, you will work in an environment that combines scientific curiosity with a hands-on mentality. You will receive personal guidance while having room to develop your own ideas, ambitions, and talents. Together with supportive colleagues from different disciplines and backgrounds, you will push the boundaries of sustainable polymer chemistry and contribute to research with clear societal relevance.

Ideal start date: January 01 2027

jobs.title: PhD in Fair Distributed Optimization and Control of Large-Scale Networked Systems
jobs.description_html:
Can thousands of autonomous agents, each with only local information, reach decisions that are optimal, stable and provably fair? In this PhD you will build the distributed optimization and control theory that answers this question. You will design scalable multi-agent algorithms with fairness built in, handle uncertainty with stochastic and robust methods, and prove convergence, stability and fairness guarantees. Your testbed will be one of the largest and most demanding networked systems there is: the electricity distribution grid, where thousands of solar panels, heat pumps and electric vehicles compete for limited network capacity. If you enjoy turning hard real-world problems into elegant mathematics, this position is for you.

Note to applicants: No background in energy systems is required; you will pick up the domain knowledge during the project, together with our energy experts. We are looking for candidates with a strong background in control systems, optimization or applied mathematics.

Information
At its core, this project tackles a fundamental problem in networked control: how to allocate a scarce shared resource among many agents in a way that is efficient, scalable and fair, using only local computation and limited communication. The motivating application is congestion management in electricity distribution networks. As rooftop photovoltaics, heat pumps and electric vehicles spread, local networks increasingly hit their capacity limits, and operators must decide how much power each prosumer may inject or consume. The core idea is to embed clear and interpretable notions of fairness directly into distributed control and optimization algorithms, as constraints or objectives with provable guarantees.

The project advances fundamental science at the intersection of distributed optimization, control theory, multi-agent systems and machine learning. It seeks to redefine how societal objectives such as fairness are formalized mathematically and enforced in intelligent control systems.

You will be embedded in the Control Systems group at TU/e, contributing to its research program on intelligent and responsible control of networked systems.

You will work closely with experts in distributed control, responsible AI and power systems across departments, who provide the domain knowledge and real-world data to test your methods.

Beyond the theory, your algorithms will help distribution system operators manage congestion transparently and equitably, speeding up the integration of renewable energy and strengthening public trust in the energy transition.

As a PhD candidate, you will:
  • Formulate fair resource allocation problems: Cast congestion management as a large-scale, constrained multi-agent optimization problem, and formalize interpretable fairness notions (e.g., proportional, max-min or probabilistic fairness) as mathematical constraints or objectives.
  • Design distributed optimization algorithms: Develop and analyze consensus-based, primal-dual, ADMM-type and game-theoretic algorithms that coordinate thousands of agents using only local information and limited communication.
  • Develop fairness-aware feedback controllers: Design distributed controllers (e.g., distributed MPC, online feedback optimization) that enforce fairness while guaranteeing scalability, stability and constraint satisfaction.
  • Analyze probabilistic allocation policies: Study randomized and weighted allocation schemes, such as raffle-based curtailment, and characterize their fairness and efficiency over time.
  • Handle uncertainty: Incorporate stochastic models of generation and demand using tools from stochastic, robust and learning-based control.
  • Prove theoretical guarantees: Establish convergence, stability, robustness and fairness guarantees, including under forecasting errors, model mismatch and communication delays.
  • Validate on realistic large-scale networks: Test your algorithms in simulations of realistic distribution networks and on real-world data from Dutch distribution system operators.
  • Publish and collaborate: Publish in leading control and optimization venues (e.g., IEEE TAC, Automatica, CDC) and work with colleagues in control, AI and electrical engineering.

This PhD position is part of the project "Responsible AI for Fair and Efficient Control of Energy Systems (RAICES)“ (https://www.tue.nl/en/research/institutes/eindhoven-artificial-intelligence-systems-institute/ai-research/eaisi-emdair-program)

jobs.title: PhD Candidate on Responsible AI for Online Safety (1.0 FTE)
jobs.description_html:
Artificial intelligence, and generative AI in particular, is reshaping digital ecosystems and the way people access information, make decisions, and stay safe, creating new opportunities and new risks for society. This PhD project sits at the intersection of AI, cybersecurity, and computational social science, and focuses on responsible AI, developing trustworthy and accountable methods that remain reliable when people or AI systems actively try to manipulate them. You will contribute to this area through methodological and empirical research, collaborating with colleagues at LIACS and international partners. Potential research topics include, but are not limited to, modeling and detecting AI-driven manipulation such as coordinated influence campaigns and social bots, building early warning systems for online harms such as fraud and scams, and studying how humans and AI systems can jointly recognize and counter manipulation.

What you will do
The PhD student will be embedded in the System and security cluster at the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science, supervised by Dr. Valerio La Gatta and Dr. Olga Gadyastkaya from the Leiden Organizational Cyber Security Group. The successful candidate will conduct original research on responsible AI methods for online safety, publish and present scientific articles at leading venues in AI, computational social science, and cybersecurity, contribute to educational activities as a (head) teaching assistant and finally write a PhD thesis detailing the outcome of the research activities.

Where you will work
The Faculty of Science is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription and bicycle scheme;

jobs.title: Promovendus Strafrecht en Criminologie (1,0 fte)
jobs.description_html:
Bij het Instituut voor Strafrecht en Criminologie is per 1 februari 2027 een vacature voor de functie van promovendus die promotieonderzoek verricht naar financiële kwetsbaarheid en strafrechtelijke boetes in Nederland.

Dit ga je doen
Als promovendus zal je zowel sociaalwetenschappelijk als juridisch onderzoek uitvoeren naar de rol van financiële kwetsbaarheid bij strafrechtelijke boetes in Nederland. Jaarlijks worden in Nederland tienduizenden strafrechtelijke geldboetes opgelegd maar inzicht in de manier waarop financiële kwetsbaarheid een rol speelt bij de boeteoplegging is schaars. Aan de hand van zowel juridisch als sociaalwetenschappelijk onderzoek wordt binnen dit PhD-project de rol van financiële kwetsbaarheid onderzocht bij de oplegging en tenuitvoerlegging van geldboetes, onderzocht wat de effecten van geldboetes zijn en nagegaan hoe dit zich verhoudt tot juridische uitgangspunten en beginselen.

Het promotieonderzoek wordt verricht binnen het Instituut voor Strafrecht en Criminologie. Het onderzoek zal worden verricht onder begeleiding van prof. mr. L.A. (Marloes) van Noorloos (strafrecht), dr. R.M. (Rosa) Koenraadt (criminologie) en prof. Mr. S. (Sigrid) van Wingerden (criminologie). Het onderzoek mondt aan het eind van de aanstellingsperiode uit in een dissertatie. Het gaat om een fulltime functie als PhD-kandidaat (38 uur per week) voor de periode van vier jaar.

Naast inhoudelijke onderzoekstaken zul je ook onderwijs verzorgen, word je betrokken bij de organisatie van wetenschappelijke activiteiten en neem je deel aan het opleidingstraject voor promovendi.

Jouw werkzaamheden:
  • Uitvoeren van sociaalwetenschappelijk en juridisch onderzoek naar financiële kwetsbaarheid en boetes, onder andere door middel van interviews, statistische analyses via R en analyse van rechtspraak.
  • Je neemt deel aan het opleidingstraject voor promovendi van de Faculteit der Rechtsgeleerdheid.
  • Ongeveer 10% van de tijd verzorg je onderwijs op het gebied van de criminologie of straf(proces)recht en verricht je ondersteunende taken binnen het onderzoeksprogramma Criminal Justice: Maatschappelijk effectieve strafrechtspleging;
  • Je neemt deel aan en draagt bij aan de organisatie van wetenschappelijke activiteiten die door het Instituut voor Strafrecht en Criminologie worden georganiseerd (lezingen, conferenties, symposia);

Het promotietraject zal begin 2027 van start gaan.

Hier ga je werken
De Faculteit der Rechtsgeleerdheid is gevestigd in Leiden en Den Haag en is met ruim 7000 studenten en ongeveer 600 medewerkers een van de grootste faculteiten van Nederland. De faculteit richt zich op innovatief multidisciplinair onderzoek en een steeds vernieuwend onderwijsaanbod aan de hand van maatschappelijke vraagstukken. Onze faculteit is groot genoeg om nationaal en internationaal het verschil te maken en klein genoeg om persoonlijk onderwijs te bieden. Zo leveren we dagelijks een bijdrage aan een veilige en duurzame wereld. Impact met recht! Zie voor meer informatie https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/rechtsgeleerdheid.

Je gaat werken bij zowel de Afdeling Criminologie als Straf- en strafprocesrecht, die samen het Instituut voor Strafrecht & Criminologie in Leiden vormen. Bij de afdeling Criminologie werken ongeveer 50 medewerkers en bij de afdeling Straf- en strafprocesrecht ongeveer 20 medewerkers, waarvan de meesten onderzoek verrichten en met elkaar onderwijs verzorgen in de bachelor- en masteropleidingen Criminologie, Rechtsgeleerdheid en Strafrecht. Het (inter)nationale onderzoek is voor een belangrijk deel ingebed in het facultaire onderzoeksprogramma Criminal Justice: Maatschappelijk effectieve strafrechtspleging: zie

https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/onderzoek/onderzoeksprojecten/rechtsgeleerdheid/criminal-justice-legitimacy-accountability-and-effectivity .

Dit breng je mee
  • Je hebt een afgeronde masteropleiding Criminologie, Sociologie, Psychologie, Sociale Wetenschappen of gerelateerde opleidingen, in combinatie met een afgeronde juridische opleiding, bij voorkeur met specialisatie Strafrecht.
  • Aantoonbare belangstelling en vaardigheden voor het verrichten van wetenschappelijk onderzoek, bij voorkeur blijkend uit een goede afstudeerscriptie, papers en/of publicaties;
  • Je hebt affiniteit met en aantoonbare kwalitatieve en geavanceerde kwantitatieve onderzoeksvaardigheden en bij voorkeur reeds ervaring met het interviewen en analyseren van kwalitatieve onderzoeksgegevens (bijv. in Atlas.ti) en het werken met statistische software (bijv. SPSS/Stata/R).
  • Sterke analytische vaardigheden;
  • Uitstekende beheersing van de Nederlandse en Engelse taal in woord en geschrift;
  • Je kunt goed samenwerken in teamverband, maar bent ook in staat om zelfstandig je weg te vinden binnen en buiten onze organisatie;

Dit bieden we je
We streven ernaar om met elkaar een transparante, inclusieve werkomgeving te creëren, waarin iedereen zich welkom en gewaardeerd voelt. Onze organisatie is volop in beweging en met jouw ideeën voor verbetering en vernieuwing komen we verder. We besteden graag met jou aandacht aan je persoonlijke ontwikkeling.

Je kunt rekenen op een leuke maatschappelijk relevante baan binnen de wereld van onderwijs en onderzoek. De uitdagende en internationale werkomgeving van de universiteit bevindt zich op een steenworp afstand van de levendige Leidse binnenstad of in het bruisende stadscentrum in Den Haag. Ook hebben we – samen met jou – aandacht voor gezondheid en vitaliteit. Vanuit Healthy University organiseren we leuke activiteiten die hieraan bijdragen.

Daarnaast bieden we je:
  • Aanstelling als promovendus conform de cao Nederlandse Universiteiten. In eerste instantie krijg je een dienstverband van een jaar. Daarna kan het dienstverband met drie jaar verlengd worden; met het oog op die verlenging vindt aan het einde van het eerste jaar een evaluatie plaats waarin gekeken wordt naar de promovendi-opleiding, naar de haalbaarheid van het proefschrift, en naar de progressie in didactische kwaliteiten;
  • Een salaris tussen €3204 - €4051,- bruto per maand bij een fulltime (38 uur) aanstelling (Promovendus);
  • Daarnaast kent de Universiteit Leiden goede arbeidsvoorwaarden. Zo is er sprake van een eindejaarsuitkering (8,3%), vakantietoeslag (8%), uitstekende opleidingsfaciliteiten, betaald ouderschapsverlof en de mogelijkheid om via een keuzemodel arbeidsvoorwaarden op maat te kiezen;
  • Volledige vergoeding van reiskosten met OV voor woon-werkreizen.
  • Samenwerking in een enthousiast en professioneel team aan een gefinancierd onderzoeksproject met grote maatschappelijke relevantie;;
  • Veel vrijheid, flexibiliteit en verantwoordelijkheid: je krijgt alle ruimte om je talent verder te ontwikkelen;;
  • Deelname aan het opleidingsprogramma voor promovendi.

Meer informatie over arbeidsvoorwaarden lees je hier: https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/werken-bij/sollicitatieprocedure-en-arbeidsvoorwaarden

Dit vinden wij belangrijk
Het bevorderen van een inclusieve gemeenschap staat centraal in de waarden en visie van de Universiteit Leiden. We streven ernaar om een open gemeenschap te zijn waar alle studenten en medewerkers zich gewaardeerd en gerespecteerd voelen en zich volop kunnen ontplooien. Diversiteit in ervaringen en perspectieven verrijkt ons onderwijs en versterkt ons onderzoek. Een inclusieve academische omgeving waarin studenten en medewerkers hun ervaringen en opvattingen kunnen delen, zien we als essentieel voor de ontwikkeling van talenten.

Solliciteren of meer weten?
Solliciteren kan via ons sollicitatiesysteem. Sollicitaties voorzien van het vacaturenummer en vergezeld van een motivatiebrief en cv kunnen tot uiterlijk 3 december worden ingediend, gericht aan mw. S. Mattheus. De gesprekken zullen worden gevoerd op 8 en 9 december 2026.

Wil je eerst nog meer informatie over de inhoud van deze functie? Neem contact op met R.M. (Rosa) Koenraadt, r.m.koenraadt@law.leidenuniv.nl.

Om elkaar goed te leren kennen, volgen we een aantal stappen in de sollicitatieprocedure. Meer informatie lees je hier: https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/werken-bij/sollicitatieprocedure-en-arbeidsvoorwaarden
  • Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze vacature wordt niet op prijs gesteld. Mocht je ons toch cv’s toesturen dan kunnen daar geen rechten aan worden ontleend.

jobs.title: PhD Candidate: Museums, Collections and Society - Indigenous Heritage (1.0 FTE)
jobs.description_html:
PhD Candidate
The Department of Archaeological Heritage and Society, Faculty of Archaeology, Leiden University, is looking for a PhD Candidate in the field of Museums, Collections and Society - Indigenous Heritage to join a project funded by the Dutch Research Council (NWO) and carried out at the Faculty of Archaeology, Leiden University.

Project Description
The Faculty of Archaeology, Leiden University, seeks to appoint a full-time PhD candidate to carry out research in Museums, Collections and Society - Indigenous Heritage. The successful candidate will join the Department of Archaeological Heritage and Society of our Faculty. The research should lead you to obtain a PhD within a four-year timeframe (1.0 FTE).

The PhD candidate will be supervised by Prof. dr. M. Françozo (PI) and by Dr. L. Maciel at the Faculty of Archaeology, Leiden University. The PhD candidate’s research is part of the NWO-funded VICI grant: Making History in Indigenous South America (1500-2025): A Multi-Method Approach

The Making History project brings together scientific research and Indigenous knowledge on equal terms. It combines historical research, the study of museum collections, material culture analysis, and close collaboration with Tupinambá communities in Brazil and Mapuche communities in Chile. The project explores the impact of colonial encounters on these communities, while also highlighting their agency, resilience, and continuity over time.

This PhD position is part of the work package focusing on Mapuche histories. The PhD candidate will conduct their research under the supervision of the Principal Investigator (PI), working closely with other members of the research team and collaborating partners.

Key tasks
  • Develop and maintain collaborative relationships with Mapuche communities and research partners in Chile, taking Indigenous perspectives and research priorities as the starting point for the research.
  • Develop an inventory of Mapuche objects in European museum collections and collaboratively select those most relevant to the project.
  • Apply an interdisciplinary methodology combining historical research and material culture studies in collaboration with specialists and community partners.
  • Undertake research visits to museums and archives and conduct fieldwork (Europe and Chile).
  • Complete a PhD dissertation and publish research findings in international peer-reviewed journals.
  • Present research findings at international conferences, workshops, and other academic and public events.
  • Actively contribute to the Vici research team, including joint research activities, workshops, and the dissemination of project results to academic and non-academic audiences.
  • Actively participate in discussions and events at the faculty, department, and research group level;
  • Follow PhD courses based on an individual training and supervision plan.

Selection criteria
  • Master’s degree completed in Archaeology, Anthropology, or a related field;
  • Demonstrable ability and enthusiasm for collaborative research with Indigenous communities;
  • Experience with museum collections research;
  • Skills in material culture analysis are considered an advantage;
  • Very good knowledge of the Spanish language is essential. Knowledge of (or willingness to learn) Mapudungun is considered an advantage;
  • Knowledge about or lived experience in the South of Chile is considered an advantage;
  • Availability to live in the Netherlands, and willingness to travel and conduct fieldwork outside the Netherlands;
  • Demonstrable good time-management, organizational, and communication skills;
  • Ability to work both independently and as part of a team in an organized and results-oriented fashion.

Our faculty
The future of the past begins at Leiden University. The Faculty of Archaeology is internationally leading for its research, home to a broad array of specializations and notable for its strong connection between teaching and research. Home to over 500 students in the multidisciplinary world of Archaeology, the Faculty, and its researchers from all areas of the archaeological field, determine the future of archaeological research. What we offer

  • The salary is the standard offered to PhD researchers in the Netherlands in accordance with the Collective Labor Agreement for Dutch Universities (P scale: P0 to P3 = € 3204 - € 4051 gross per month).
  • Leiden University offers an attractive benefits package with additional holiday (8%) and end-of-year bonuses (8.3 %), training and career development and sabbatical leave. Candidates from outside the Netherlands may be eligible for a substantial tax break. More at https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions.
  • All our PhD students are embedded in the Graduate School of Archaeology. Our graduate school and Leiden University offer several PhD training courses at various levels.
  • If your work allows it, hybrid working is possible within the Netherlands;

Diversity

For other matters, please contact Human Resources HR@arch.leidenuniv.nl

More information about Leiden University can be found at https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en.

Apply

Applications must be submitted via SuccessFactors.
