jobs.title: PhD in Intelligent Gate Drivers for Silicon Carbide Power Semiconductors
jobs.description_html:
Can power converters become intelligent systems that monitor their own condition and adapt their operation? Join our ERC-funded project to bring real-time models and local intelligence close to power semiconductors -the heart of power electronics- and advance the energy transition.

Information
Renewable energy integration and the electrification of transport depend on efficient and reliable power electronic converters. Silicon carbide (SiC) semiconductors offer opportunities to improve their performance, but how can we also enable these converters to interpret their own behaviour and act on this information?

This PhD position is part of the ERC-funded project Power Electronics As Edge Computing Grid Components (PELCom), which aims to transform SiC-based power electronic converters into intelligent, data-processing systems. You will join the Electromechanics and Power Electronics (EPE) group within the Department of Electrical Engineering at Eindhoven University of Technology, under the supervision of Professor Dimosthenis Peftitsis.

Your research will focus on intelligent active gate drivers for SiC semiconductors: circuits that control power semiconductor switching while combining sensing, embedded processing and real-time models. You will investigate how electrical, thermal and reliability models can operate locally within these drivers to enable rapid, finely tuned switching adjustments and condition monitoring at semiconductor device level.

Your main research activities will include:
  • Developing electrical, thermal and reliability models and identifying the computational resources and processing platforms (e.g., FPGAs and DSPs) needed for real-time execution.
  • Designing an optimised network of onboard sensors and identifying the minimum set of measured quantities needed to fit the models.
  • Developing a wireless communication framework between the intelligent gate drivers and the converter’s central processor.
  • Designing, building and experimentally validating an intelligent active gate driver with embedded real-time models.

You will combine modelling, embedded implementation and experimental research, working with the PELCom team to connect device-level intelligence with converter-level functions. You will be part of a research group with several PhD students working on power electronics, offering opportunities to exchange ideas, share expertise and collaborate on related research challenges. Your work will contribute to more efficient and reliable power conversion technologies for a sustainable, increasingly electrified society.

jobs.title: Promovendus Politieke socialisatie en democratisch moreel vakmanschap
jobs.description_html:
Ben je geïnteresseerd in welke democratische en morele normen en waarden politieke ambtsdragers meekrijgen via training en opleiding? Ben je benieuwd hoe formele en informele processen van socialisatie binnen politieke partijen het democratisch moreel vakmanschap beïnvloeden? En wil je weten hoe de professionalisering van politieke ambtsdragers verder kan worden versterkt? Dan is het promotietraject ‘Politieke socialisatie en democratisch vakmanschap’ iets voor jou.

Jouw functie
Deze promotieplaats maakt deel uit van het project Democraft: een door de NWA-ORC gefinancierd samenwerkingsverband van maar liefst 4 universiteiten, 2 hogescholen en 27 maatschappelijke partners. Dit consortium onderzoekt hoe het democratisch moreel vakmanschap van politici kan worden versterkt: de kennis, vaardigheden, houding en praktijken die nodig zijn om het politieke ambt integer en volgens democratische en rechtsstatelijke normen uit te oefenen. Zulk democratisch moreel vakmanschap is cruciaal in tijden van crises en maatschappelijke transities. Ontwikkelingen zoals klimaatverandering, migratie, polarisatie en digitalisering zetten democratische instituties onder druk om snel én verantwoord te handelen. Politici staan daarbij voor complexe morele dilemma’s, waarin botsende waarden en belangen vragen om zorgvuldige afwegingen. Binnen Democraft onderzoeken we hoe politieke ambtsdragers met deze normatieve uitdagingen omgaan, hoe hun democratisch moreel vakmanschap beter kan worden ondersteund en hoe dat de institutionele veerkracht versterkt. Om die vragen te beantwoorden combineert het Democraft-consortium een interdisciplinaire mix van benaderingen (o.a. vanuit de politicologie, de bestuurskunde, de geschiedenis, communicatiewetenschap en het staats- en bestuursrecht).

In dit specifieke PhD-project onderzoek je hoe socialisatieprocessen bijdragen aan de ontwikkeling en internalisering van democratische en morele normen bij (aankomende) politieke ambtsdragers: hoe ontwikkelen politieke ambtsdragers de kennis, vaardigheden, houding en praktijken die nodig zijn om hun ambt integer en in overeenstemming met democratische normen uit te oefenen? Je richt je daarbij in het bijzonder op de rol van politieke partijen, beroepsverenigingen en opleidingen en trainingen voor politieke ambtsdragers. Wat wordt er in die context verstaan onder democratisch moreel vakmanschap? Welke waarden en normen worden er expliciet of impliciet overgedragen? Hoe wordt dat aangeleerd en getraind? Welke formele en informele processen spelen daarbij een rol?

Je onderzoekt onder meer trainings- en professionaliseringsprogramma’s voor politieke ambtsdragers. Je combineert daarbij literatuur- en documentstudie met interviews, focusgroepen en participerende observatie. Je werkt nauw samen met de beroeps- en belangenverenigingen en onderzoekt de randvoorwaarden voor effectieve training en opleiding van (aankomende) politieke ambtsdragers en andere vormen van politieke socialisatie. Het project resulteert in wetenschappelijke inzichten en concrete aanbevelingen voor de praktijk. Zo draagt je onderzoek bij aan beter begrip en versterking van het democratisch moreel vakmanschap van politieke ambtsdragers.

Je wordt begeleid door Niels Karsten (TiU), Leonie Heres (VU), Charlotte Wagenaar (VU) en Take Sipma (TiU) en werkt samen verschillende maatschappelijke partners, zoals de Nederlandse Vereniging voor Raadsleden, het Nederlands Genootschap van Burgemeesters, de Wethoudersvereniging en verschillende gemeenten.

Je proefschrift schrijf je bij de vakgroep Public Law & Governance (PLG), die onderdeel is van Tilburg Law School. Tegelijk maak je onderdeel uit van het Democraft-consortium. Democraft besteedt veel aandacht aan de ontwikkeling van promovendi en postdocs. Zo word je actief begeleid op het inter- en transdisciplinair samenwerken en netwerken buiten je eigen discipline en onderzoeksdomein. Ook organiseren we halfjaarlijkse workshops waar je met elkaar en met topwetenschappers uit het veld kunt sparren over je onderzoek, inspiratie kunt opdoen, en getraind wordt in vaardigheden die belangrijk zijn voor impactgericht onderzoek. En er is een mogelijkheid om naast je academische begeleidingsteam ook bij één van onze maatschappelijke partners een mentor te krijgen die je wegwijs maakt in de ambtelijke en/of politiek-bestuurlijke praktijk.

Als promovendus in dit project draag je uiteraard bij aan activiteiten van Democraft en van de vakgroep PLG, zoals bijvoorbeeld het participeren in, of organiseren van lezingen, workshops en/of seminarlunches. Daarnaast draag je bij aan het onderwijs van de vakgroep PLG in de Bachelor Bestuurskunde en/of de Master Public Governance & Strategy.  Concreet houdt dit alles in, het:

  • Uitvoeren van verschillende (empirische) deelstudies naar politieke socialisatie en democratisch moreel vakmanschap;
  • Schrijven van een Engelstalig interdisciplinair proefschrift, bij voorkeur op basis van artikelen;
  • Deelnemen aan programma’s van de Tilburg University Graduate Law School en de promovendi-opleiding van het Netherlands Institute of Governance (NIG);
  • Bijdragen aan het onderwijs in de Bachelor Bestuurskunde en/of de Master Public Governance & Strategy (0.1 FTE);
  • Samenwerken met collega-onderzoekers en maatschappelijke partners om het Democraft-consortium verder te versterken.

jobs.title: PhD Position: Prospective Environmental Assessment of Technological Innovations
jobs.description_html:
Would you like to help advance environmental sustainability in healthcare from the very first design step? As a PhD candidate at Radboud University, you will join the European Doctoral Network Implant-to-Market, an interdisciplinary collaboration between environmental scientists, clinicians, health economists and policy experts working towards sustainable innovation of medical devices across Europe.

Environmental impacts are still rarely considered in the design phase of medical devices, such as implants, although decisions at that stage largely determine their life cycle impact on human health and ecosystems. Robust methods are needed to assess the future impacts of medical devices under development.

Your research will focus on developing methods in Life Cycle Assessment to support Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD) medical devices. A particular focus will be on developing methods to estimate material, energy, chemical and water use of lab scale technologies, and to assess impacts that are relevant for this sector, such as toxicity and water use.

As a PhD candidate, you will develop, evaluate and apply innovative methods in prospective Life Cycle Assessment for medical devices. A particular focus will be on improving the scientific basis to assess prospective inventory data collection and quantifying the corresponding impacts on ecosystems and human health. You will investigate how robust estimates can be made to guide developers towards SSbD medical devices with advice from innovation to market introduction. In addition, together with developers, you will apply and evaluate these methods in real-world implant case studies. This will allow you to connect methodological innovation with real-world design and development, and contribute to more sustainable innovations.

Within the Implant-to-Market project, 15 doctoral candidates will be hired at institutes throughout Europe. A secondment of at least 3 months to a partner institute in another country is mandatory. You will also have the opportunity to further develop and improve your skill set by attending training courses organised within the project, and courses of the Graduate School of the Radboud Institute for Biological and Environmental Sciences and elsewhere. You will communicate your findings through publications in peer-reviewed journals; and part of your workload (10%) will consist of teaching activities at our institute, assisting staff members in their courses at the MSc level (in English) and supervising thesis research.

Would you like to learn more about what it’s like to pursue a PhD at Radboud University? Visit the page about working as a PhD candidate.

jobs.title: PhD: AI for early detection of cardiometabolic diseases using oral health data
jobs.description_html:
You develop and clinically validate innovative AI-based screening models integrating retrospective and prospective data from multiple sources. These models are applied in the context of oral and systemic health, with a particular focus on the early detection of cardiometabolic diseases (CMD). You also assess the usability of the models in clinical practice. Working within a multidisciplinary research team, you help translate advanced AI methods into clinically relevant applications. In addition to your research activities, you may contribute to ongoing educational activities within the department, including the supervision of bachelor's and master's theses.

About the project
Cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, oral cancer and osteoporosis remain among the most important public health challenges in Europe. Increasing evidence suggests that oral health and general health are closely connected, yet these links are not routinely used to support disease prevention and early detection.

The MYDIAG.AI project, funded by EU-Horizon, aims to address this gap by developing a generative AI-powered virtual assistant capable of analyzing multiple sources of health information, including electronic health records, clinical notes, intraoral photographs, and panoramic dental X-rays. The AI assistant will help healthcare professionals identify potential health risks, support clinical decision-making, and generate draft medical notes and referral letters. By bringing together expertise in dentistry, medicine, data science and AI, MYDIAG.AI seeks to strengthen collaboration between oral healthcare and general healthcare.

The Academic Center for Dentistry Amsterdam (ACTA) will focus on the development and validation of a multimodal AI-model, which will serve as a core component of the virtual assistant. ACTA will also contribute to the clinical validation and implementation of the virtual assistant in dental settings. Both retrospective and prospective observational data will be collected and used in the study.

jobs.title: Promovendus Agressie te Lijf+ voor volwassenen met een LVB
jobs.description_html:
Agressief gedrag komt vaak voor bij volwassenen met een licht verstandelijke beperking (LVB) en heeft impact op henzelf en omgeving. Begeleiding en psychomotorische therapie (PMT) wordt ingezet om agressie te verminderen. Agressie te Lijf+ (ATL+) is een vorm van PMT die helpt om lichamelijke signalen van angst en boosheid te herkennen en er beter mee om te gaan (coping), zodat agressie wordt voorkomen. Dit project heeft als doel om ATL+ te toetsen, om daarmee inzicht te krijgen in de mate waarin het volwassenen met een LVB helpt om minder vaak agressief te zijn en meer lichaamsbewustzijn, mogelijkheden voor coping en kwaliteit van leven te ervaren. Het onderzoek vindt plaats met deelnemers met agressief gedrag en een Wlz indicatie uit vijf instellingen, willekeurig verdeeld over twee groepen: ATL+ en begeleiding of alleen begeleiding. Hiertoe werkt je vanuit de Academische Werkplaats Viveon samen met de academische werkplaats Leven met een Verstandelijke Beperking in Tilburg, Hogeschool Windesheim in Zwolle, ’s Heeren Loo, Reinaerde, Prinsenstichting en de Nederlandse Vereniging voor Psychomotorische Therapie.

Wat ga je zoal doen
  • je voert een Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) uit naar de effectiviteit van Agressie te Lijf+ (ATL+)
  • je bent betrokken bij de voorbereiding, opzet en uitvoering van het onderzoek, waaronder het werven en includeren van deelnemers en coördineren van de dataverzameling
  • je verzamelt, verwerkt en analyseert onderzoeksgegevens en interpreteert de resultaten
  • je werkt nauw samen met de zorgorganisaties, psychomotorisch therapeuten, onderzoekers en andere betrokken professionals
  • je presenteert de onderzoeksresultaten op wetenschappelijke bijeenkomsten en congressen en schrijft wetenschappelijke artikelen die samen leiden tot je proefschrift
  • je draagt bij aan de vertaling van onderzoeksresultaten naar de praktijk, zodat de kennis over PMT en agressieregulatie verder wordt ontwikkeld en toegepast

jobs.title: PhD position Data-Driven Distribution Systems Planning with District Heating
jobs.description_html:
Job Description

The Delft University of Technology is hiring a doctoral candidate on the subject "Data-Driven Distribution Systems Planning with District Heating".

The decarbonization of the heating sector in the Netherlands is resulting in an increased adoption of district heating at the city scale. Depending on the type of district heating system and its interface with the electricity infrastructure, uncoordinated operation and poor planning may increase congestion at the medium-voltage level. In this PhD project, we will investigate how the electricity infrastructure can accommodate district heating networks by properly coordinating their future operation. To do this, we first investigate which data are needed (from distribution system operators, municipalities, users, etc.) to properly model future district heating demand and operations. We will also aim to understand what the barriers are to obtaining and using such data. As more data becomes available, we will investigate the role of artificial intelligence and machine learning models in facilitating coordinated planning, as well as how to incorporate risk and uncertainty. This PhD Position is part of the NWO Share the “Warmth Project: Data Sharing for Urban Heat Transition Planning”. The Sharing the Warmth Project aims to help Dutch cities move toward affordable, sustainable, and gas-free heating. The project brings citizens, municipalities, and grid operators together to share data in a safe and trustworthy way. By developing privacy-preserving tools and fair data-sharing arrangements, this project strengthens cooperation and informed decision-making. This enables municipalities to plan heating upgrades more efficiently and creates a fairer, more future-proof energy system for everyone.

This is a four-year doctoral appointment. You will be jointly supervised by Dr. Pedro P. Vergara (Associate Professor), Prof. Peter Palensky (Chair IEPG) and Dr. Ivo Potof (CEG Faculty). You will be a member of the section Intelligent Electrical Power Grids in the Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, and Computer Science. The project will offer opportunities to collaborate with industrial partners but also with academics from other disciplines, as required (mathematics, operations research). Within the team, we strive to develop methods that are mathematically rigorous and have near-term application potential. We are strong supporters of open science (publishing, source code, data). You will also be expected to assist in teaching activities (student supervision, labs) related to your subject area.

About the ESE Department

The research in the Department of Electrical Sustainable Energy is inspired by the technical, scientific, and societal challenges originating from the transition towards a more sustainable society and focuses on four areas:
  • DC Systems, Energy Conversion and Storage (DCE&S).
  • Photovoltaic Materials and Devices (PVMD).
  • High Voltage Technologies (HVT).
  • Intelligent Electrical Power Grids (IEPG).

The Electrical Sustainable Energy Department provides expertise in each of these areas throughout the entire energy system chain. The department owns a large ESP laboratory assembling High Voltage testing, DC Grids testing environment, and large RTDS that is actively used for real-time simulation of future electrical power systems, AC and DC protection and wide-area monitoring and protection.

The Intelligent Electrical Power Grid (IEPG) group, headed by Professor Peter Palensky, works on the future of our power system. The goal is to generate, transmit and use electrical energy in a highly reliable, efficient, stable, clean, affordable, and safe way. IEPG integrates new power technologies and smart controls, which interact with other systems and allow for more distributed and variable generation.

Job requirements
Essentials:
  • Basic knowledge of power systems and/or district heatings.
  • Basic knowledge of machine learning/AI is a plus.
  • Completed an MSc degree in a highly technical related discipline (computer science, electrical engineering, etc.) and ou were at the top of your class.
  • Excellent analytical skills and a solid basis in operational research (optimization).
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills in English proven by a minimum score of 100 in TOEFL or IELTS of 7.0 per sub-skill (writing, reading, listening, speaking). Candidates do not need to present the test results as part of their application. These results will be requested at a later stage during the selection procedure. For more information see https://www.tudelft.nl/onderwijs/opleidingen/phd/admission
  • You enjoy performing research. You are independent, self-motivated and eager to learn.
  • You are keen to work with partners to link real-world challenges to fundamental research questions.

Desirables:
  • Experience with optimization methods and scheduling problems as well as optimization packages such as Pyomo.
  • You enjoy programming and have experience with Python, machine learning, command-line tools, version control.

TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.

For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.

At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.

Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science
The Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science (EEMCS) brings together three scientific disciplines. Combined, they reinforce each other and are the driving force behind the technology we all use in our daily lives. Technology such as the electricity grid, which our faculty is helping to make completely sustainable and future-proof. At the same time, we are developing the chips and sensors of the future, whilst also setting the foundations for the software technologies to run on this new generation of equipment – which of course includes AI. Meanwhile we are pushing the limits of applied mathematics, for example mapping out disease processes using single cell data, and using mathematics to simulate gigantic ash plumes after a volcanic eruption. In other words: there is plenty of room at the faculty for ground-breaking research. We educate innovative engineers and have excellent labs and facilities that underline our strong international position. In total, more than 1000 employees and 4,000 students work and study in this innovative environment.

Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science.

Conditions of employment
Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met.

Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%.

As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills.

The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged.

Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands.

Additional information
If you would like more information about this vacancy or the selection procedure, please contact P. Vergara, Associate Professor.

For information about the selection procedure, please contact Carla Jager, Secretary, IEPG group.

Application procedure
Applications will be assessed on a rolling basis and suitable candidates will be invited for interview, so it is recommended not to wait until the deadline with your application.

Applications can be addressed to Dr. Pedro P. Vergara, before December 13, 2026. Please submit (1) your CV, (2) a list of grades of your qualifying degrees (BSc, MSc), and (3) a cover letter that details your motivation and fit to the job requirements. Incomplete applications will not be considered.

Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements.

Please note:
  • To protect your personal data, we only accept applications submitted via the ‘Apply’ button advertised under the vacancies on our website. Applications and additional information sent by email or through other channels, including unsolicited applications, will not be considered or responded to. This also applies to open applications.
  • As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security.
  • Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

jobs.title: PhD Candidates in Gravitational-Wave Astroparticle Physics (GRAPPA, University of Amsterdam)
jobs.description_html:
Are you interested in working at the interface of general relativity, gravitational wave astrophysics, and dark matter phenomenology?

Do you enjoy working in an interdisciplinary research setting and do you want to be active in a variety of educational programmes? The GRAPPA team is looking for one or more ambitious PhD positions.

Join Us!
You will join the GRAPPA centre of excellence for Gravitation and Astroparticle Physics at the University of Amsterdam, embedded in the Institute of Physics at Amsterdam Science Park. You will be part of an international team working on dark matter in strong‑gravity environments, in close contact with collaborators in the LISA community and beyond. Your mission is to advance the theory and computation needed to identify dark matter signatures in gravitational wave data.

This is what you will do
  • Carry out research on gravitational wave sources in dark matter or related astrophysical environments;
  • Present your work in group meetings and conferences; write and co‑author publications;
  • Contribute to education (exercise classes and BSc/MSc supervision) as customary at the Faculty of Science.

You will be based at GRAPPA — an internationally recognized hub in gravitation, astroparticle physics, and cosmology. GRAPPA hosts experts in gravitational waves, numerical relativity, multimessenger astrophysics and dark matter, and collaborates with LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA, LISA, and the Einstein Telescope communities.

What we ask of you
  • We are looking for highly motivated candidates who will have completed an MSc in Physics, Astronomy, or a closely related field by the start date;
  • have a solid grounding in General Relativity and/or gravitational wave astrophysics;
  • have experience in scientific programming (for example in Python or C++);
  • can communicate clearly in English;
  • enjoy working in a collaborative research environment.

It is a plus, not a requirement, if you are already familiar with cosmological or N‑body simulations, basic concepts in gravitational wave data analysis, or dark matter phenomenology.

This is what we offer you
We offer a temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The gross monthly salary, based on 38 hours per week ranges between € 3,204 to € 4,051 (Scale P). This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile PhD candidate is applicable. A favourable tax agreement, the ‘30% ruling’, may apply to non-Dutch applicants.

The preferred starting date is to be discussed. This employment should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students.

The Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands is applicable.

You will work in this team
The Faculty of Science has a student body of around 8,000, as well as 1,800 members of staff working in education, research or support services. Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, be it elementary particles, the birth of the universe or the functioning of the brain.

The Institute of Physics (IoP) of the University of Amsterdam is located in the centre of the Amsterdam Science Park. The IoP – as part of the Faculty of Science –is housed in a modern building with excellent labs and technical facilities. Surrounded by several national research institutes and with our partners at the Vrije Universiteit (VU) Amsterdam, the institute is part of a strong physics centre of international standing.

You will be based at GRAPPA — an internationally recognized hub in gravitation, astroparticle physics, and cosmology. GRAPPA hosts experts in gravitational waves, numerical relativity, multimessenger astrophysics and dark matter, and collaborates with LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA, LISA, and the Einstein Telescope communities.

GRAPPA was established as a research priority area of the university in 2010 and is part of the Anton Pannekoek Institute for Astronomy and the Institute of Physics and connects to Nikhef and Institute for Informatics. Over the last 15 years, GRAPPA has established an excellent track record in groundbreaking research and has produced many junior scientists who went on to successful careers. GRAPPA members have won high-profile awards including the Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics, the Shakti Duggal Prize and the Humboldt Research Award. GRAPPA members play key roles in the Einstein Telescope and CTAO, as well as in ongoing efforts including black hole imaging with the Event Horizon Telescope, neutrino detection with KM3NeT, gamma-ray observations with H.E.S.S., and gravitational wave observations with LIGO/VIRGO.

Do you want to know more about our organisation? Read more about working at the University of Amsterdam.

If you feel the profile fits you, and you are interested in the job, we look forward to receiving your application, exclusively through AcademicJobsOnline (AJO) at the following link: University of Amsterdam, GRAPPA, https://academicjobsonline.org/ajo/jobs/32885. Applications submitted by email or only through this UvA portal will not be considered.

AcademicJobsOnline accepts applications until and including 2 December 2026.

If you have any questions or do you require additional information? Please contact:
  • Prof. Gianfranco Bertone email address: g.bertone@uva.nl

What to submit on AJO:
  • a detailed CV including the start and finish months (not just years) when referring to your education and work experience;
  • a letter of motivation;
  • Research Statement
  • Two reference letters (to be uploaded directly by referees on AJO) .

The UvA attaches great importance to the contribution of female scientists in research and education.

A knowledge security check can be part of the selection procedure (for details: national knowledge security guidelines). Only complete applications received within the response period via AJO will be considered.

jobs.title: PhD position: ‘Action research into learning about knowledge in policy practice’
jobs.description_html:
The Athena Institute at VU University Amsterdam is seeking a PhD candidate for the research project Cocreating Research to Improve Science for Policy (CRISP), funded under the Dutch Research Agenda (NWA). The PhD candidate will conduct research within the subproject ‘Learning from and evaluating new knowledge-for-policy arrangements’.

The overarching project:

Research-based knowledge is an essential building block for effective policymaking. In practice, however, the systematic use of research evidence in policymaking cannot be taken for granted. The research project Cocreating Research to Improve Science for Policy (CRISP) aims to strengthen forms of collaboration between research and policy to foster more usable knowledge and more effective knowledge use. The CRISP consortium brings together several knowledge institutions and government ministries and will include eight PhD candidates and three postdoctoral researchers. The research will be conducted in co-creation with government ministries and other stakeholders and focuses on a set of current policy issues. For a description of the CRISP consortium and its subprojects, please see: www.scienceforpolicy.nl

Your research:
As a PhD candidate in this subproject, you will develop an approach to designing and monitoring (inter)departmental learning processes on knowledge in policy. You will support the work of policymakers who, together with academics and other stakeholders, experiment in so-called Policy Labs with new ways of constructing and utilising knowledge in their day-to-day policy work. Among the project aims is to assist in the development of cross-sectoral policy by integrating objectives and instruments for the general well-being of society (‘Brede Welvaart’) into domain specific policy. Key questions in this subproject are: How can we map learning in policy? How does monitoring experimental ‘knowledge work’ help improve the policies at issue? How can we embed lessons on integrated knowledge utilization from the Policy Labs into existing policy processes?

To answer these questions, you will conduct action research in various Policy Labs, facilitate a systematic comparison of their results, and empirically test how the insights from the CRISP project on policy-oriented learning and knowledge utilisation can be effectively shared in policy practice. The research will be carried out under the supervision of Dr Anne Loeber, Dr Kristiaan Kok and Dr Eva Kunseler.

Concretely, your tasks are:
  • developing the research proposal into a coherent and feasible PhD plan that aligns with the overarching CRISP project
  • collecting and analysing empirical data in support of the subproject ‘Learning from and evaluating new knowledge-for-policy arrangements’
  • co-creating research with partner from policy and science, by actively involving them in the research process and translating results into practice-oriented recommendations
  • completing an English-language doctoral dissertation within four years
  • publishing in international peer-reviewed journals and contributing to Open Access and professional publications
  • presenting research findings at national and international academic and practitioner-oriented conferences
  • actively participating in meetings and research activities organised by the Athena Institute, the subproject and the CRISP consortium
  • contributing to BSc and/or MSc teaching provided by the Athena Institute (up to 20 per cent of the appointment)

jobs.title: PhD position Societal entrepreneurship in equitable global health innovation
jobs.description_html:
The Athena Institute of Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam is looking for a motivated PhD candidate for the project ‘Navigating multiple accountabilities: societal entrepreneurship in equitable global health innovation’. In this position, you will study how organisations in global health innovation navigate competing accountabilities, and how these accountability relations can be reshaped to foster equity.

Creating an equitable and socially responsible global health innovation system is a widely shared ambition. It includes access to medicines, vaccines, diagnostics and medical devices, but also where R&D and manufacturing take place, who owns IP and data, and who captures value. Pharmaceutical and biotech companies, product development partnerships (PDPs), funders, universities and LMIC-based manufacturers present themselves as societal entrepreneurs committed to this ambition. Yet translating these ambitions into practice is far from straightforward. Everyday organisational decisions involve trade-offs between different expectations, responsibilities and values. Questions about research priorities, licensing arrangements, intellectual property, manufacturing strategies, partnerships and pricing become moments where broader societal ambitions are interpreted, negotiated and enacted. Organisations involved in global health innovation are accountable to multiple actors at the same time, including investors, funders, regulators, patients, civil society organisations and communities. These actors often have different expectations about what constitutes equitable and socially responsible innovation, what outcomes matter, and who should benefit from innovation processes and outcomes. As a result, organisations must continuously navigate competing demands and values in everyday decision-making. Navigating this web of accountabilities is a lived challenge for companies, PDPs, NGOs under funding pressure, and manufacturers and regulators in the Global South, and some of them are already experimenting with new arrangements.

Questions that you can focus on are: How do organisations navigate multiple and sometimes competing accountabilities? Which values, responsibilities and understandings of social responsibility and equity are prioritised, negotiated or marginalised in organisational decision-making? How are societal responsibilities reflected in licensing, IP and data-sharing terms, manufacturing location and portfolio decisions? Under which conditions do accountability mechanisms contribute to organisational learning and change, rather than compliance alone? And how can organisations and those to whom they are accountable jointly reshape accountability relations in practice, in ways that support more equitable and socially responsible global health innovation?

This is a transdisciplinary PhD project: knowledge is produced together with partner organisations directly experiencing these challenges in their daily work, from pharmaceutical companies and PDPs to NGOs, manufacturers and regulators, operating across high-, middle- and low-income countries. You will examine concrete decisions and practices, identify tensions between accountability demands, and explore and test changes in practices and arrangements, supported by reflexive monitoring in action. At least one case is anchored in the Global South. The project focuses on how organisations make and justify strategic decisions, not on evaluating health interventions or clinical outcomes.

The project draws on governance and accountability studies, organisational behaviour, responsible and societal entrepreneurship, and the literature on sustainability transformations. You will be supervised by a team consisting of dr. Lieselot Vandenbussche and dr. Kenneth Fernald (daily supervisors), prof. dr. Linda van de Burgwal, dr. Nora Engel and prof. dr. Barbara Regeer.

Your duties
The PhD project is organised in three work packages. In year 1 you map, together with the partners, which accountabilities organisations face and how these are reflected in index scores, agreements, portfolios and manufacturing and IP arrangements, and you jointly select concrete cases and shared learning questions. In years 2 and 3 you run living labs with two to three partner constellations, working through concrete decisions with reflexive monitoring. In year 4 you draw cross-case lessons on the conditions under which accountability mechanisms move organisations beyond compliance, and translate these with the partners into actionable approaches for their organisations and networks. Together with the supervision team, in the first year you will develop a research proposal in which you outline your own ideas and interests for the PhD research.

Concretely, your tasks are:
  • conducting research and collaboratively writing scientific articles that will form the basis of your PhD thesis
  • setting up and facilitating living labs and workshops with partner organisations and stakeholders, in the Netherlands and in the Global South
  • contributing to recommendations for policy and practice based on the research outcomes
  • presenting your work at conferences
  • following courses to develop your research skills (formal PhD training)
  • teaching working groups in the education programmes of the Athena Institute (max 0.2 fte)

jobs.title: PhD positie ‘Actieonderzoek naar leren over kennis in de beleidspraktijk’
jobs.description_html:
Het Athena Instituut van de Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam zoekt een promovendus (m/v) binnen het Cocreating Research to Improve Science for Policy (CRISP) project, gefinancierd in het kader van de Nationale Wetenschapsagenda (NWA). De promovendus zal onderzoek doen in het deelproject ‘Leren in en evalueren van nieuwe kennis-voor-beleid arrangementen.’

Het overkoepelende project
Kennis uit onderzoek vormt een belangrijke bouwsteen voor effectief beleid. De praktijk leert echter dat de systematische benutting van kennis uit onderzoek voor beleid niet vanzelfsprekend is. Het consortium ‘Cocreating Research to Improve Science for Policy’ (CRISP) wil door onderzoek bijdragen aan een verbeterde aansluiting tussen kennis en beleid. De verwachting is dat dit leidt tot beter bruikbare kennis en betere kennisbenutting. Daarmee kunnen complexe maatschappelijke opgaven beter worden begrepen, en effectiever en efficiënter aangepakt.

In het CRISP-consortium nemen verschillende kennisinstellingen en ministeries deel en zullen 8 promovendi en 3 postdocs onderzoek doen. Het onderzoek vindt plaats in co-creatie met ministeries en andere stakeholders en richt zich op actuele publieke vraagstukken. Voor een beschrijving van het CRISP-consortium en de deelprojecten: zie www.scienceforpolicy.nl

Het promotieonderzoek
Als promovendus in dit deelproject ontwikkel je een benadering om (inter)departementale leerprocessen vorm te geven rond kennis in beleid. Je ondersteunt en monitort het werk van beleidsmakers die samen met wetenschappers en andere actoren experimenteren in zogenaamde Policy Labs met nieuwe manieren van kennisproductie en kennisgebruik in hun dagelijks werk. Doel is onder meer om hen te assisteren bij het ontwikkelen van domeinoverstijgend beleid door doelen en instrumenten vanuit het perspectief van het algemeen welzijn in de samenleving (‘Brede Welvaart’) te integreren in specifieke beleidsdomeinen. Centrale vragen in dit deelproject zijn: Hoe kunnen we leren in beleid in kaart brengen? Hoe helpt monitoren van experimenteel ‘kenniswerk’ het beleid dat centraal staat te verbeteren? Hoe kunnen we lessen over integraal beleid en kennisgebruik uit de Policy Labs verankeren in bestaande beleidsprocessen?

Voor een antwoord op deze vragen voer je actieonderzoek uit in verschillende Policy Labs, maak je een systematische vergelijking van de resultaten mogelijk en toets je empirisch hoe de inzichten uit het CRISP-project over beleidsgericht leren en kennisbenutting effectief kunnen worden gedeeld in de beleidspraktijk. Het onderzoek wordt uitgevoerd onder begeleiding van dr. Anne Loeber, dr. Kristiaan Kok en dr. Eva Kunseler.

Concreet zijn jouw taken:
  • het uitwerken van het onderzoeksvoorstel tot een samenhangend en uitvoerbaar promotieplan, dat aansluit bij het overkoepelende CRISP-project
  • dataverzameling -en analyse in functie van het deelproject ‘Leren in en evalueren van nieuwe kennis-voor-beleid arrangementen’
  • het co-creëren van onderzoek met praktijkpartners, door hen actief te betrekken bij het onderzoeksproces en het vertalen van resultaten naar praktijkgerichte aanbevelingen
  • het binnen vier jaar afronden van een Engelstalig proefschrift
  • het publiceren in internationale peer-reviewed tijdschriften, bijdragen aan Open Access-publicaties en professionele publicaties
  • het presenteren van resultaten op nationale en internationale wetenschappelijke en praktijkgerichte conferenties
  • actieve deelname aan bijeenkomsten en onderzoeksactiviteiten van het Athena Instituut, het deelproject en het CRISP-consortium
  • het leveren van bijdragen aan BSc en/of MSc onderwijs dat verzorgd wordt door het Athena Instituut (max. 20% van de aanstelling)

jobs.title: PhD Position Understanding Incentives for Software Reuse
jobs.description_html:
Why do teams build new software rather than reuse existing solutions? Investigate how technology, incentives and organisational behaviour shape these choices in this PhD project.

Job description
Software reuse promises to reduce duplicated effort and help organisations develop technology at scale. Teams build data assets, software components, APIs and AI agents that other teams can adopt. Yet making these resources available does not necessarily mean they will be reused. What appears efficient for the organisation as a whole may create additional costs, dependencies or risks for individual teams.

This raises a research question that extends across organisations: under what conditions do teams choose to reuse existing solutions, and when do they build their own? Technical explanations, such as integration difficulties or poor documentation, may tell only part of the story. Performance targets, budget allocation, professional norms and regulatory requirements may also shape these decisions. Understanding how these factors interact is essential to explaining when reuse succeeds—and when developing a separate solution makes sense.

This PhD project investigates these questions through empirical research within a large international bank. A particular focus is how people become attached to their own solutions and their ideas of what “good” looks like—and how this shapes their willingness to adopt alternatives. You will use evidence from this setting to develop and test explanations relevant to the wider challenge of organising software reuse.

As a PhD researcher, you will conduct interdisciplinary research at the intersection of software engineering, economics and organisational behaviour. Your work will include:
  • Interviewing engineers, data scientists, product owners, architects and managers to understand how teams decide whether to build or reuse.
  • Analysing internal usage data to measure reuse and identify differences across teams, business units and types of software assets.
  • Examining how performance targets, ownership arrangements, budgets and regulatory requirements influence these decisions.
  • Comparing teams’ stated reasons with their observed behaviour to understand which explanations are supported by the evidence.
  • Developing proposals to improve reuse and evaluating selected interventions in practice.

The project draws on theories of incentives, transaction costs and the governance of shared resources. You will test existing assumptions and develop new explanations, including findings that challenge prevailing ideas about what enables effective reuse.

The research will be conducted in close collaboration with the partner bank. You will regularly spend time within the organisation and work with its experts. This collaboration provides an empirical setting for studying how technical and organisational factors interact across teams, business units and jurisdictions.

Your four-year PhD is part of a joint research programme between TU Delft and the partner bank. The programme brings together four PhD projects investigating incentives for reuse, resource orchestration, the evolution of software assets and reliable AI-assisted software development. Your findings will inform related work on improving support for reuse.

You will be supervised by Professor Michel van Eeten and Dr Yury Zhauniarovich at TU Delft’s Faculty of Technology, Policy and Management. Your project will be embedded in an interdisciplinary team of more than 20 researchers, bringing together computer science, social science and other disciplines. PhD researchers collaborate on research and publications, supported by daily scrum sessions, a weekly colloquium and monthly sprint planning. These activities sustain a culture of collaborative research and innovation.

Job requirements
We are looking for a candidate who is curious about how technical and organisational factors shape software development, and who enjoys testing explanations against empirical evidence.

You have:
  • A master’s degree either in a technical discpline (computer science, software engineering, information systems) or in a relevant social science, or in a closely related field.
  • An understanding of software development sufficient to discuss software components, APIs, dependencies and integration trade-offs with practitioners. You may have developed this understanding through education, research or professional experience.
  • Demonstrated experience conducting empirical research, for example through your master’s thesis. You have a solid grounding in quantitative methods, such as statistical analysis of observational data, or qualitative methods, such as interviewing and systematic qualitative analysis, and are willing to develop competence in both.
  • An interest in explaining organisational behaviour, including how incentives, governance arrangements and professional norms influence technical decisions.
  • The ability to work independently, critically assess evidence and collaborate with researchers and practitioners from different disciplines.
  • Strong English communication and writing skills, including the ability to conduct interviews and communicate research findings clearly. See PhD admission requirements: https://www.tudelft.nl/onderwijs/opleidingen/phd/admission.

Experience with programming for data analysis, research on software development teams, or working in a software-intensive organisation is an advantage. Prior experience in banking is not required.

TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.

For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.

At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.

Faculty Technology, Policy & Management
The Faculty of TPM provides an important contribution to solving complex technical-social issues, such as energy transition, mobility, digitalisation, water management and (cyber) security. TPM does this with its excellent education and research at the intersection of technology, society and policy. We combine insights from both engineering and social sciences as well as the humanities. TPM develops robust models and designs, is internationally oriented and has an extensive network of knowledge institutions, companies, social organisations and governments.

Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Technology, Policy and Management.

Conditions of employment
Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met.

Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%.

As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills.

The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged.

Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands.

Additional information
For more information about this vacancy, please contact Michel van Eeten (M.J.G.vanEeten@tudelft.nl) or Yury Zhauniarovich (Y.Zhauniarovich@tudelft.nl). For more information about the application procedure, please contact Martine van de Vorst, HR Advisor via recruitment-tbm@tudelft.nl.

Application procedure
Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 4 January 2027 via the application button and upload the following documents:
  • CV
  • Motivational letter

(No other documents). In your motivation letter, briefly describe an empirical research project you conducted, the methods you used and your own contribution. Explain how your background equips you to study both the technical and organisational dimensions of software reuse.

You can address your application to Michel van Eeten and Yury Zhauniarovich.

Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements.

Please note:
  • To protect your personal data, we only accept applications submitted via the ‘Apply’ button advertised under the vacancies on our website. Applications and additional information sent by email or through other channels, including unsolicited applications, will not be considered or responded to. This also applies to open applications.
  • As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security.
  • Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

jobs.title: Promovendus op het gebied van communicatie over onzekerheden bij forensische risico-inschattingen
jobs.description_html:
Ben je (bijna) afgestudeerd in de rechtsgeleerdheid, met een specialisatie in het strafrecht, de criminologie of forensische psychologie en wil je onderzoek doen op het snijvlak van het strafrecht en de forensische gedragskunde? Wij zoeken een promovendus die onderzoek wil doen naar de communicatie van onzekerheden rondom recidiverisico-inschattingen en de betekenis daarvan voor juridische besluitvorming. Het departement Criminal Law van Tilburg Law School biedt je, in samenwerking met het Nederlands Instituut voor Forensische Psychiatrie en Psychologie (NIFP), de mogelijkheid om vier jaar als onderzoeker (PhD) aan de slag te gaan met dit interdisciplinaire vraagstuk.

Jouw functie
Inschattingen van het recidiverisico spelen een belangrijke rol bij de onderbouwing van ingrijpende strafrechtelijke beslissingen, bijvoorbeeld over behandeling, toezicht en vrijheidsbeperking. Maar inschattingen van toekomstig delinquent gedrag zijn inherent onzeker. Juist vanwege de betekenis van deze inschattingen voor individuele beslissingen is het van belang dat ook relevante onzekerheden zorgvuldig worden gecommuniceerd, zoals de betrouwbaarheid van beschikbare informatie, de beperkingen van gebruikte instrumenten en toekomstige omstandigheden die het risico kunnen beïnvloeden. Het promotieonderzoek richt zich op de vraag hoe binnen de forensisch-psychiatrische en juridische praktijk kan worden omgegaan met de communicatie over onzekerheden in risico-inschattingen. Het project heeft een interdisciplinair karakter waarbij empirische en juridisch-normatieve onderzoeksmethoden worden gecombineerd. Met het onderzoek wordt beoogd aanknopingspunten te bieden voor een zorgvuldige communicatie en weging van risico en onzekerheid in strafrechtelijke beslissingen, mede vanuit een juridisch-normatief kader voor de vraag welke onzekerheidsinformatie daarbij relevant is.

Je wordt onderdeel van zowel het departement Criminal Law van Tilburg Law School (50%) als de afdeling Wetenschap en Opleidingen van het NIFP (50%). Je maakt deel uit van een interdisciplinair onderzoeksteam, draagt bij aan het onderwijs van de vakgroep Strafrecht en begeleidt in het kader van dataverzameling stagiairs die werkzaam zijn bij het NIFP. Het project zal worden uitgevoerd onder supervisie van prof.mr. J. (Joeri) Bemelmans (Tilburg University), prof.dr. Maaike Kempes (NIFP) en mr.dr. L.E. (Laura) van Oploo (Tilburg University; NIFP) en wordt mede mogelijk gemaakt door subsidie van Stichting Koningsheide.

jobs.title: PhD position: High-voltage power conversion for electric-propulsion spacecraft
jobs.description_html:
BESCAPE (Advanced Wide Bandgap-based Power Processing and Management for Future Space Exploration) is a Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network – Joint Doctorate (Grant Agreement 101312786). It trains 11 doctoral candidates in power conversion, control and electrical power distribution for future space exploration, together with European universities, ESA and leading space companies.

High-power spacecraft with electric propulsion need highly efficient battery discharge regulators (BDRs) that deliver a regulated 300 V secondary bus from a 48 V battery. Your research will find the best converter solutions for this, and prove them in hardware.

Your research activities:
  • Investigate isolated and non-isolated high step-up DC/DC converter topologies for 48 V to 300 V conversion.
  • Benchmark converter designs for efficiency, specific power, reliability and cost, including multi-objective optimisation.
  • Design, build and experimentally validate a hardware demonstrator against the project’s performance targets.
  • Perform several months secondments at ESA and at UMH, and take part in the network’s training events and conferences.

jobs.title: PhD position: Ultra-high-current power supplies for AI processors in satellites
jobs.description_html:
BESCAPE (Advanced Wide Bandgap-based Power Processing and Management for Future Space Exploration) is a Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network – Joint Doctorate (Grant Agreement 101312786). It trains 11 doctoral candidates in power conversion, control and electrical power distribution for future space exploration, together with European universities, ESA and leading space companies.

Future satellite AI processors need efficient conversion from 48 V distribution rails to about 1 V at currents of 100 A or more, under strict spacecraft mass, thermal and reliability constraints. Your research will push the limits of efficiency and power density for this extreme step-down ratio.

Your research activities:
  • Explore modular series/parallel, hybrid and multiphase converter architectures for high step-down ratios.
  • Investigate advanced magnetic structures and GaN semiconductor technology to maximise efficiency and gravimetric power density.
  • Develop digital-twin models and circuit design tools, and build a hardware demonstrator targeting 48 V to 1 V, 100 A and at least 92% efficiency under the specified conditions.
  • Perform several months secondments at Leonardo and at KU Leuven, and take part in the network’s training events and conferences.

jobs.title: PhD position: Smart latching current limiters with AI-based anomaly detection for spacecraft
jobs.description_html:
BESCAPE (Advanced Wide Bandgap-based Power Processing and Management for Future Space Exploration) is a Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network – Joint Doctorate (Grant Agreement 101312786). It trains 11 doctoral candidates in power conversion, control and electrical power distribution for future space exploration, together with European universities, ESA and leading space companies.

Spacecraft DC distribution requires highly reliable current limitation and fault management. This project develops switching latching current limiters (swLCLs) with intelligent health monitoring and fault detection.

Your research activities:
  • Study switching LCL circuits that modulate semiconductor switches to reduce power dissipation during current limitation.
  • Investigate intelligent anomaly detection, health monitoring, predictive maintenance and potential autonomous recovery.
  • Design, manufacture and experimentally validate a swLCL module that integrates protection, monitoring and fault-management functions.
  • Perform several months secondments at OHB and at UNIOVI, and take part in the network’s training events and conferences.

jobs.title: PhD: Lensless 3D optical imaging
jobs.description_html:
Work Activities
Computational optical imaging is a powerful tool to recover object structure from diffraction patterns without relying on conventional high-quality optics and microscope objectives. While many lensless approaches already work well for 2D imaging, achieving high-resolution volumetric reconstruction of complex structures in compact fiber-based format remains a major challenge.

In this project you will push the boundaries of optical microscopy and develop new approaches for 3D lensless imaging based on ptychography, structured illumination, fiber-based detection and physics-informed computational reconstruction. The work will combine optical experiments with algorithm development. On the experimental side, you will build and optimize ptychography setups using visible light, spatial light modulators, and multimode fibers. You will investigate optimized illumination and detection schemes that maximize information content and imaging performance. On the computational side, you will develop reconstruction algorithms based on compressive sensing and data-driven machine learning approaches for depth-resolved 3D imaging. You will exploit the diversity provided by structured speckle illumination together with sparsity priors to reconstruct complex optical fields and depth-dependent sample structure from a limited set of measurements.

The project includes the development of a compact all-fiber 3D imaging demonstrator aimed at applications in semiconductor metrology. You will therefore collaborate with ASML research on wafer metrology.

Qualifications
You have a MSc degree in physics, optics, photonics or a related field.

Work environment
ARCNL performs fundamental research, focusing on the physics and chemistry involved in current and future key technologies in nanolithography, primarily for the semiconductor industry. While the academic setting and research style are geared towards establishing scientific excellence, the topics in ARCNL’s research program are intimately connected with the interests of the industrial partner ASML. The institute is located at Amsterdam Science Park and currently employs about 100 persons of which 65 are ambitious (young) researchers from all over the globe. www.arcnl.nl

Working conditions
The position is intended as full-time (40 hours / week, 12 months / year) appointment in the service of the Netherlands Foundation of Scientific Research Institutes (NWO-I) for the duration of four years, with a starting salary of gross € 3.115 per month and a range of employment benefits. After successful completion of the PhD research a PhD degree will be granted at a Dutch University. Several courses are offered, specially developed for PhD-students. ARCNL assists any new foreign PhD-student with housing and visa applications and compensates their transport costs and furnishing expenses.

More information?
For further information about the position, please contact Lyuba Amitonova: l.amitonova@arcnl.nl

Application
You can respond to this vacancy online via the button below.

Online screening may be part of the selection.

Diversity code
ARCNL is highly committed to an inclusive and diverse work environment: we want to develop talent and creativity by bringing together people from different backgrounds and cultures. We recruit and select on the basis of competencies and talents. We strongly encourage anyone with the right qualifications to apply for the vacancy, regardless of age, gender, origin, sexual orientation or physical ability.

Commercial activities in response to this ad are not appreciated.

jobs.title: Promovendus 'STRONGER2GETHER | Van schoolplein tot sportveld: hoe positieve relaties jongeren laten floreren'
jobs.description_html:
Functie
Hoe dragen positieve sociale relaties in verschillende leefwerelden bij aan het welzijn en floreren van jongeren? Hoe beïnvloeden sociale relaties op school en in de klas, thuis, online, in de natuur, tijdens sport en in de buurt elkaar? En hoe kunnen we zorgen dat positieve relaties in de ene omgeving bijdragen aan het floreren in andere omgevingen?

Binnen het landelijke onderzoeksprogramma STRONGER2GETHER ga jij als promovendus onderzoek doen naar positieve sociale relaties, welzijn en floreren in het voorbereidend en middelbaar beroepsonderwijs (vmbo en mbo).

Achtergrond en doel van het onderzoek
Positieve sociale relaties vormen een belangrijke basis voor het welzijn en floreren van jongeren. Jongeren groeien op in verschillende, met elkaar verbonden sociale en fysieke omgevingen, zoals school, thuis, sport, buurt en online omgevingen. Hoe deze omgevingen sociaal én fysiek zijn ingericht, kan mede bepalen waar en hoe jongeren elkaar ontmoeten en positieve relaties ontwikkelen. Relaties en ervaringen in deze omgevingen kunnen elkaar beïnvloeden: een jongere kan bijvoorbeeld moeite hebben om aansluiting te vinden op school, maar binnen een sportomgeving juist positieve en ondersteunende relaties ervaren.

Tegelijkertijd is nog onvoldoende bekend hoe positieve sociale relaties van jongeren zich over verschillende sociale omgevingen heen tot elkaar verhouden, welke sociale en fysieke kenmerken van deze omgevingen daarbij een rol spelen, hoe ervaringen in de ene omgeving doorwerken in andere en wat dit betekent voor hun welzijn en floreren.

Binnen dit promotietraject onderzoek je daarom positieve sociale relaties binnen en tussen verschillende sociale en fysieke omgevingen van jongeren. Je onderzoekt welke patronen, mechanismen en kenmerken van de sociale en fysieke leefomgeving bijdragen aan positieve sociale relaties en hoe deze samenhangen met mentaal welzijn en floreren. Daarbij werk je samen met jongeren en professionals, en draag je bij aan de verdere ontwikkeling van het CARES-framework (Child & Adolescent Relationships & Ecological Support).

Jouw taken en verantwoordelijkheden
  • Organiseren en uitvoeren van focusgroepen met jongeren en professionals.
  • Uitvoeren van een cross-context DEEP-analyse binnen Research & Development Communities.
  • Uitvoeren van kwalitatief, kwantitatief en/of mixed-methods onderzoek naar sociale relaties over verschillende sociale contexten.
  • Bijdragen aan de verdere ontwikkeling van het CARES-framework.
  • Schrijven van een proefschrift op basis van 3 à 4 Engelstalige wetenschappelijke publicaties.
  • Schrijven van 2 à 3 praktijkgerichte publicaties.
  • Presenteren van onderzoeksresultaten op nationale en internationale conferenties.
  • Samenwerken met andere promovendi, postdocs en praktijkpartners binnen STRONGER2GETHER.
  • Bijdragen aan een documentaire, handboek en andere kennisproducten voor professionals.

Wat bieden wij jou?
STRONGER2GETHER biedt een rijke onderzoeksomgeving met ruimte voor wetenschappelijke ontwikkeling, maatschappelijke impact en persoonlijke groei. Je maakt deel uit van een landelijk consortium waarin onderzoekers, jongeren, professionals en opleidingen samenwerken aan één gezamenlijk doel: het versterken van sociale relaties zodat jongeren kunnen floreren.

Je krijgt de mogelijkheid om innovatieve onderzoeksmethoden toe te passen, samen te werken met jongeren als co-onderzoekers en een zichtbare bijdrage te leveren aan zowel de wetenschap als de praktijk.

Samen willen we bijdragen aan de mogelijkheid dat alle jongeren kunnen floreren doordat hun relaties floreren.

jobs.title: PhD in System Dynamics modelling for resilience in pharmaceutical supply chains
jobs.description_html:
Are you worried about the ever-increasing medicine shortages in Europe? Are you passionate about understanding how we can maximize drug availability to patients in a sustainable and resilient way? Do you want to apply System Dynamics simulation techniques to develop supply chains that support a sustainable availability of critical medicines? If you have experience with System Dynamics modeling and are eager to unravel the complexity of pharmaceutical supply chains this PhD position could be a good fit!

Your contribution and responsibilities include:
  • Map and analyse the global supply chains of selected critical medicines from active ingredients to finished dosage products in the Netherlands.
  • Build multi-echelon simulation models using both qualitative and quantitative modelling techniques in System Dynamics to stress test the global pharmaceutical supply chain for a selected set of drugs.
  • Evaluate strategies to maximise drug availability and resilience sustainably, while considering stock strategies for finished products as well as intermediates and active ingredients, taking manufacturing capacity into account.

For this position we also request the successful candidate to be active in education and providing project management support for the overarching project (including project admin, meeting organisation, etc) for about 20% of her/his time.

jobs.title: PhD Position: Immunology & Hematology
jobs.description_html:
Are you eager to unravel how red blood cells are cleared and recycled, and how the immune system regulates these processes? Then this PhD opportunity could be the perfect next step in your scientific career.

In this project, you will investigate how red blood cells are removed under both physiological and pathological conditions, how neutrophils contribute to transfusion-related immune responses, and which mechanisms regulate the balance between red blood cell clearance and recycling.

Working at the interface of immunology, hematology, and transfusion medicine, you will be part of a dynamic and multidisciplinary research team tackling fundamental questions with direct clinical relevance.

The department
You will be embedded within the Anemia research priority, a vibrant and collaborative research environment that brings together several groups studying blood biology in health and disease. Research within the program spans topics ranging from erythropoiesis and iron homeostasis to transfusion medicine and immune-mediated blood disorders.

A central theme of the program is understanding how senescent or damaged red blood cells are recognized and removed by the immune system, and how the iron recovered from these cells is efficiently recycled to support the production of new red blood cells. By combining expertise in hematology, immunology, iron metabolism, and stem cell biology, the Anemia research priority offers a unique environment for tackling fundamental questions with direct clinical relevance.

What will you do?

  • Design and perform innovative experimental studies.
  • Work with advanced mouse models and cutting-edge immunological techniques.
  • Investigate how neutrophils and phagocytes regulate red blood cell clearance and iron recycling in health and disease.
  • Study the mechanisms underlying hemolysis, alloimmunization, and immune-mediated red blood cell destruction.
  • Analyze, interpret, and present complex experimental data.
  • Publish your findings in leading international scientific journals.
  • Present your work at national and international conferences.


Who are you?

  • You hold an MSc degree in Biomedical Sciences, Immunology, Life Sciences, or a related field.
  • You are curious, motivated, and passionate about solving fundamental biological questions.
  • You have a strong interest in experimental research; experience with immunological, hematological, or cell biology techniques is an advantage.
  • You can work independently while also thriving in a collaborative environment.
  • You have excellent communication skills and are proficient in English.


What we offer

jobs.title: PhD-student IC-you project (1fte)
jobs.description_html:
Een op de drie jongeren (12 tot 25 jaar) ervaart emotionele problemen, zoals depressie en angst. Binnen het IC-YOU project onderzoeken we of en hoe gesprekken met mensen die je vertrouwt kunnen bijdragen aan het welzijn van jongeren – of juist onbedoeld schadelijk kunnen zijn. Als PhD-student richt je je op het versterken van die communicatie. Je onderzoekt samen met jongeren waarom, wanneer en met wie jongeren hun gevoelens delen én welke barrières hen daarbij in de weg staan. Ben jij geïnteresseerd in het welzijn van jongeren? Ben jij geinteresseerd in wetenschappelijk onderzoek in het dagelijkse leven van jongeren? Dan nodigen we je uit om te solliciteren.

Functieomschrijving
Steeds meer jongeren ervaren emotionele problemen. Een gesprek met iemand die je vertrouwt – zoals een docent, sportcoach of buur – kan hen helpen zich beter te voelen. Maar niet alle jongeren hebben iemand bij wie ze terechtkunnen, en het delen van gevoelens is vaak lastig. In dit PhD-project onderzoek je hoe we de communicatie tussen jongeren en vertrouwde volwassenen kunnen versterken en welke barrières we daarbij moeten doorbreken.

Je zult verder bouwen op wetenschappelijk onderzoek met participatieve methoden en focusgroepen met jongeren, een nationale survey, en intensieve longitudinale data, zoals experience sampling methodes (ESM). Met statistische analyses (in R en Mplus) onderzoek je met wie, wanneer en waarom jongeren hun dagelijkse zorgen of ernstigere problemen delen, en wat hen daarin belemmert of juist helpt. Met hulp van twee senior begeleiders schrijf je op basis van deze data vier wetenschappelijke artikelen die samen een proefschrift vormen.

Dit PhD-project maakt deel uit van het IC-YOU onderzoeksproject, gefinancierd door de Nederlandse Organisatie voor Wetenschappelijk Onderzoek (NWO-VICI). Je werkt nauw samen met collega’s (twee postdocs) én hebt ook contact met maatschappelijke partners zoals De Kindertelefoon en MIND Us. Jouw theoretische inzichten vormen een sleutel in het verbeteren van de communicatie tussen jongeren en hun omgeving.

Naast je onderzoek besteed je een deel van je tijd (10%) aan onderwijs binnen de opleiding Pedagogische Wetenschappen aan de Erasmus Universiteit Rotterdam. Dit kan bijvoorbeeld bestaan uit het begeleiden van scripties of het verzorgen van werkgroepen. De voertaal van het onderwijs is Nederlands.

Members of the lab actively develop theories, methods and software in a variety of domains, for our own empirical studies and for our collaborative endeavors across multiple discplines. The group of Prof. Christoph Stadtfeld is looking for a motivated Doctoral student interested in the field of Statistical Network Modeling . Project background The Social Networks Lab develops, extends and applies cutting-edge statistical models for network data. Social networks are multi-layered, dynamic systems that play a crucial role for the lives of individuals they connect. In our empirical research we often asks questions about how social networks emerge and change, and how individuals’ positions in these networks matter for very personal outcomes, such as well-being, identities and behavior. But there are some statistical challenges. Connections between individuals and individual outcomes in social networks are not independent observations, like we often assume in standard statistical models. The presence of one tie can indeed alter the probability of another tie, and individuals are commonly influenced by those they are connected with. This observational dependence is not merely a nuisance but lies at the core of what networks researchers in the social sciences are interested in: how much do shared contexts, shared friends, prior interactions, or popularity increase the chance of two individuals to connect? How much do people change in response to their peers’ identities and behaviors? Job description During this project, you will be at the forefront of social network research, both independently and as a member of our research team.
